Growth

Posting plan (2 videos a day)

  • 16:00 IST (10:30 UTC): India, Middle East, Southeast Asia afternoon/evening; UK and Europe late morning. Our own Metricool peak every day of the week.
  • 04:30 IST (next morning) (23:00 UTC): US and Canada after school (6 PM New York, 3 PM Los Angeles), Latin America evening. AIR's kids study peak slot; the US is the heaviest kids YouTube audience. Metricool posts it automatically, nobody needs to be awake.
  • Every day. Put the strongest song of the week and the weekly compilation on Friday; weekends get lighter, evergreen songs.
  • Short 5 minutes after each video; extra Shorts work best Thursday to Saturday evenings local time.
  • Run this for 2 weeks, then compare in YouTube Studio (Audience: When your viewers are on YouTube) and move each slot to 2 to 3 hours before our real peaks. Extra test: post one bonus Short a day for a week at 22:30 IST (17:00 UTC, the strongest Shorts hour in PostFast's data) and compare its views with the Shorts that follow our two main videos. Third test: for one week post each Short 4 hours after its long video instead of 5 minutes later (vidIQ's suggestion, no data shown) and compare. Fourth test: Metricool's 22 to 28 Nov grid puts Instagram's second peak at 18:00 IST, so for one week move the 16:00 Reel to 18:00 and compare views and shares.

Playbook for next week's songs

  1. Major key, 4/4, 110-125 BPM for dance songs; keep one slow 60-70 BPM wind-down song in the week with no drum groove, a narrow melody and soft repeated phrases (the lullaby shape that calms babies in every culture). Christmas songs: G or C major around 110 to 118 BPM, sleigh bells and bright bells, an optional swing shuffle and a big 'everyone sing' group chorus (about 2 to 3 minutes). Keep dance grooves moderately syncopated (a few off beat kicks and claps, not straight four on the floor and not busy), the level children 3 to 6 rate best for dancing.
  2. One 1-2 bar hook repeated in every chorus, simple melody inside about 5 notes sitting mostly between middle C and A (C, F or G major), where preschoolers sing best; add nonsense syllables (la la, doo doo) kids can sing before they can talk.
  3. Every lyric line has an action kids can copy (Total Physical Response): clap, jump, wiggle, freeze, stomp, with big quiet and loud contrasts (tiptoe, then jump, then a sudden stop) because toddlers move to changes in energy, not to the beat.
  4. Use call-and-response or riddle lines ('What colour? RED!') with a short pause so kids can answer at home.
  5. A tiny story that is easy to follow (one problem, one fix, one clear lesson such as kindness or a healthy habit) with one tempo change kids can act out, ending in a happy payoff; show people and places from many cultures. A missing snack or toy mystery ('who took the cookie?') is our most proven story hook: it gave our two best Reels and the two biggest songs of a 3.5M subscriber German channel.
  6. A bright, young sounding lead voice (in Suno ask for 'bright youthful vocals' rather than 'children's choir', which often comes out uncanny; start the Style field with 'one clear lead singer', put the chorus lift into drums and synths instead of extra voices, and list choir, crowd and gang vocals in Exclude); characters look into the camera and talk to the viewer, with spoken lines in their own [Spoken] section; master every song to about -14 LUFS with -1 dBTP peaks.
  7. Subjects: family, animals, dogs, dinosaurs, vehicles, helpers, pretend play jobs and daily routines; each week make 2 songs as fresh Bro Bros twists on public domain rhymes (Wheels on the Bus, Old MacDonald, Five Little Ducks) with an animal or job twist, a mission in the title ('Catch the...!', 'Help the...!', 'Cure the boo boo!') and a learning tag.
  8. Half step key lift for the final chorus; start each song with a 2 bar clap or drum pattern (rhythm hooks babies first) and colour the arrangement with bright high register sounds (bells, xylophone, ukulele); reach the chorus by about 0:15, because our long songs hold viewers only about 20 seconds on average.
  9. Camera and motion: calm cuts every 3 to 6 s, lead Bro centred and big, gentle constant background motion (drifting clouds, bubbles, stars) that matches the song, bright rounded visuals, big friendly eyes; no flashing, no sudden loud sounds.
  10. Hide one learning point (counting, colours, routine, feelings, safety) and name it in the description; every week make at least one healthy habit song led by a friendly helper mascot (brush teeth for two minutes, wash hands) and one sharing or taking turns song, the topics behind this autumn's biggest kids breakouts. Sing the learning word itself on the chorus melody, never only speak it, because 1 to 2 year olds learn new words only when they are sung (QJEP 2024). Every other week also make one cheerful everyday safety song (lifts, crossing the road, staying close in crowds), a top hit topic for Cocobi (stranger danger 32.7M, elevator safety 23.6M) and Zoobees.
  11. Shorts and Reels: our skip rate in the first 3 s is 58 to 90%, so open on full body dancing at the chorus peak, a spoken action call by a Bro (speech in the first 3 s lifted 10 s retention by about 25% in brand Reels) or a tiny mystery question ('Who took the cookie?'), with motion or text in the first half second; make each Short a new cut with its own hook that loops back to the start; keep music Shorts about 30 to 40 s and set each Short's related video link to its full song. Lead Reels with a game cue ('Uh oh... catch it!', 'FREEZE!'): on 18 Nov our two game hook Reels passed 100 views while calm story Reels stayed under 20. On Reels use three to five specific hashtags (Instagram caps posts at five). Frame every vertical cut for the shared safe box (on 1080x1920: faces, hands and on screen words between about 290 px from the top and 670 px from the bottom, 120 px from the left and 190 px from the right), so captions, usernames and the button column on Reels, Shorts and TikTok never cover the Bros.
  12. Thumbnails: one or two happy faces cropped big (both Bros, or a Bro with an animal friend; several face layouts beat single faces) (about 40% of the frame height), one clear action, one recognisable object, high contrast with a warm accent on a plain bright background (red and white or blue and orange), max 3 outlined words kept out of the bottom right corner; never scared, crying or shocked faces; test changes by hand because Test and Compare is off for kids videos. After each upload, check Metricool for a "Could not upload video thumbnail" warning and set the thumbnail by hand in YouTube Studio if it appears.
  13. Weekly long form: one 25 to 45 minute themed compilation (one topic, best performer first, a bonus blooper dance at the end) every Friday, because videos over 40 minutes break out far more often and kids compilations lift RPM; add a timestamp chapter per song named in the plain words parents search ('Brush Teeth Song', 'Dinosaur Stomp'); make the 25 Dec and 1 Jan Fridays holiday mega mixes, and have the main Christmas songs live by the first days of December because December ad rates run about 40 to 60% above January's and Christmas Reels are already peaking in late November; keep a 24/7 live stream of all songs running once we pass about 50 songs.
  14. Originality and compliance: write our own lyrics, vary story situations and endings week to week (no template clones), vary Suno style prompts, instruments and tempo song to song so our audio does not cluster, build compilations from distinct full songs (never loops), run YouTube's copyright check on every track, tick the AI music disclosure on every upload, set made for kids per video, and make every Suno song on the paid plan; publish only songs generated fresh on a paid Suno plan and downloaded through the plan (Remix outputs stay personal use on every plan since Sep 2026); rescue and doctor songs show gentle problems and quick happy fixes, never a suffering or scared animal, and stay a small share of each week. Pass the parents' 'AI slop' check (ZERO TO THREE, May 2026): a clear named creator, a stated purpose for every song, accurate facts and no loud surprises used only to hold attention. Every voice, cheer and sound effect must be our own (Suno, our recordings or a licensed library with the licence kept); never lift even one clip of audio from another show, because that alone cost Wolfoo its whole catalogue in July 2026.
  15. Mix in older kid energy: at least two songs a week should be full body dance alongs (Danny Go! style) or movement games (freeze dance, going on a hunt, floor is lava, the top five hits of The Kiboomers) with a funny chantable nonsense word kids can shout, and make a part 2 of any game that wins; on Instagram post fewer, better Reels (the best 1 or 2 songs a day), captions as one keyword sentence plus a question to parents and at most 2 hashtags; group Shorts of one song family into a YouTube Shorts series and test two hooks per song with Trial Reels after 1,000 followers.
  16. Every week, build 2 to 3 Shorts/Reels on a current trend format from the trend bank, adapted kid-safe with our own original song (never copyrighted trending audio).
  17. Upload slots: 16:00 IST (Asia, Middle East, Europe) and 04:30 IST (US after school); strongest song plus the weekly compilation on Friday; re-check slots after 2 weeks in YouTube Studio.
  18. Going global: add Spanish first, then Portuguese, Arabic and Indonesian as extra audio tracks on our main videos (not new channels), starting with the best 10 songs; keep songs at about 110 to 125 BPM in C or G major with one repeated hook. Ask an official YouTube partner to submit us to the YouTube Kids app (we pass the 1,500 subscriber bar), because made for kids discovery favours big channels and small kids channels need outside routes in.

Song ideas for next week

  1. Here Comes the Garbage Truck! (Stomp, Lift and Dump Recycling Dance Song): Working vehicle songs with a shout back chorus keep charting (Danny Go!'s garbage truck song in the iTunes kids top 15) and become evergreen job songs that get suggested for years.
  2. Freeze, Then Jingle! (Jingle Bells Funk Freeze Dance Song): Rides the top TikTok dance of late November with a public domain melody in our own funk arrangement, and the freeze then dance structure is a proven kids game that makes children join in.
  3. Dear Santa, I'm THIS Tall! (Measure Me and Make a Kind Wish Song): Later's 20 Nov Reels pick is 'Dear Santa, I'm a size...' and YouTube counts over 90M views for Christmas wishlist videos; Little Bro measures himself on the door frame, lists his good deeds and wishes for a present for his brother, a kind twist that works as a long song, a Short and a Reel.
  4. Shh! Secret Santa Swap! (Tiptoe, Make a Gift, Surprise Song): YouTube's 2026 holiday report lists Secret Santa family challenges as a rising gamified format; each friend draws a name, tiptoes around making a handmade gift and everyone opens at once with a confetti pop, teaching giving and counting with a 'shh' chorus kids can act out.
  5. What's Inside the Egg? (Hatch a Surprise Animal Song): Egg hatching and pet collecting games are the fastest growing new Roblox games this autumn; each chorus cracks a mystery egg to reveal a new animal and its sound, a guess along hook with no protected characters.
  6. Tickle Monster Giggles! (Tickle, Tickle, Who Laughs First Song): The hottest holiday 2026 toys react when touched (a laughing tickle plush, a roaring cub); a call and response tickle song with a giggle on every beat matches that cause and effect play.
  7. The Bro Bros Theme Song: Bluey's most streamed track is its short theme tune; a 20 to 30 second catchy Bro Bros theme with the brothers' names, used as the intro of every video, builds instant recognition and its own replays.
  8. My Body Can Do Amazing Things: Body positive move along songs (Meekah's Oct 2026 release) win brand partners and parents; Big Bro and Little Bro show stretch, jump, wave and clap moves, all standing in place.
  9. Red Light, Green Light, Cross With Me! (Stop, Look and Hold Hands Song): Our 20 Nov traffic light car Reel drew 25 shares from 44 people, our first real sharing, so a road safety lesson parents want to pass on is our most shareable topic so far; a crossing song with a freeze on red and a march on green adds a game.
  10. Uh Oh, My Zipper's Stuck! (Getting Dressed Helper Song): BabyBus's stuck zipper song hit 1.36M views in two weeks: a tiny everyday problem in the title, then the Bros solve it step by step with a dance on each fix; winter coats make it timely worldwide.
  11. Draw a Snowman With Me! (Circle, Circle, Carrot Nose Song): 'How to draw a snowman' and 'how to make a snowman' are searched worldwide every December; the Bros draw three circles, a carrot nose, a scarf and a beanie in time with the beat, then the drawing comes alive and dances.
  12. Use Your Words! (Little Bro's Big Feelings Song): Bebefinn's 18 Nov feelings song (cry, then say what is wrong) is its fastest starting upload this month; ours: Little Bro gets upset, Big Bro helps him say 'I feel sad, I need help', with a stomp, breathe and hug dance.
  13. Vroom Vroom Vacuum! (Clean Up Helper Song): A kids 'vacuum cleaner song' Short and a morning tooth brushing song both sit in this week's worldwide top 30 YouTube videos (about 81M and 86M views in a week, TubeStats 20 Nov 2026): household machines and routines are huge for toddlers. The Bros push a friendly vacuum that hums a tune, sucks up toy blocks in rhythm and 'burps' them into the toy box; a stop and go freeze when it switches off.
  14. Knock Knock, Who's There at Christmas? (Guess the Friend Song): Moonbug's best Christmas song on its compilation channel is a simple 'who's at the door' guessing game (about 6.3M views), and disguised gift guessing is trending now; each verse a knock, a sung clue, then the door opens on a friend (a penguin, a snowman, Grandma). Standing moves: knock knock with one fist on two beats, hand to ear, then jump and wave on the reveal.

Trend bank: trends to use in our videos

  • Say the word on beat (Bros picture beat game) evergreen TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube long form on smart TVs (family holiday game, about 1.2B views)
    Our own original drum loop with a tick and a whistle. A grid of 8 bright pictures (snowman, star, sock, bell...) appears, each picture lights up on a beat and the Bros on either side point at it and say the word on the beat, then the family at home joins. Each round speeds up and sneaks in rhyming look alikes (cat, hat, bat) for giggles; end the long version with a 'grandma level' bonus round. Bros stand in place and point, clap and bounce on the beat, no floor moves.
  • The urge to... peak TikTok, Instagram Reels
    8 second wordless Short: caption 'the urge to jump in the BIG puddle' (or press the shiny red button, or eat the snowman's carrot nose); Little Bro stands still, looks at the puddle, looks at the camera with wide eyes, pauses one beat, then hops in with both feet on the drop of our own two bar jingle and freezes with a big grin. Meshy prompt: standing still, slow head turn to the side, look forward, small hop forward with both feet, arms up in a happy freeze.
  • Villain chair, oops! rising TikTok, Instagram Reels (POV: you're the villain but...)
    8 to 12 second Reel or Short: Big Bro sits in a big spinny chair stroking a toy cat and says in a deep silly voice, over our own original two bar 'evil plan' music sting, that he will eat ALL the cookies; then the chair slowly spins him the wrong way, or Little Bro switches the lights on and he squeaks 'oops' in his normal voice, both giggle and share the cookies. No real threats, no mean words; the mishap is the punchline. End on a freeze pose and loop back to the chair.
  • Ride the reindeer over the rooftops seasonal TikTok AI templates (rising 20 Nov 2026), Reels, Shorts
    A 10 to 15 second Short: Little Bro climbs onto a friendly reindeer in the snowy garden, it lifts off with a jingle and they swoop over glowing rooftops with Big Bro waving from the sleigh behind, then land and both do a happy bounce; set to a 6 second loop from our own Christmas song. Dance for the landing: standing in place, small bounce on both feet, both arms up in a V, then a big two hand wave to camera.
  • Together, my turn, your turn, together peak TikTok (Ba Ba Ba duo, Oct to Nov 2026), Reels, Shorts
    A 20 second Short to our own funky beat: 0 to 5 s Big Bro and Little Bro side by side do chest taps, a clap and shoulder bounces; 5 to 9 s Big Bro solo with arms crossed, a finger point to the sky and a turn while Little Bro watches; 10 to 15 s Little Bro solo with big arm swings, a spin and arms up; 16 to 20 s both in sync push their hands toward the camera with knee bounces and finish with arms overhead, then on screen text 'Your turn!'. Meshy steps: standing in place, chest taps, clap, shoulder bounce, arms crossed then point up, turn in place, big arm swings, spin in place, push both hands forward, arms overhead.
  • Jingle Bell funk freeze and chest tap rising TikTok (top dance 20 Nov 2026), Reels, Shorts
    Big Bro, Little Bro and a friend in Santa hats stand in a row, frozen with hands clasped low and blank faces for 3 seconds, then on the drop of our own funk arrangement of the public domain Jingle Bells: cross both forearms over the chest, one fist to the mouth with the other hand on the hip, then four alternating forearm chest taps with a small knee bounce; repeat and end on a big grin. Meshy steps: standing in place, hands clasped low, cross forearms over chest, fist to mouth with other hand on hip, tap chest with alternating forearms while bouncing knees slightly.
  • Everybody's out playing, except me rising TikTok and Reels (Virlo top 12, week of 21 Nov 2026)
    On screen text 'Everybody is outside playing...' over a quiet window shot, then 'except me' and a hard cut to Little Bro in his room proudly doing a silly dance, building a block tower or practising piano, ending with him shouting 'Ta da!' to camera. Original voice line and our own music bed; no trending audio.
  • How we looked this year, month by month seasonal TikTok, Reels, Shorts (rising late Nov, peaks late Dec 2026)
    A 12 to 15 second Short or Reel: a month label (January, February...) pops up on screen and each beat shows a 1 second clip of Big Bro and Little Bro from a different Bro Bros song in that month's outfit or setting, ending on both waving in Christmas jumpers with 'see you next year!'. Music: a bouncy 8 bar loop from our own song of the week.
  • Deck the Halls pyjama duo rising TikTok and Reels (UK, rising mid Nov 2026), YouTube Shorts
    Big Bro and Little Bro in matching Christmas pyjamas side by side in front of the tree do a mirrored 16 count routine to our own bouncy arrangement of the public domain carol Deck the Halls (fa la la chorus): step touch right and left with claps, two arm rolls, point up on 'fa la la', hip bump on the last beat, then repeat; end with a big cheesy pose. Meshy steps: standing in place, step touch side to side with claps, forearm roll in front of the chest, point one finger up, small side bump toward the other brother.
  • Hmph! Grumpy, then giggle rising TikTok and Reels (rising Nov 2026), YouTube Shorts
    An 8 second Short: Little Bro is 'grumpy' because Big Bro ate the last cookie. On our own drum beat he stands stiff, spins away with arms crossed, snaps back with hands on hips, puffs his cheeks and turns his nose up 'hmph!'; then Big Bro offers half a cookie and Little Bro melts into a giggle and a happy wiggle. Meshy step: standing in place, arms crossed, quarter turn left, hands on hips, small chin up, then a loose happy side to side wiggle; no floor moves.
  • Dear Santa, I'm this tall rising Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube Shorts (late Nov to 24 Dec)
    Little Bro stands against the door frame while Big Bro marks his height, then he reads a crayon letter to camera: 'Dear Santa, I'm THIS tall now, I shared my toys, I brushed my teeth...' and ends with a kind wish (a present for his brother). Cut to Big Bro writing his own letter with a funny twist. Our own jingle, never the licensed Christmas pop. Meshy step: standing tall on tiptoes with one hand flat on the head, then a little two step sway holding a letter with both hands.
  • Secret Santa swap reveal seasonal YouTube long form and Shorts, TikTok, Reels (December)
    Big Bro and Little Bro each pull a friend's name from a hat, sneak around making a handmade gift (the camera follows each in turn), then everyone swaps on the last chorus and opens at the same time with a confetti pop; end on the funniest gift (a sock puppet of Big Bro). Our own song, a counting chorus 'shh, it's a secret'. Dance step for Meshy: standing in place, finger to lips on 'shh', two tiptoe steps left and right, then both arms open wide on 'surprise'.
  • Advent door a day seasonal YouTube Shorts and Reels daily December series (Vlogmas, Shortsmas), 1 to 24 Dec
    From 1 Dec post one 15 second Short a day: a big wooden advent calendar, the Bros count 'one, two, three, open!' and a door pops open to show a soft squishy toy we invent (a snow bunny, a jam donut bear) plus one new dance step from our own Christmas song. Steps for Meshy: standing, knock knock on the air twice with one fist, then pull an imaginary door open with both hands and jump in place with arms up. On 24 Dec post the full song with all 24 steps as one dance.
  • Christmas tree sway rising TikTok and Instagram Reels (AI Christmas dance, mid Nov 2026)
    A 5 to 8 second vertical Short with our own jingly Christmas chorus: both Bros in Santa hats stand in front of our 3D Christmas tree and do the tiny routine three times: sway left and right for four beats, clap once above the head, then one small turn in place. Meshy prompt: standing in place, gentle side to side sway, one overhead clap, a slow 360 degree turn, no floor moves. End with the caption 'Your turn! Sway, clap, spin!' so families copy it.
  • Silent dinner table glances rising TikTok (NewEngen 20 Nov 2026)
    A 12 second Short at the family dinner table: one cookie left on the plate, Big Bro and Little Bro trade slow side eye looks on each beat of our own funny tune (look left, look right, eyebrows up), freeze, then both break into a smile and split the cookie in half. Standing or sitting still, no floor moves; caption 'Who gets the last cookie?'
  • Confetti pop on the beat rising TikTok (fresh, 206M views since 6 Oct)
    Short or Reel: Big Bro and Little Bro sing the hook of our own song, freeze for one beat, then a confetti cannon bursts on the drop and both throw arms up in a star shape. Meshy prompt: character stands in place, sways side to side twice, freezes, then jumps lightly and throws both arms up in a V. Optional funny fail version: Little Bro's popper only puffs a tiny cloud, he shrugs, then it bursts late.
  • Chores ballet waltz rising Instagram Reels
    The Bros tidy their toy room as if it were a grand ballet, set to our own original waltz in 3/4 (or a fresh arrangement of a public domain waltz, never a recorded version): Big Bro twirls once while lifting a teddy, Little Bro sweeps with slow side steps and a little bow at the end. Meshy prompt: standing in place, slow graceful turn with arms raised in a circle, then side step left and right, then a small bow. 15 seconds, title 'Clean up time, but make it ballet'.
  • Shy, then dance rising TikTok, Reels
    Little Bro turns his face away from the camera, arms crossed, says 'hmph' and shakes his head twice; on the beat drop of our own song he gives in, smiles and dances: bounce in place with knees soft, then two arm rolls in front of the chest, then point at the camera. Meshy prompt: standing in place, turn head away with arms crossed, then bounce and roll arms forward, then point forward. 10 to 15 seconds, loop back to the shy pose.
  • Meanwhile, btw rising TikTok (Virlo rising, week to 19 Nov 2026)
    A 12 second Short: on screen text 'While everyone's building snowmen...' over a quick snowy clip, then 'Little Bro, btw:' and a proud shot of him practising our new dance in his room, ending with Big Bro joining in. Uses our own song. Dance for the payoff: standing in place, step side to side with arms swinging for four beats, then a big proud chest point with both thumbs.
  • Burst through the gift paper seasonal TikTok, Reels and Shorts, every December
    A 15 second Short: a doorway covered in giant wrapping paper, a drum roll in our own song, then Little Bro steps through the paper with a big smile, followed by Big Bro and a friend, each in a new festive outfit; end on all three doing the chorus move. Dance: standing in place, arms up in a V on beat 1, clap on beat 2, twist the hips left and right on beats 3 and 4. Show it as a soft paper sheet only, never glass or anything sharp.

Newest learnings

  • Platforms Emplifi's Q3 2026 benchmark of about 77,000 brand Instagram profiles found shares are now the second biggest interaction after likes and that shares relative to reach rose 52% in a year worldwide, so every Bro Bros Reel needs one moment a parent wants to send to another parent (a funny face, a 'tag your little dancer' move, a useful routine). (Emplifi, Oct 2026)
  • Platforms On the US iTunes kids Christmas songs chart (21 Nov 2026) the No. 1 is a toy brand's snowflake shuffle dance song from 2022, and almost all of the rest of the top 20 are decades old recordings (1951 to 2005 carols, Raffi, Cedarmont Kids); only one 2026 release (No. 12) made it, so new kids Christmas songs break in mainly when they are a simple December dance, not another carol. (PopVortex (iTunes), Nov 2026)
  • Platforms Dash Social's children and baby benchmark (brand accounts with 1K+ followers, Jul to Dec 2025) puts average views per post at about 77.6K on Instagram, 120.6K on TikTok and 58.9K on YouTube, all about half the all industry average, so kids content reaches fewer people per post than other niches and small numbers on our Reels are normal at the start. (Dash Social, 2026)
  • Platforms In the same Dash Social report children and baby brands lifted YouTube views 455% in six months while doubling uploads from 2 to 4 a week across Shorts and long videos, but engagement rates fell about 20% on Instagram (2.0% to 1.6%) and 18% on TikTok, so in this niche more volume on YouTube buys views while likes and comments thin out; judge our posts on views and watch time, not likes. (Dash Social, 2026)
  • Platforms Dash Social says the average Instagram Reel is watched for only about four seconds and tells brands to hook in the first four seconds; for a Bro Bros Reel that means the chorus move or a funny face has to be on screen in the first beat, not after an intro. (Dash Social, 2026)
  • Platforms Clutch's survey of 483 consumers (Dec 2025) found 55% stop scrolling for a compelling hook and 55% for humour, against 43% for striking visuals and 40% for curiosity, so every Bro Bros Short should open on a funny moment or a sung hook line, not just a pretty shot. (Clutch, Dec 2025)
  • Platforms A TikTok estimate reported by NPR puts typical viewing at about 260 videos in under 35 minutes, roughly 8 seconds per video, so a Bro Bros Short has about 8 seconds to make a child or parent stay, and the chorus should arrive by then. (Clutch citing NPR, Dec 2025)
  • Platforms Instagram started rolling out Content Protection to eligible creators on 17 Nov 2026 (copies of an original video can be tracked, hidden or given an 'original by' credit) and is testing matches on spoken or sung words even when AI swaps the visuals, which helps an original song channel like Bro Bros keep credit when Reels are re uploaded. (Keywords Everywhere, Nov 2026)
  • Platforms Instagram added 'Use as reference' for Reels under 90 seconds (iOS first, Oct 2026): the original Reel plays in a small movable window over the camera with a countdown so a creator can copy its timing, which makes dance along and reaction Reels much easier for families to film against our dance Reels. (Social Media Today, Oct 2026)
  • Platforms Since mid 2026 the YouTube Shorts player has no dislike button; the like is a heart and the down option is now 'Not interested' or 'Don't recommend this channel', so a viewer who dislikes a Short now sends a direct negative signal against the whole channel and a weak opening costs more than before. (GSMArena, Jun 2026)
  • Platforms Shorts Series (from 23 Sep 2026 on web, mobile and TV) play a creator's Shorts as numbered episodes in order and resume where the viewer stopped, so a numbered December run (for example 24 advent door Shorts) can be grouped as one series that pulls viewers to the next episode, but made for kids channels should first check the option appears in their Studio. (Digital Trends, Sep 2026)
  • Platforms YouTube is also showing channel Posts inside the Shorts feed on web and mobile; made for kids channels cannot post them, so this new surface helps general channels only and our Instagram has to carry channel news to parents. (Digital Trends, Sep 2026)

  • Kids/baby content gets about 71K views per Instagram post, similar to TikTok and far above typical brand YouTube posts. (Dash Social benchmark, medium)

  • Vertical 9:16 beats square by 2-3x on short-form platforms. (kineclip.com 2026 trends, medium)

  • Sheriff Labrador (BabyBus, China) grew 784% on Netflix after expanding from Latin America worldwide, proof that a Chinese 3D animal kids brand travels globally. (What's on Netflix, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Bluey was the most streamed title in the US for the second year in 2025 (about 45 billion minutes); calm, funny family play beats frantic content on the living room TV. (Variety, Jan 2026, high)
  • Spotify added a global setting (Sep 2026) so parents can keep kids and family music out of their own recommendations and Wrapped; kids songs are clearly a big share of family streaming. (Music Business Worldwide, Sep 2026, high)
  • Nonsense chant songs spread among Gen Alpha on TikTok and Reels: 'Chicken Banana', a techno track by a Swedish channel, became a dance trend and then a playground catchphrase. (Newser, Feb 2026, medium)
  • KPop Demon Hunters showed a kids music franchise can keep growing long after launch; K pop style songs and dance are a strong worldwide kid taste in 2025 and 2026. (Netflix data via TheWrap, 2026, medium)
  • YouTube added Shorts series with seasons and episodes (23 Sep 2026) and custom Shorts thumbnails (Jul 2026); the dislike button left Shorts in Jun 2026, replaced by 'Not interested' and 'Don't recommend this channel'. (OutlierKit, Oct 2026, high)
  • About 55% of Reel views come from non followers, and DM sends are weighted roughly 3 to 5 times more than likes for reaching non followers; 3 to 4 strong Reels a week in one consistent niche is the suggested cadence. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Instagram flags accounts as 'aggregators' with reduced non follower reach when most posts in 30 days reuse 70% or more of another creator's visuals or audio; our own original songs keep us safe. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Instagram Trial Reels (accounts with 1,000+ followers) show a Reel to non followers first, a free way to test two hooks for the same song before sharing to followers. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Reels can be up to 20 minutes for eligible accounts, but only Reels up to 3 minutes are recommended to non followers. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, medium)
  • YouTube reaches 67% of US kids aged 2 to 5, 78% of 6 to 9 and 80% of 10 to 12, far ahead of tablet games, streaming services and other social video apps. (Precisify via Advanced Television, Feb 2026, high)
  • Kids streaming trends for 2026: learning wrapped in stories (science, nature, feelings), interactive quizzes and choices, shorter flexible episodes, characters from many cultures and family types, and nature and recycling themes. (TodoTV News, Jul 2026, medium)
  • On Netflix, PAW Patrol led kids hours in H2 2025 and Gabby's Dollhouse led 2025 overall; preschool is now so crowded that new IP needs strong marketing as well as strong content to break in. (Kids StreamerSphere, Mar 2026, high)
  • UK 8 to 14 year olds spend about 3 hours a day online; YouTube reaches almost all of them in a month and Roblox is the top games app at 61% reach. (Ofcom, Jun 2025, high)
  • In Tubefilter's most subscribed chart for the week of 8 Nov 2026, 37 of the top 50 channels are mainly Shorts channels and India has 14 of them, so Shorts remain the fastest subscriber engine worldwide. (Tubefilter, Nov 2026, high)
  • After YouTube Kids entry, PlayToys and Play Dolls launched Shorts for the first time and reached about 1.18M views with 27 to 30 second average watch, so Kids app access and Shorts work best together. (AIR Media-Tech, Aug 2025, medium)
  • Instagram's Your Algorithm lets viewers add or remove topics they want; it started on Reels (Dec 2025), reached all English speakers (Jan 2026), Explore (15 Apr 2026) and the main Feed (Jun 2026), so each Reel should signal one clear topic like kids songs or kids dance. (SocialPilot and The Keyword, 2026, high)
  • Reels guidance for 2026: show motion or on screen text within about half a second, use keyword rich captions rather than piles of hashtags, and add short on screen text so Instagram's AI can read the topic. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Instagram near duplicate penalties (70% or more shared visuals or audio) last from 24 hours to 30 days and cut only non follower reach; since Apr 2026 they also apply to photos and carousels. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Reels advice is about 90% niche consistency; mixing Hindi Didi story Reels with English dance songs on one account may blur our topic signal, so a separate story account or a steady weekly slot is worth testing. (SocialPilot Sep 2026 with our posting mix, low)
  • Baby Shark joined Spotify's Billions Club in May 2026 with about 137M streams in a year and about 400K a day from 23M listeners, led by the US, UK, Australia and Canada, so audio streaming of kids songs is strongest in high paying English markets. (BSCkids, May 2026, high)
  • Netflix's global top 10 for 14 to 20 Sep 2026 held Gabby's Dollhouse S14 (best debut since S8), YouTube creator Mark Rober's CrunchLabs, A Minecraft Movie and KPop Demon Hunters still charting in week 65. (What's on Netflix, Sep 2026, high)
  • KIDZ BOP (11B+ streams) reaches Gen Alpha on Roblox by placing its album inside a popular obstacle course game (Really Easy Obby, about 580K daily visits) where kids collect music notes while songs play. (KIDZ BOP, Jan 2025, medium)
  • More people now watch YouTube on TVs than on phones and it is the No. 1 streaming platform on US TV screens (Nielsen), so our songs must look and sound good on a big living room screen. (YouTube Official Blog, Jan 2026, high)
  • Shorts series (announced 23 Sep 2026) let Partner Program channels group Shorts into seasons and episodes with custom thumbnails and continuous story playback on web, mobile and connected TVs, built on Creator Shows from 2025; once we qualify, a Bro Bros Shorts season (one mini story per Short) fits it. (TechCrunch, Sep 2026, high)
  • YouTube's own holiday Shorts formats are a before and after door transition (plain room to decorated room), making or decorating holiday treats to a festive tune, and decorate with me montages; all translate into kids song Shorts with the Bros. (YouTube Blog, Dec 2023, medium)
  • On 1 Nov 2026 the top 20 US trending videos came from 20 different creators and six were under 24 hours old, and music videos dominate YouTube's all time most viewed list, so a fresh daily music upload has a real chance to surface. (Mean CEO blog, Nov 2026, low)
  • Zootopia 2 logged 1.72B Disney+ minutes in the week ending 15 Mar 2026, beating every Netflix title; 44% of viewers were adults 18 to 49 and 39% children 2 to 11, showing animal comedies built for whole family co viewing win big. (Nielsen via Pulse, Apr 2026, high)
  • Disney Jr. held all top 3 US preschool streaming spots in Q1 2025: Bluey, Spidey and his Amazing Friends, and Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, which still ranks though it stopped making new episodes in 2016; a strong library keeps earning for a decade. (Kidscreen and Nielsen, May 2025, high)
  • Bluey passed 70B minutes of US streaming watch time from Dec 2023 to Apr 2025, the benchmark for calm, funny sibling play stories that parents enjoy too. (Kidscreen and Nielsen, May 2025, medium)
  • Big kids song brands also sit on free ad supported TV (FAST) and connected TV apps (Roku, Samsung TV Plus, LG, TCL, Pluto TV) besides YouTube, another reason to render in TV friendly quality. (Senal News, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Netflix H1 2026 YouTube born kids hours: Ms. Rachel 208M, Sheriff Labrador 111M (BabyBus), Salish and Jordan Matter 99M, CrunchLabs 81M, Danny Go! 54M from one season; CoComelon left the top 10. (What's on Netflix, Sep 2026, high)
  • India's family and kids Shorts channels keep scaling faster than any other market: Koko and Golu ranked #16 to #19 worldwide in late Oct 2026 with 500 to 600M weekly views. (Tubefilter, Nov 2026, high)
  • In Metricool's study of 24.36M Instagram posts from 375K accounts (Jan to Feb 2026 vs 2025), posts with hashtags got 32% fewer views and 34% fewer interactions than posts without, so our 7 hashtag Reel captions should be cut to a keyword sentence and 1 or 2 tags. (Metricool via Net Influencer, Jun 2026, medium)
  • Average Instagram Reel watch time rose from 4 to 8.5 seconds year on year and Reels were the only format with rising engagement (+25%); our 2 to 4 second average is well under the norm. (Metricool via Net Influencer, Jun 2026, high)
  • Instagram captions that ask viewers to comment drew 203% more comments than average, and Story replies rose 88%, so a simple question to parents ('Which animal should the Bros help next?') in captions can start interaction. (Metricool via Net Influencer, Jun 2026, medium)
  • Share focused Reel advice: 15 to 45 seconds, payoff within 15 seconds, text overlay of 6 words or fewer in the upper third, and three variations of one idea compared over 7 days; a 1 to 3% share rate is solid, and over 5 Reels a week is usually counterproductive without a team. (Socialync, 2026, low)
  • The iTunes Top 100 Kids Songs (Nov 2026) is led by gentle faith songs and soft covers (You Are My Sunshine), plus parent nostalgia themes (Kim Possible, VeggieTales, Return to Pooh Corner): paid downloads are driven by parents' own taste. (PopVortex iTunes chart, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Silly food and body novelty songs chart high on iTunes kids (String Cheese, Raining Tacos, Shiny Teeth, The Cuppycake Song), so a funny food song with a catchy nonsense chorus can sell beyond YouTube. (PopVortex iTunes chart, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Bluey's Dance Mode and the Bluey theme, Baby Shark, and Ms. Rachel's Wheels on the Bus and Caterpillar sit in the iTunes kids top 20, showing brands born on TV or YouTube carry into audio sales. (PopVortex iTunes chart, Nov 2026, medium)
  • US kids aged 2 to 5 who use YouTube watch cartoons (62%), toys and games (49%), educational videos (43%), nursery rhymes (41%) and comedy (35%), so a funny cartoon song with a learning point covers four of their top five interests. (Precisify via Advanced Television, Feb 2026, high)
  • For US kids 6 to 9, cartoons (47%), comedy (45%), toys and games (45%) and music (41%) lead, and for 10 to 12 comedy (53%) and music (47%), so humour grows in importance with age and our dance songs should be funny to reach older siblings. (Precisify via Advanced Television, Feb 2026, high)
  • More than half of US kids watch YouTube on a TV screen and nearly half second screen (YouTube or mobile games while TV is on), confirming TV first viewing for kids songs. (Precisify via Advanced Television, Feb 2026, high)
  • 62% of US parents sometimes watch YouTube with their young child versus only 17% for TikTok (Common Sense 2025 census), so YouTube songs must please parents too; 40% of children have their own tablet by age 2. (Common Sense Media, Feb 2025, high)
  • For music Shorts, 30 to 45 seconds built on the strongest chorus or beat drop performs best; under 15 seconds can be too thin and over 55 seconds lowers completion, so our Shorts should be about 30 to 40 seconds. (Chartlex, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Links typed into Shorts descriptions and comments are not clickable; the Short's 'related video' setting adds a tappable link under the channel name, so every Bro Bros Short should point to its full song. (Chartlex, Oct 2026, high)
  • YouTube creator data cited in 2026 says channels that post Shorts see about 80% more channel watch time within three months, and strong music Shorts hold 80% or more average view duration. (Chartlex, Oct 2026, low)

(socialpilot.co, Nov 2026, medium)

  • Netflix's English film top 10 for 2 to 8 Nov 2026 still holds Sing 2 (4.3M views, week 14), Sing (3.2M, week 18) and KPop Demon Hunters (2.8M, week 69, hours up 7%): animated films built around singing animals and catchy songs keep pulling families for months.   • A Dog's Perfect Christmas topped Netflix's English films (8.6M views) yet had the weakest opening of 11 Netflix Christmas films compared since 2024, a sign holiday content is crowded and a fresh twist matters more than another generic Christmas story. (whats-on-netflix.com, Nov 2026, medium)

  • In the week of 11 Nov 2026 three of the top eight Reels sounds were Christmas label tracks (about 5.8M, 571K and 451K Reels) used for 'it's time' seasonal reveals and Christmas countdowns; our own song can copy the countdown format with original audio. (CreatorDB, Nov 2026, medium)

  • Community benchmarks for 'how many chose to view' (viewed vs swiped away, mostly the first 2 seconds) are 70 to 79% working and 80% plus strong; average percentage viewed should be 80 to 90% for Shorts under 35 seconds and can pass 100% with loops; YouTube publishes no official targets. (1of10, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Since 31 Mar 2025 a Shorts view counts as soon as it starts playing, but the older 'engaged views' (in Studio's Advanced Mode) are what count for Partner Program eligibility and Shorts revenue sharing, so track engaged views when judging Shorts. (1of10, Oct 2026, high)
  • Across daily Netflix kids top 10s worldwide in 2025 (FlixPatrol points) the leading series were Peppa Pig, Gabby's Dollhouse, Masha and the Bear and PAW Patrol, and the leading film was KPop Demon Hunters, ahead of Despicable Me 3. (What's on Netflix, Jan 2026, high)

  • Masha and the Bear (Russia) at No. 3 and Bebefinn (Korea) at No. 9 show non US 3D kids brands with little dialogue and lots of music and slapstick travel across Netflix's whole world audience. (What's on Netflix, Jan 2026, medium)
  • YouTube auto dubbing now covers 27 languages, with expressive speech (keeps pitch and energy) live in English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Hindi and Indonesian, and over 6M viewers watch 10+ minutes of dubbed video a day; it skips videos with no speech and videos with Content ID claims, so our sung songs need our own re sung tracks.   • In AIR's 274 channel study (Sep 2026) kids and teens Shorts were monetised on about 46% of playbacks against only about 12% for long videos, because made for kids rules block most long form ads; matching 1,000 long views takes only about 2,150 Shorts views for large kids channels against 11,000 to 34,000 in most niches.   • Large kids channels that post 21 or more Shorts a month earn about 41% of their revenue from Shorts, while in most other niches Shorts bring under 2% of revenue, so for a made for kids channel a steady daily Short is a real income line, not only a reach tool. (air.io, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Instagram's own Reels guide (Sep 2026) splits lengths into 3 to 15 seconds for quick trends, 15 to 60 seconds as the main sweet spot, and 60 seconds to 3 minutes for stories and lessons, and recommends its auto caption sticker for on screen subtitles. (iphoneincanada.ca, Sep 2026, high)
  • Netflix's most watched animated series worldwide in H1 2026: Peppa Pig 81.8M views, The Creature Cases 49.3M, Masha and the Bear 40.4M, CoComelon 39.4M, Little Angel 38.1M, Booba 32.7M, Lottie Dottie Chicken 31.5M, PAW Patrol 27.5M and Bebefinn 26.5M; six of the nine began on YouTube.   • Gamefam (a Roblox brand studio) reports Roblox passed 151M daily users in 2025 (+70%) and Gen Alpha and Gen Z users spend about 2.7 hours a day there, against about 2 on TikTok and 1.2 on YouTube; its viral hits (Grow a Garden, Steal a Brainrot, 99 Nights in the Forest) set the jokes and words older kids repeat. (gamefam.com, Dec 2025, medium)
  • YouTube Health's Dr Garth Graham released back to school screen habit tips as a video call with Mummy and Daddy Pig on the Peppa Pig parenting channel (Sep 2026), showing YouTube actively promotes healthy habit and family routine messages inside kids brands. (blog.youtube, Sep 2026, medium)
  • T-Series Kids Hut, a big Indian nursery rhyme brand on YouTube, had only about 4,820 Instagram followers in Oct 2026 (flat over a year) and posted about once every five weeks, so animated rhyme brands rarely build Instagram audiences; creator led accounts like Ms Rachel are the exception. (creatordb.app, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Dash Hudson's baby and children industry benchmark (H1 2024, 2,956 Instagram handles) found average monthly follower growth of only 0.7% on Instagram against 4.1% on TikTok and 0.8% on YouTube, so slow Instagram growth for our account is normal for the category. (dashhudson.com, 2024, medium)
  • In the same benchmark parenting tip content (a baby sleep brand's posts) outperformed the baby and children industry by 114%, so on Instagram, where the audience is parents, Reels that pair a song with a parenting win (bedtime, brushing, tidy up) should beat plain dance clips. (dashhudson.com, 2024, medium)
  • Metricool's study of 799,718 videos (Jul 2026) found Shorts views grew about 127% year on year against 76% for long videos, and Shorts now bring over 61% of organic views, with subscribers (11%) and Search (9%) far behind. (metricool.com, Jul 2026, high)
  • Shorts average view duration fell about 67% year on year to roughly 16 seconds across 71K accounts, so a 30 to 40 second song Short must land its main hook inside the first 15 seconds to be seen by most viewers. (metricool.com, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Spotify's kids genre popularity list (Nov 2026) has 5 sleep tracks in its top 20: a Swedish animal lullaby (77), German baby white noise with ocean sounds (76) and three 'Relaxing Music For Kids' bedtime pieces, so on audio services calm sleep songs earn as much attention as movie hits. (soundcharts.com, Nov 2026, medium)

(toptal.com, 2026, medium)

  • Instagram's Your Algorithm topic search works only at a broad level and narrow topics often return nothing, so Reel captions should state broad, common topics (kids songs, dance for kids, nursery rhymes) rather than niche labels. (socialmediaexaminer.com, Jul 2026, medium)

(thestar.com.my, May 2026, high)
  • One of TikTok's top sounds in October 2026 drove a 'Find the Beat' challenge, a partner dance test on a slowed Jersey club beat, showing that two person timing games travel well; a gentle kids version where the brothers take turns finding the beat fits our format. (buffer.com, Oct 2026, medium)

(senalnews.com, Jun 2026, medium)
  • YouTube Shorts now lets viewers press and hold the edge of the player for 2x speed (swipe down to lock it) and tap for a clear screen with no buttons, so slow intros get fast forwarded; every Bro Bros Short should start moving in the first second and keep the dance centred where no overlay covers it. (igeeksblog and Metricool, Jun 2026, high)
  • Instagram added a Watch History for Reels in mid 2026 (Your activity, Watch history), so a parent whose child loved a Bro Bros Reel can find it again later; a clear song name in the first caption line makes it easy to spot in that list. (Android Central and WERSM, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Instagram's Edits app now lets creators put tappable links inside a clip that open another Reel or account (no outside websites), so each Bro Bros Reel can link to the full dance tutorial Reel or last week's hit, keeping viewers inside our profile.   • Edits can auto translate captions into a second language (15 supported, including Hindi, Bengali, Spanish, Portuguese, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean and Thai), a free way to give Bro Bros Reels bilingual on screen lyrics for big non English markets. (Indian Television, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Edits gives creators up to 10 personalised clip ideas each week built from their own past Reels, plus 25 effects like bounce and fisheye; the weekly ideas are a quick free check of what Instagram thinks our channel is about. (Buzzincontent, 2026, low)
  • Spotify's managed accounts for children 13 and under reached families on any plan, including free, in the US, UK, Australia, France, Germany and the Netherlands on 15 Jul 2026 and about 30 more countries by 28 Jul (Brazil, Mexico, Spain, Italy, Canada, Poland and others), so millions of kids now have their own Spotify profile. (Spotify Newsroom, Jul 2026, high)
  • Children on managed accounts get personalised Made For You mixes and daylist from the full catalogue, so once Bro Bros songs are distributed to Spotify, a child who plays one can be fed more of ours automatically; explicit songs are blocked by default, which clean kids songs never trigger. (Spotify Newsroom, Jul 2026, high)
  • Video and Canvas looping visuals are switched off by default on kids' managed accounts, so on Spotify our songs must win on audio alone: the hook and the song title carry everything, the cover art is the only picture. (Spotify Newsroom, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Each child on a managed account gets their own Spotify Wrapped in early December, so families will see their kids' top songs; a Bro Bros song in a child's Wrapped is free word of mouth, one more reason to put our catalogue on Spotify before December. (Spotify Newsroom, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Classic slow public TV for preschoolers is moving onto YouTube in 2026: Fred Rogers Productions opened the first official Mister Rogers' Neighborhood channel in June and New Zealand's You and Me was rebuilt for YouTube with puppets, songs and filming in real preschools, betting on parents choosing calm shows for autoplay. (Tubefilter Jun 2026; Newswire NZ, May 2026, medium)
  • Third party data puts Reels' average reach at about 31% of followers (over double static posts) and Explore's at about 38%, the highest on Instagram, with Reels under 3 minutes still the only ones sent to non followers. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, low)
  • YouTube says episodic microdramas passed 6.5B views in the first half of 2026 with watch time up over 50% a year, and 40% of episode views and 30% of clicks came more than 30 days after upload, so Shorts grouped into a numbered series keep pulling views long after posting. (YouTube Blog, Oct 2026, high)
  • Shorts series add seasons, episodes, custom thumbnails and sequential playback, and YouTube pairs them with multi language audio, AI subtitles and localised metadata, so a 'Bro Bros Winter Week' Shorts series can play in order on TVs and travel to other languages. (YouTube Blog, Oct 2026, high)
  • Cocomelon's estimated Instagram audience leans to Indonesia, the US and the Philippines, with English 67%, Spanish 9% and Portuguese 7% of followers, so Southeast Asian parents are a big Instagram audience for kids song brands. (IQFluence, Oct 2026, low)
  • Tonies, the screen free audio box for kids, grew revenue 38% to about 243M EUR in H1 2026, with North America up 48% (Q2 alone up 83%) and 63% of sales now outside Germany, driven by licences such as Bluey and Pokemon. (Spielwarenmesse, 2026, high)
  • Both audio players sell curated, licensed content from big brands rather than taking open uploads, so Bro Bros songs reach audio only listening first through streaming (Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon) and could pitch to Tonies or Yoto once the brand has a following. (Spielwarenmesse and RouteNote, 2026, medium)
  • Adam Mosseri said Instagram Trial Reels will 'almost always' get less reach than normal Reels, and Buffer's tests saw trials top out around 180 views against 1,500 to 5,000 for regular Reels, so trials are a test tool, not a growth engine. (Planoly (Buffer, Mosseri), 2026, medium)
  • Kapwing's small Trial Reels test (Oct 2025) had a trend style trial beat its regular twin (2,258 vs 949 views) and one trial broke out to 1.4M views, 130 followers and 8.6K profile visits, showing trials can occasionally find a new audience for discovery, not conversions. (Planoly (Kapwing), 2026, low)
  • Good trial practice: change only one thing per test (the first second hook, or the caption), always use fresh video, compare trials only with other trials on sends, likes and watch time, and wait at least 24 hours before judging. (Planoly, 2026, medium)
  • In Buffer's three version test the same Reel with trending audio got 24% more views than a voiceover version and 33% more than an ASMR version with similar watch time; for us the safe equivalent is a catchy original song hook from the first frame rather than talking. (Planoly (Buffer), 2026, low)
  • Socialinsider's study of about 9.8M organic brand Reels (Jan to Jun 2026) found 45 to 60 second Reels got the highest median views (about 10,400) and engagement (0.35%), 30 to 45 seconds about 8,600, under 30 seconds only about 4,700, and Reels over 3 minutes fell to about 4,400 views and 0.15%. (Socialinsider, Oct 2026, high)
  • An Adobe survey of 507 Shorts creators (Mar 2026) found 53% say Shorts under 30 seconds get the most views and 49% say they drive more clicks to long videos, while subscriber growth was tied between under 30 and 30 to 60 seconds. (Adobe Express, Jun 2026, medium)
  • Since late June 2026 YouTube Shorts has no dislike button and the thumbs up became a heart, the 'Not interested' option now asks viewers for a reason, and swipe away rate stays the key Shorts signal, so a Short that annoys viewers is punished through skips and reasons rather than dislikes. (PPC Land, Jun 2026, high)
  • Emplifi's 2026 benchmark of 10,110 Facebook Reels from 704 brand pages found human speech in the first three seconds raised 10 second retention by nearly 25% and engagement by 5.6% against music only videos, so Bro Bros Shorts and Reels should open with a Bro speaking one short line ('Can you jump like me?') before or over the music. (Emplifi via The Reel Stars, Mar 2026, medium)
  • In the same Emplifi data a face in the first three seconds improved short view retention by about 10%, very short looping clips under 7 seconds got 18.7% more replays and 16.1% more engagement, and vertical video had 20.9% more reach than other shapes. (Emplifi via The Reel Stars, Mar 2026, medium)
  • Dash Social's Q2 2026 Shorts benchmarks (via eMarketer) show wellness Shorts with guided, follow along routines averaging 116% viewed (people replay them) against an 84.6% overall benchmark, the only category above 100% every quarter since Q1 2025, so follow along kids routines (brush teeth, stretch, copy the dance) are the Short type most likely to loop. (eMarketer, 2026, medium)
  • Instagram's 'Your Algorithm' topic controls spread from Reels (global English, Jan 2026) to Explore (15 Apr 2026) and the main Feed (Jun 2026), so parents can now add topics like 'kids songs' across the app, which makes clear topic captions and hashtags matter in every surface. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, medium)
  • SocialPilot's tracker reported no significant Reels ranking changes in August or September 2026 and puts Explore's average reach rate at about 37.8%, the highest surface, against about 30.8% for Reels overall. (SocialPilot, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Planoly's October 2026 review found no independent large study of Trial Reels; Instagram's own claim (80% of frequent posters saw more non follower reach) is unverified and small tests swing from about 180 to 1.4M views, so Trial Reels are a cheap hook test, not a strategy. (Planoly, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Across about 800K videos from 71K accounts, Metricool found 2026 views up 76% but estimated ad revenue down 55%, with ad impressions down 51% and monetised playbacks down 59%, because viewers left long videos earlier (average view about 2.5 minutes, down from about 4). (Creator Handbook (Metricool study), Aug 2026, high)
  • The same study found the average Short now runs about 16 seconds and Shorts drive 61% of organic views, so Shorts bring reach while revenue still depends on keeping kids watching long compilations past the first minutes. (Creator Handbook (Metricool study), Aug 2026, medium)
  • Metricool's data showed two to four long form uploads a week performed best per video, suggesting Bro Bros should keep daily output in Shorts and Reels while making fewer, stronger long songs and compilations. (Creator Handbook (Metricool study), Aug 2026, medium)
  • Amazon Kids+ launched in Italy on 19 Oct 2026 for children aged 3 to 12 at 6.99 euros a month for Prime members (7.99 otherwise), ad free, with series, Kids+ Originals, full games without in app purchases and audiobooks, widening ad free subscription viewing in Europe. (SmartWorld, Oct 2026, high)
  • In mid November 2026 only one holiday song sat in the iTunes kids top 20, so on kids download charts the Christmas wave starts later than on Reels, leaving room to land a holiday song in late November. (PopVortex iTunes chart, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A brand new BabyBus song gains only about 900 views an hour in its first half day (46K in 13 hours) on a 44M subscriber channel, so even giant kids channels rely on slow building back catalogue views rather than launch day spikes. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Instagram now shows each Reel with 100+ plays a second by second retention curve and a skip rate (viewers who swipe away before 3 seconds), filling in about 48 hours; one analysis of about 200 Reels rates skip under 20% and 3 second retention above 70% as strong, and skip above 40% as poor. (CreatorStack, Mar 2026, medium)
  • Socialinsider's study of about 25M brand Reels (2025 data, updated Nov 2026) finds Reels gather most views in the first 5 days, slow from day 5 to 10, fall sharply after day 10 and plateau around day 20, so judge a Reel after about a week and repost or remix winners later. (Socialinsider, Nov 2026, low)
  • A YouTube Short longer than one minute that carries an active Content ID claim can be blocked worldwide, so before any Bro Bros song is sent to a distributor that enrols it in Content ID, our own YouTube channel must be whitelisted, or our 60 to 90 second Shorts could vanish. (Bytecap research, Jul 2026, high)
  • In OpusClip's count of 2.9M YouTube clips made by its users over 12 months, 40% were 30 to 60 seconds, 28% were 15 to 30, 15% were 60 to 90, 12% were over 90 and only 4% were under 15 seconds; this shows what creators make, not what performs, so our own retention data should decide Short length. (Bytecap / OpusClip, Jul 2026, low)
  • Planoly's Oct 2026 rules for Trial Reels: use fresh footage (reused clips may be held back), change only one thing per test such as the hook, compare trials only with other trials using sends, likes and watch time, wait at least 24 hours, and judge patterns over several weeks, a cheap way to test two openings of the same song. (Planoly, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Spotify's kids genre ranking by popularity (Nov 2026) is topped by family friendly adult pop tagged for kids (Avicii's Wake Me Up at 88, The Clash at 84) and Halloween novelty songs, ahead of Ms Rachel (highest 72), so on Spotify our songs compete with pop that parents enjoy too, which favours polished, parent pleasing production. (Soundcharts, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Sleep audio is a big part of Spotify kids listening: a Swedish lullaby duo (77), a German baby sleep track with sea sounds (76) and four 'Relaxing Music For Kids' instrumentals sit in the kids top 31, so a calm instrumental or hummed bedtime version of our best songs is a cheap extra Spotify release. (Soundcharts, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Netflix's 14 to 20 Sep 2026 top 10 still had KPop Demon Hunters in its 65th week (2.5M views) next to A Minecraft Movie's debut and Gabby's Dollhouse Season 14, whose 4.3M first week views were its best debut since Season 8, showing that music led family films and long running preschool series keep pulling for over a year. (What's on Netflix, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Metricool's 2026 Instagram study (as cited by Mean CEO) found Reels get 65% of their views and 61% of interactions in the first three days, so a Reel's fate is set by day 3 and Story shares in the first 72 hours help. (Mean CEO citing Metricool, Nov 2026, medium)
  • YouTube is testing image Posts, including carousels of up to 10 images with text and Audio Library music, inside the Shorts feed, so a Bro Bros lyric or 'spot the difference' carousel could one day reach Shorts viewers without a new render. (Pulse citing 9to5Google, Apr 2026, medium)
  • Quso's dataset of about 508K posts from 1,900+ creators in 80+ countries (Jun 2026) puts the median YouTube Short at about 45% average view through and the top 10% at about 91%, so 50 to 60% is a good target for our Shorts and 90% is breakout level. (Quso, Jun 2026, medium)
  • In the same dataset Shorts of 11 to 20 seconds earned the highest median views, clips under 10 seconds often felt too thin, and longer ones gave more chances to drop off, so a 15 second chorus cut is the sweet spot for our song Shorts. (Quso, Jun 2026, medium)
  • Instagram is testing an option to open the app straight into Reels instead of the home feed (Stories stay on top and users can switch back), and US creators can link up to eight Reel clips to one longer video, so short song cuts could later lead viewers into a full Bro Bros compilation. (Gain blog, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Edits added beat synced video effects, bulk caption editing and clip volume boosts up to 150% in November 2026, and a desktop Edits app with Trial Reels is planned for December, an easy way to make our Reels flash and pop on the beat of our own songs. (SocialBee, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Disney+ added Gracie's Corner Season 2 and a separate 'Gracie's Corner: Shorts' Season 2 on 13 Nov 2026, so a YouTube born sing along brand now ships both full episodes and short song clips as streaming seasons; Bro Bros Shorts grouped into themed sets would be ready for that kind of deal later. (Scary Mommy, Nov 2026, high)
  • Disney Jr. premiered 'Ariel: Dolphin Cove Tales: Shorts' on Disney+ on 4 Nov 2026, more proof that streamers now copy YouTube's short episode format for preschoolers. (Scary Mommy, Nov 2026, medium)
  • 'Bluey Fancy Restaurant' (Disney+, 16 Nov 2026) is a live action spin off where real children cook, decorate and plan a special dinner for their parents, a sign that kids love 'we surprise our parents' missions, a good song topic for the Bros. (Scary Mommy, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Roblox's Q3 2026 results showed its first year on year drop in daily players (about 138M, down 9%), hours played down 15% and paying users down 16%, after age checks and chat limits added friction for young players; daily players still grew 37% in India and 33% in Japan, and adults were 29% of age checked players. (GGRecon, Nov 2026, high)
  • Since Feb 2026 YouTube has tested two AI tools in the Shorts Remix menu: 'Add object' inserts items into up to 8 seconds of another creator's Short and 'Reimagine' turns one frame of it into a new AI video; it is limited to a small English speaking group outside the EU and UK, and every result links back to the original Short. (PPC Land, Feb 2026, high)
  • YouTube plans Shorts made with a creator's own AI likeness, clearly labelled and with controls over how the likeness is used, which is aimed at human creators; for us the takeaway is that YouTube is building tools to protect a character's look, so registering the Bros' designs early is worth doing. (TweakTown, 2026, low)
  • In the iTunes kids songs chart in mid November 2026 only one of the top 25 is a Christmas song (a TobyMac track at 13; Jingle Bells is at 39 and Silent Night at 60), while gentle faith songs, novelty food songs and Ms Rachel, Bluey and Baby Shark tracks lead, so kids' music charts turn to Christmas later than TikTok; our Christmas audio releases should peak in December. (PopVortex (iTunes), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Amazon's best selling Tonies music item in June 2026 was the Ms Rachel figurine (about 6K units a month), ahead of film characters like Woody, Lightning McQueen, Elsa and Toothless (about 2K to 3K each), showing a YouTube born music brand can outsell major film characters in screen free audio. (AsInsight, Jun 2026, medium)
  • Ms Rachel and Mr Aron versions of Wheels on the Bus and Caterpillar both sit in the iTunes kids top 20 beside CoComelon's Wheels on the Bus, so a well known rhyme can carry two competing brand versions at once; a fresh Bro Bros version of a public domain classic still has room. (PopVortex (iTunes), Nov 2026, medium)
  • In vidIQ's July 2026 study of 448K new channels, a typical first Short drew about 1,360 views in 30 days and Shorts stayed flat across the first ten uploads (about 1,275 by the fifth, 1,344 by the tenth), while long videos rose from 180 to 272 views; 86.5% of new Shorts channels had at least one Short pass 1,000 views. (vidIQ Research, Jul 2026, high)
  • Meta One (launched 15 Sep 2026) sells Instagram Plus at 3.99 USD a month and creator bundles from 14.99 USD (Essential) to 499 USD (Max); creator plans add a bold follow button on Reels and automatic follow invitations to people who engage, while Advanced (from 49.99 USD) adds links in organic Reels and scheduled Stories; Meta promises no extra reach. (Meta Newsroom, Sep 2026, high)
  • For an account with almost no followers, Meta One's automatic follow invitations to people who liked or watched a Reel are the one paid feature that directly targets follower conversion; it is worth a one month trial only after Reels reach a few hundred views each, since invitations scale with engagement. (Meta Newsroom, Sep 2026, low)
  • Instagram's updated Reels camera (2026) adds an undo button for the last clip, stronger countdown and timer tools and less flicker on green screen, which makes recording parent facing behind the scenes Reels (for example the owner showing a Bro Bros render) quicker to do in app. (BetaNews, 2026, low)
  • A 2025 case shows YouTube Kids access is granted per channel: two toy channels with over 7M subscribers each were missing from YouTube Kids until their agency asked for a review; about four weeks later the YouTube Kids team approved them and they appeared in Kids search and suggestions, after which their new Shorts reached about 877K and 301K views. (AIR Media-Tech, Aug 2025, medium)
  • In Emplifi's study of over 10,000 Reels, adding text overlays to music backed Reels raised 30 second retention by up to 9.8% and vertical 9:16 Reels had about 21% more reach and 38.5% better 30 second retention, so every Bro Bros Reel should be full vertical with big on screen lyric words. (Hypebot / Emplifi, 2026, medium)
  • The same study found seamless loops under 7 seconds raised replay rate by 18.7% and reach by 23.6%, so each song should also get one 6 second dance loop Reel whose last frame matches its first. (Hypebot / Emplifi, 2026, medium)
  • Instagram's extra protections for adult managed accounts that feature real children (strict DMs, Hidden Words on by default, less discoverable to accounts teens block) target accounts showing real kids; an animated account like Bro Bros is not covered automatically, so switching on Hidden Words and comment filters by hand keeps our comment section clean for parents. (The Tech Outlook, Jul 2025, low)
  • YouTube Shorts average about 200 billion daily views in 2026 (up from 70 billion in March 2024) and Meta's Reels are played over 200 billion times a day, so short video is where most new viewers first meet a channel. (Kapwing, Jul 2026, medium)
  • The average YouTube Short is watched for about 14 seconds, so every Bro Bros Short needs its hook, the chorus and the signature move inside the first 14 seconds, with anything after that treated as a bonus for loopers. (Kapwing, Jul 2026, medium)
  • About 74% of Shorts views and 55% of Reels views come from non subscribers or non followers, so a Short or Reel must make sense to a stranger with no context (show both Bros, say the song name, no inside jokes). (Kapwing, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Captioned short videos earn about 12% more watch time and are about 80% more likely to be watched to the end, and of viewers who pass the first 3 seconds about 65% stay 10 seconds and 45% stay 30 seconds; big lyric captions are a cheap win for every Bro Bros Short and Reel. (Kapwing (Facebook IQ, Verizon), Jul 2026, medium)
  • The screen free kids audio toy market (Tonies, Yoto) is estimated at about 860M USD in 2026, and parents say they buy these players to protect eyesight, reduce addictive screen habits and build listening skills and focus, so Bro Bros songs should also be released as clean audio tracks that make sense without pictures. (Pulse (parenting news), May 2026, medium)
  • Socialinsider's 2025 YouTube Shorts dataset (millions of Shorts, updated 6 Nov 2026) found views often arrive late: average views were about 833 in days 1 to 5 and 1,786 in days 5 to 10 but about 3,310 in days 25 to 30, the largest window, so a Short should be judged after about 30 days (review over 90) rather than deleted or reposted after a slow first week. (Socialinsider, Nov 2026, medium)
  • YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels age differently: Reels gather most views in their first 5 days and fade after day 10, while Shorts can spike weeks later as YouTube keeps testing them, so a slow Reel can be remixed after a week but a slow Short should be left alone for a month. (Socialinsider, Nov 2026, medium)
  • YouTube held about 13.4% of all US TV screen viewing in April 2026 (Nielsen's Gauge), matching its July 2025 peak and up from about 12.7% in January and February 2026, so the living room TV is now a main screen for our songs and compilations, where big, readable visuals and full length mixes matter. (Adwave (Nielsen Gauge), Jul 2026, high)
  • Samsung TV Plus (about 100M monthly active users) expanded creator led FAST channels to the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Thailand and the Philippines in Sep 2026 and brought Mark Rober TV, dubbed, to Brazil and Mexico; channels come through partner studios, not open sign up, so a big Bro Bros catalogue with dubbed tracks could later be pitched through such a partner. (Señal News, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Amazon announced a Fire TV Creator Hub at Cannes Lions (Jun 2026) to surface YouTube and TikTok creators on Fire TV, aiming to support 500+ creators by 2027 (MrBeast and 5-Minute Crafts among the first); no kids channels were named, so the TV creator lane is still open for kids music brands. (Tubefilter, Jun 2026, medium)
  • PwC's 2026 Gen Alpha survey (1,004 US kids aged 7 to 14) found the top reasons kids quit an app are boredom (52%), too many ads (47%) and slow loading (36%), so slow intros and repetitive filler lose older kids fast. (pwc.com, Mar 2026, high)
  • In the same PwC survey 68% of 7 to 14 year olds regularly use YouTube against 21% to 46% for TikTok (rising with age), and kids average 3.6 hours of recreational screen time a day. (pwc.com, Mar 2026, high)
  • Precisify (Feb 2026) found 55% of US parents watch YouTube together with their children, so our videos should be pleasant for adults too (no shrill loops) because a parent is often on the sofa. (advanced-television.com, Feb 2026, high)
  • A plain 'Musical Chairs' party game on Roblox has about 560M visits, 1.7M favourites, a peak of about 33K players at once and 8.4 minute average sessions (late 2026), proof that 'music stops, everybody stops' games still hook kids, which supports our freeze dance and musical statues songs. (rotrends.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Rapper bbno$'s charity concert on Roblox (mid 2026) reached 28M unique viewers with 8.5M watching at the peak, so music events inside kids games now draw audiences bigger than most kids TV premieres. (tubefilter.com, Jul 2026, high)
  • Roblox added a library of licensed pop tracks (Teddy Swims, Alex Warren and others) to its Creator Store through the indie distributor Too Lost in July 2026, so game builders now pick soundtracks there; distributing our own songs through such a partner could one day put Bro Bros music inside kids' games. (tubefilter.com, Jul 2026, low)
  • Kaspersky's 2026 Safe Kids data (worldwide, May 2025 to Apr 2026) puts YouTube at 29% of children's time in the top 25 Android apps, ahead of WhatsApp (16%), TikTok (12%), Roblox (9%) and Instagram (8%), with Spotify at only about 1%. (kaspersky.com, 2026, high)
  • In Amazon's UK Alexa review of Jan to Nov 2025, the KPop Demon Hunters soundtrack was the second most played artist, just behind Taylor Swift, and its song 'Golden' was the second most requested song, so family films' music dominates what households ask smart speakers for. (t3.com, Dec 2025, high)
  • Amazon publishes its national 'most asked of Alexa' year lists around 11 to 15 December (UK 11 Dec, India 15 Dec 2025, covering January to November), a yearly moment to see which kids and family songs households request by voice. (t3.com and aboutamazon.in, Dec 2025, medium)
  • KIDZ BOP and Amazon once made a voice duet ('Alexa, play a duet with KIDZ BOP') of its most requested Halloween song, at a time the brand had nearly 1B Amazon Music streams, so voice assistants reward kids songs with short, easy to say names that children can request themselves. (kidzbop.com, Oct 2019, low)
  • Tubi, the free ad supported streaming service, calls 2026 its 'cartoon era': it added hundreds of classic Sesame Street episodes (seasons 1 to 38, April 2026) and classic Cartoon Network series that a paid service removed, filed under a Family Shows genre, so free streamers are actively collecting kids catalogues and could later license a large Bro Bros song library. (cabletv.com, Apr 2026, medium)
  • Sesame Street is now split across a paid service for new seasons, another for some library, and free episodes on Tubi, PBS Kids and YouTube, showing that even the biggest kids brands spread one catalogue over many windows; our plan of full songs on YouTube plus compilations elsewhere follows the same playbook. (cabletv.com, Apr 2026, low)
  • Yoto's Canadian best seller list in mid November 2026 holds 16 story collections and only four music cards in its top 20 (KPop Demon Hunters 4th, Disney Hits, Sing with Raffi, Frozen songs), so on screen free audio players stories outsell songs and only film soundtracks or a classic family singer make it as music. (ca.yotoplay.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Blank 'Make Your Own' Yoto cards are the second best seller in that list, meaning many parents load their own audio onto kids' players, so offering free downloadable audio of our songs (for personal use) is a way into screen free listening without a licensing deal. (ca.yotoplay.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • Meta's Creator Fast Track (18 Mar 2026) gives creators with 100K+ followers on Instagram, TikTok or YouTube instant Facebook monetisation plus 1,000 dollars a month for three months (3,000 dollars with 1M+), if they post at least 15 Reels on Facebook in every 30 days on at least 10 different days; reposts from other platforms count if original, so once a Bro Bros account passes 100K our daily songs could be cross posted to Facebook for parents. (tubefilter.com, Mar 2026, high)
  • Facebook's audience is adults, so for Bro Bros it is a parent channel rather than a child channel: Reels there should be framed for grown ups sharing songs with their kids (sing along clips, bedtime songs, holiday songs to play at home), and we must check Facebook's monetisation rules for content made for children before relying on that income. (tubefilter.com, Mar 2026 (our reading), low)
  • Kidoodle.TV is a free, ad supported 'safe streaming' service for under 12s in over 160 countries with 30,000+ hand picked, human vetted episodes and 10 to 20 new shows added each week, and it lists music based streams as a priority, a possible extra home for Bro Bros song compilations beyond YouTube. (worldscreen.com, undated, medium)
  • Instagram's 'Use as reference' option (three dot menu on Reels under 90 seconds, iOS first) opens the camera with the original Reel playing in a small window and a countdown, so families can copy a dance in time; Bro Bros dance Reels kept under 90 seconds with a clear, front facing, follow me routine are easy to copy and can spread through copies. (metricool.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Instagram stopped letting creators link Reels together into a series on 28 Oct 2026 and is only testing a new Series hub with a Watch Next button, so for multi part song stories we should use pinned Reels, a highlight and clear part numbers in captions rather than relying on series links. (metricool.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Edits now lets creators add a clickable link to the sound used in a Reel, so every Bro Bros Reel should carry our own named original audio (for example 'Bro Bros, Snow Is Lava') with the link on, making it easy for other families and creators to find and reuse our song rather than a copyrighted track. (metricool.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Shorts trackers put Shorts at over 200B daily views in 2026 (about 70B in 2024) and say top performers post 18 to 22 Shorts a month against an average of about 7, which supports our daily Shorts plus Reels cadence, although the article does not name its sources. (anijam.ai, Nov 2026, low)
  • A 2026 Precisify parent survey reports 88% of US parents say their 2 to 5 year olds prefer YouTube over on demand and broadcast TV, 55% of parents watch YouTube with their kids and over half of kids watch it on a TV screen, so long form Bro Bros videos are often a shared living room watch. (Precisify via Tubefilter, Feb 2026, medium)
  • In Instagram's Features test (from 26 Oct 2026) up to eight short vertical Reels can link to one long horizontal video, so each Bro Bros compilation could get up to eight song teaser Reels that all lead to the full playlist video once the tool reaches our account. (Variety via Online Tech Tips, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Instagram Features does not share ad revenue with creators yet (Instagram is only exploring brand, fan and platform deals), so on Instagram long compilations are for reach and fan building while YouTube stays the place that earns from long videos. (Variety via Online Tech Tips, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Meta's 'Series' tab, which groups episodic Reels on a profile and lets a viewer tap from one episode to the whole set, has been in testing since spring 2026 in the US, India and Mexico, so numbered Bro Bros story Reels (Episode 1, 2, 3) are ready to slot into it when it opens to us. (TechCrunch via Lindsey Gamble, Jun 2026; Online Tech Tips, Oct 2026, medium)
  • A 2026 Shorts retention study sorts curves into three shapes: a cliff (30 to 50% gone by second 3), a hump (strong middle, hard ending, best for shares) and a plateau (above 70% all the way with a rewatch spike over 100% at second 1), and the plateau is what the feed rewards most. (Aibrify, Apr 2026, medium)
