  • YouTube's 'Get Feedback' button for Shorts (expanding from 9 Sep 2026) checks a draft's hook strength, pacing and visuals in the upload screen and suggests fixes without editing; it is only for US creators over 18 on the phone app, so from India we cannot rely on it and must keep our own hook checklist. (searchenginejournal.com, Sep 2026, high)
  • Since 24 Aug 2026 paid ad views, including bumper and non skippable ads, also add to a video's public view count, so if we ever promote a Bro Bros song with ads its public count will rise without matching engaged views; engaged views and watch hours are what YouTube pays on. (newscaststudio.com, Aug 2026, high)
  • A YouTube Labs experiment called VibeCheck acts as an AI coach for a Short's pacing, hook and lighting; it is separate from Get Feedback and only open to test users, a sign YouTube now grades hooks and pacing automatically, which supports our rule of a clear hook in the first second. (searchenginejournal.com, Sep 2026, low)
  • UK broadband data from Virgin Media O2 shows home network traffic jumping at 3:40 PM every weekday as children get home and climbing until about 5 PM, with parents naming YouTube (61%) as the top after school screen; 3:40 PM in the UK is 21:10 IST, so a song posted by about 18:30 to 19:30 IST would be fresh for the UK after school wave. (yorkshirepost.co.uk, 2026, medium)
  • EU Kids Online 2026 (29,169 children aged 9 to 16 in 19 European countries) found screen use peaks after school in the afternoon (about 80% use screens then) and again in the evening before bed (about 67%), while family dinner time is mostly screen free (about 15%), so European kids' two windows are after school and pre bedtime, not dinner. (lisboncouncil.net, 2026, high)
  • Metricool's model for our brand for 20 to 26 Nov 2026 puts Friday 20 Nov at 10:00 IST (about 10.5K) almost level with 16:00 IST (10.7K), while Saturday and Sunday peak at 16:00 IST with only about half the weekday value, so our two existing slots stay right and Friday is the one day the morning slot is as strong as the afternoon. (Metricool, Nov 2026, high)
  • YouTube demoed video cut testing on 25 Sep 2026: upload two or three edits of the same video (for example two different openings) and Studio shows each one's retention curve so the creator keeps the cut that holds attention; it is still 'coming soon', title testing took 84 days from stage debut to creators, so mid December is the earliest likely date, and access for made for kids channels is not confirmed. (PPC Land, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Since YouTube publishes no universal Shorts retention target, the sound way to judge a Bro Bros Short is against our own Shorts in the same length band (15 to 30 seconds versus 30 to 60 seconds) and topic, using 'chose to view' and engaged views rather than raw views. (bytecap.io, Jul 2026, medium)
  • YouTube's 1 Oct 2026 Shorts update ranks original clips first, and Shorts revenue sharing counts only engaged views, which exclude re uploads and compilations with nothing new added (simple template edits or a voice over describing the clip do not count as new), so a Bro Bros 'best of' Short stitched from older Shorts should add a fresh intro, new scene or new verse rather than just re cut old clips, and the same Short should never be posted twice. (ppc.land, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Creator analysts report (not confirmed by YouTube) that Shorts search now shows more recent Shorts from small channels, and the Shorts that rank there answer one specific search in plain words, so each Bro Bros Short title should name the exact need a parent types, such as 'brush your teeth song for toddlers'. (tunepocket.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • Metricool's YouTube model for our brand for Friday 20 Nov 2026 scores 10:00 IST (about 10.5K) almost level with 16:00 IST (about 10.7K), while Wednesday and Thursday clearly favour 16:00 (about 12.0K), so on Fridays either slot works for the week's strongest song. (Metricool, Nov 2026, medium)
  • YouTube says no single metric ranks a video and signal weights change by device and moment: time spent tends to count more on the TV app, while likes and dislikes count more on phones, so our long compilations should be built to hold the living room screen and our Shorts to earn quick reactions on phones. (ppc.land on Creator Insider, Sep 2026, medium)
  • YouTube once tested capping how many times one video is recommended to the same viewer at eight, after finding a single upload had been shown to one person 19 times without a click; repeated unclicked impressions are therefore wasted, which is another reason to refresh a weak thumbnail rather than wait. (ppc.land on Creator Insider, Sep 2026, low)
  • YouTube's growth lead advises keeping one channel when the same viewers would enjoy both kinds of video and opening a second channel only when the promise to viewers truly differs, so Bro Bros dance songs, holiday songs and learning songs belong on one channel, while a future dubbed language would need its own audio track rather than a new channel. (ppc.land on Creator Insider, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Metricool's Instagram best times for 20 to 26 Nov 2026 put Friday 10:00 IST highest of the week (about 6.7K), with Wednesday and Thursday 10:00 close behind and a second weekday rise at 18:00 IST; Saturday and Sunday run at about half, so the 10:00 Reel slot stays right and Friday morning is the best Reel of the week. (Metricool, Nov 2026, medium)
  • On 13 Nov 2026 YouTube renamed desktop Studio Analytics to 'Insights', with written summaries of why numbers moved, and turned the Trends tab into 'Research', which ranks outlier videos against each channel's usual views (a 5x score means five times that channel's normal for the format). (ppc.land, Nov 2026, high)
  • The new Research tab in YouTube Studio adds a 'Watched by my viewers' filter that shows what our own audience watched on other channels in the last month, a free, made for kids safe way to see which competitor songs and topics our viewers also choose. (ppc.land, Nov 2026, medium)
  • The AI summary card in the new Insights view only shows for creators eligible for Ask Studio, which excludes made for kids channels, so Bro Bros should rely on the standard desktop reports and the Research outlier list, which YouTube says remain available. (ppc.land, Nov 2026, medium)
  • YouTube's discovery lead Todd Beaupre said on 27 Oct 2026 that 'Test and compare' thumbnail tests currently split traffic evenly at random, and that a future version will send each viewer group (for example people who already watch the channel versus newcomers) the thumbnail that works best for them, so Bro Bros should keep testing two clearly different thumbnails (a close up face and a wide dance scene) rather than near copies. (founderpresence (citing Creator Insider), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Metricool's 2026 YouTube study (via eMarketer) found 61% of organic views now come from the Shorts feed, 11% from subscribers and 9% from search, and only 3% of viewers go to a creator's channel page directly, so YouTube works as a discovery feed far more than as a channel you visit. (eMarketer citing Metricool, 2026, medium)
  • In the same study Shorts views rose about 127% year on year while brands posted over 20% more Shorts, but watch time per Short fell about 67% and interactions about 15%, so each Short now has to win in the first second against far more competition. (eMarketer citing Metricool, 2026, medium)

  • In Adobe's 2026 survey of 507 Shorts creators, Saturday (25%) and Friday (23%) were named the best days and 6 to 8 pm local time the peak hours, which supports putting our strongest Shorts on Friday and Saturday evenings in the target market's time zone (creator opinion, not measured data). (ChannelX citing Adobe Express, Jul 2026, low)
  • Since 21 Oct 2026, when YouTube's systems flag unusual activity on a channel, uploads, live streams, playlist edits, custom thumbnails and visibility changes are frozen for everyone on the channel for a review that usually takes about 24 hours; existing videos and money are untouched, so if a Metricool scheduled upload fails we should check Studio for this notice before retrying. (TubeBuddy, Oct 2026, medium)
  • YouTube's 2 Oct 2026 Help Community note says recommendations now favour original content and cut reach for Shorts that re upload another channel's video without adding original work, which protects channels like ours that animate every song from scratch. (TubeBuddy, Oct 2026, medium)
  • vidIQ's study of about 40 million US long form uploads (updated Jun 2026), comparing each video's 30 day views with its own channel's average, found Sunday uploads do best (about +3.5%) and Wednesday worst (about -2%), and the hour of upload evens out within a few percent by day 30, so for Bro Bros consistency matters far more than the exact minute. (vidIQ, Jun 2026, medium)

  • vidIQ also advises clustering one long video with 2 or 3 Shorts across the week and not posting a long video and a Short within the same four hours, but shows no data for it, which conflicts with our plan of a Short 5 minutes after each song; worth testing for one week rather than changing now. (vidIQ, Jun 2026, low)
  • Metricool's best time model for our brand for 21 to 27 Nov 2026 again peaks YouTube at 16:00 IST on every day, highest on Wednesday (about 12,000) and Thursday (about 12,000) and lowest on Saturday and Sunday (about 5,600 to 5,900), matching the current 16:00 IST slot. (Metricool, Nov 2026, high)
  • A June 2026 creator blog (weak, unnamed sources) claims YouTube now gives more weight to whether a viewer keeps watching after a video and discounts videos that people quickly back out of from recommendations over about seven days, with mid sized channels reporting 20 to 30% fewer impressions; if true, every Bro Bros song should end by leading straight into the next song or a playlist.   • Fanpage Karma's 2026 summary of Instagram ranking says negative signals (hide, not interested, unfollow and quick Reel skips) now weigh more heavily and shares, especially shares with a comment, weigh more than likes, so our 75 to 89% early skip rates actively hurt each next Reel's reach.   • Metricool's Instagram best time model for 21 to 27 Nov 2026 (US Thanksgiving week) shows no holiday shift: 10:00 IST is still the top hour every day (Friday about 6.7K, Wednesday about 6.5K, Saturday 3.4K, Sunday 2.6K), so the morning Reel slot needs no change for Thanksgiving week. (Metricool, Nov 2026, high)
  • An unconfirmed creator analysis (Mario Joos, backed by Tim Chesney) suggests that since mid Sept 2025 Shorts older than about 28 to 30 days get far fewer feed impressions, so Shorts reach comes mostly in the first month and a steady stream of new Shorts matters more than hoping old ones revive; YouTube has not confirmed it. (Search Engine Journal, Dec 2025, low)
  • Metricool's 2026 data (cited 1 Nov 2026) says Reels collect about 65% of their views and 61% of their interactions in the first three days, so each Bro Bros Reel should be judged at 72 hours and go out at a time when our audience is awake, not left to grow slowly. (blog.mean.ceo citing Metricool, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In the Research tab YouTube launched on 13 Nov 2026 (Trends renamed), a video's outlier score compares it with the same channel's earlier videos of the same format, so '5x' means five times that channel's usual views; Bro Bros can use it to find which of our own songs broke out, not only big rivals. (PPC Land, Nov 2026, high)
  • YouTube says the 13 Nov 2026 move from Analytics to Insights only rewrites the desktop view into plain language summaries; advanced analytics and real time data stay the same, so the 48 hour and 7 day checks of our uploads keep working as before. (PPC Land citing TeamYouTube, Nov 2026, high)

  • Since early November 2026 US viewers see YouTube's AI custom feeds in the top bar of Home where the old topic chips used to be, so a parent typing a plain request like 'calm songs for my toddler' gets a feed built from video meaning; plain, descriptive titles and descriptions ('a counting song for preschoolers about...') help Bro Bros show up there.   • YouTube's zero minute daily Shorts limit, first a parental setting, is now offered to every phone and tablet user (June 2026) and removes the Shorts tab and Shorts shelf for that person, so a growing slice of family phones will only ever meet Bro Bros through long videos, which is another reason the long song plus thumbnail, not the Short, carries the channel.   • YouTube tested a desktop Home layout in June 2026 that puts long horizontal videos at the top and pushes Shorts lower, while mobile still opens with one big video then a row of Shorts; on computers and TVs our long songs compete mostly with other long videos, so strong thumbnails matter most there. (EURweb, Jun 2026, low)
  • YouTube's blog recap of 16 Nov 2026 (Rene Ritchie) says the coming video A/B test runs two or three cuts of one video, starting with Shorts, names a predicted winner from retention curves rather than click rate, and gives the creator seven days to choose which edit stays live; no release date or eligibility is set yet. (ppc.land citing YouTube blog, Nov 2026, high)
  • YouTube's creator liaison said in October 2026 that adding a voice over, small technical edits or a different template does not make a reused clip original for the Shorts feed, so our Shorts should always be freshly cut from our own songs with a new hook rather than the same clip reposted with a new caption. (ppc.land citing Creator Insider, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Under the spam policy that YouTube ties to its Shorts originality push, a warning can be cleared by optional training after 90 days, but three strikes within 90 days can end a channel, so any reused or mass produced looking upload risks more than just lower reach. (ppc.land, Oct 2026, medium)
  • An Instagram algorithm tracker updated 18 Nov 2026 lists no ranking rule that helps new or small accounts in particular: the routes for a new account remain Trial Reels shown to non followers first, original posts (most posts in the last 30 days must be original to be recommended) and watch time, likes and sends.   • Metricool's best time grid for our brand for 21 to 27 Nov 2026 puts the YouTube peak at 16:00 IST on every day of the week, strongest on Wednesday (about 12,000) and Thursday (about 12,000) and weakest on Saturday and Sunday (about 5,600 to 5,900), so the 16:00 IST slot stays and the week's strongest new song fits Wednesday or Thursday rather than the weekend.   • Nielsen counted Christmas Day 2025 as the biggest US streaming day ever, 55.1B minutes and over 54% of all TV time, with YouTube the top streaming platform for December (12.7%), so Bro Bros should have its Christmas songs and a long Christmas compilation live well before 25 Dec and keep both daily slots running on Christmas Day itself.   • A RouteNote post (Dec 2025) claims Boxing Day brings a wave of new phones and tablets being set up, but gives no numbers; treat it only as a reason to have a pinned 'start here' playlist of our best songs ready by 26 Dec, not as proven timing data. (RouteNote, Dec 2025, low)

  • In AIR's 31,852 video timing study, 04:00 UTC takes about 12% of all uploads and returns only average views, while 12:00 UTC (17:30 IST) gets under 4% of uploads but runs about 1.4 times normal views with good retention, so an uncrowded upload hour can beat a popular one; our planned bonus Short test should include a 17:30 IST slot. (AIR Media-Tech, Jul 2026, medium)
  • A University of South Australia study of 358 children aged 9 to 10 (Pediatric Obesity) found they spend about 39% more time on screens in school holidays than in term, over an hour more a day, so from mid December (Northern Hemisphere winter break, Southern summer) daytime hours become prime viewing and our 16:00 IST slot (late morning in Europe) gains value. (UniSA via Zee News, medium)
  • AIR reports (May 2026) a localised Spanish kids channel that YouTube's recommendation system had wrongly flagged: within 30 days of the flag being lifted its recommendations rose from about 550 to 28,222, watch hours from 1,388 to 43,178 and views 3.6 times, so if Bro Bros' Suggested traffic ever collapses overnight with no policy notice, we should check Studio for limits and ask YouTube creator support rather than keep posting into the void.   • Metricool's YouTube grid for our brand for 21 to 27 Nov 2026 shows weekends flatten into a plateau from 16:00 to 18:00 IST (Sunday 17:00 about 5,400 against 16:00 about 5,600) with a second bump at 10:00 IST on Saturday, so on weekends a video posted anywhere between 15:30 and 16:30 IST loses little. (Metricool, Nov 2026, high)
  • Google's 2026 holiday report on YouTube says gamified gift formats gain views sharply just before Black Friday and stay high until mid December, then on 26 December interest switches to unboxing and 'what I got' videos (over 30M views for such titles in Dec 2025 to Jan 2026), so Bro Bros should schedule a 'what we got' thank you song to go live on 25 or 26 December. (Google, 2026, high)
  • Sendible's April 2026 Reels timing guide gives conflicting answers (5 AM, then 9 AM to noon, then 8 AM to noon on Wednesday and Thursday) and states no time zone, a reminder that generic best time articles disagree and our own Metricool grid (Reels peak 10:00 IST) is the better guide.   • On Alphabet's 29 Oct 2025 earnings call Sundar Pichai said that in the US Shorts now earn more revenue per watch hour than regular in stream video, which explains why YouTube keeps handing Home feed rows to Shorts; for Bro Bros every long song should have a Short that leads viewers into it.   • YouTube says (Jan 2026) its recommendation safeguards for young viewers automatically break repeated viewing loops in sensitive categories such as body comparison, so a kids channel's reach depends on staying in plainly positive themes (friendship, learning, helping) that the system never needs to cap.   • YouTube describes supervised accounts for children with three levels (Explore, Explore More, Most of YouTube) next to the YouTube Kids app for ages 0 to 12, so the same Bro Bros video can reach a child through four different surfaces, and only clearly made for kids, high quality videos are eligible for the youngest one.   • Most UK schools break up for Christmas on Friday 18 Dec 2026 and return on 4 Jan 2027 (Scotland 6 Jan), so UK daytime kids viewing should rise from Saturday 19 Dec, which makes our 16:00 IST slot (10:30 London) a true family morning slot for those two weeks. (LBC, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Delhi's state school calendar puts the 2026 to 27 winter vacation at 1 to 15 Jan 2027, two weeks later than the UK and US breaks, so in north India the holiday viewing bump (and kite festival songs for Makar Sankranti on 15 Jan) falls in the first half of January rather than at Christmas.   • In an AIR case study of a large kids channel (Oct to Dec 2025) total views fell about 15% when its Shorts views dropped, yet revenue rose about 53% because long form views grew about 20% and long form revenue about 88%, so for a made for kids channel long form songs and compilations carry the money while Shorts mainly buy reach.   • Ofcom's tracking puts about 47% of UK 8 to 14s' daily online time between 15:00 and 20:59 local time, and weekends run about 4h07m against 3h24m on weekdays, which supports publishing a few hours before the after school window and expecting bigger weekend sessions.   • By 8 Nov 2026 YouTube had pinned viewers' AI described custom feeds to the top navigation bar for US users, replacing the old fixed topic chips there, so a US parent typing a feed like 'happy dance songs for toddlers' becomes a new way in; our titles and descriptions should use the plain words a parent would type (dance, toddler, sing along, bedtime). (socialmediatoday.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • YouTube is merging Ask Studio with the YouTube Help chat into one creator window (Nov 2026), and with the creator's permission Ask Studio can watch thumbnail performance and run tests on older videos, so once our channel has steady views we can let it test new thumbnails on our older songs instead of making them by hand.   • Metricool's best time grid for our brand for 22 to 28 Nov 2026 (Asia/Kolkata) puts YouTube's top hour at 16:00 IST on all seven days, strongest on Wednesday (about 12.0K) and Thursday (about 12.0K) and weakest on Saturday (about 5.9K) and Sunday (about 5.6K), so the 16:00 IST main upload stays right and our strongest song of the week fits Wednesday or Thursday better than the weekend. (Metricool, Nov 2026, high)
  • For Instagram the same Metricool grid peaks at 10:00 IST every day of 22 to 28 Nov 2026 (Wednesday about 6.5K, Friday about 6.7K) with a second smaller bump at 18:00 IST, while 16:00 IST scores only about two thirds of the 10:00 peak, so our 10:00 IST Reel is in the best Instagram hour and the 16:00 Reel could be tested at 18:00 instead. (Metricool, Nov 2026, high)

(Metricool, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Parent guides updated in October 2026 tell families to use YouTube Kids' Approved Content Only mode for ages 4 to 7 (no search, only hand picked videos), to switch autoplay off and to send children over 8 to the Subscriptions tab instead of Home, so a growing share of kids viewing is chosen by parents channel by channel and a calm, trustworthy channel page and playlists help us get picked. (Screenwise, Oct 2026, medium)

(Screenwise, Oct 2026, low)

(vidIQ, Jul 2026, high)
  • In Metricool's YouTube grid for our brand for 22 to 28 Nov 2026 the 04:00 to 05:00 IST hours score only about 1,400 to 2,900 against 9,300 to 12,000 at 16:00 on weekdays, so the plan's 04:30 IST slot reaches few of our current, mostly Indian viewers at upload time and must be judged only on whether it adds US viewers over 2 weeks. (Metricool, Nov 2026, high)
  • Sprout Social's 2026 Instagram study (about 2B engagements across 307K profiles, 27 Nov 2025 to 27 Feb 2026, so it covers the holidays) found the best hours are weekday early afternoons into evening in the audience's local time, Tuesday and Wednesday strongest, with weekends and the 3 to 7 AM window weakest and no separate timing for Reels, which backs our weekday 16:00 IST Reels for Indian viewers and lighter weekend posts.   • Since a May 2026 server side update, YouTube on Google TV and Samsung TVs lists Subscriptions and Library right under Search and Home in the sidebar and adds two direct channel shortcuts there, so on the living room screen, where most kids watch, a channel a family returns to often can sit one click from Home; repeat family viewing of Bro Bros playlists matters more than one off hits. (Advertising Week, Jan 2026, medium)
  • Metricool's 2026 YouTube study (799,718 videos, 71,177 accounts, all categories) found long videos performed best per video at 2 to 4 uploads a week, 4 to 7 a week added only about 6% more monthly views, and above 7 a week total views fell; for Shorts the lift peaked around 5 a month and disappeared above about 35 a month, so at 14 long videos and 14 Shorts a week Bro Bros is far past the point where more uploads help, and making each song stronger beats adding more (correlational, not kids specific). (Metricool, Aug 2026, medium)
  • In the same Metricool study long videos that used hashtags got about 17% fewer views but about 13% more interactions, and playlists brought about 5% of views while end screens brought well under 0.1%, so our long song descriptions should carry at most one or two hashtags and put the effort into playlists rather than end screens (which made for kids videos lose anyway). (Metricool, Aug 2026, medium)
  • Since about October 2026 YouTube tests Ask YouTube answer previews at the top of normal search results for a small group of signed in US desktop users searching in English: a short AI answer plus key moments from matching videos, shown for open ended or how to questions; YouTube said over 140M people used Ask YouTube in June 2026. (Uppbeat (citing Creator Insider), Oct 2026, medium)
  • Per YouTube's Creator Insider, clicks that come from Ask YouTube count exactly like normal search for impressions, views, watch time, ad revenue and Partner Program watch hours, and YouTube's only stated advice is clear titles, detailed descriptions and timestamp chapters, so a parent question such as 'a song to teach my toddler to brush teeth' can land on the exact chapter of a Bro Bros compilation if chapters name each song's task. (Uppbeat (citing Creator Insider), Oct 2026, medium)
  • Barb saw YouTube viewing on UK TV sets spike around 3 pm on weekdays, which it linked to school age children switching on YouTube when they get home, more support for having a fresh Bro Bros long video already live by early afternoon in each big market.   • All five of The Kiboomers' most viewed videos are movement games: Going on a Dragon Hunt (37.4M), Freeze Dance Song 2 (31.1M), Red Light Freeze Dance (30M), Going on a Dinosaur Hunt (23.4M) and Floor is Lava 2 Freeze Dance (18.2M), and sequels of a winning game (Freeze Dance 2, Floor is Lava 2) do as well as originals.   • The Kiboomers' newest upload is a seasonal movement game, Shake Your Santa Hat (6 Nov 2026), so classroom channels release Christmas dance songs in the first week of November to catch teachers' December planning. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Kaboochi (2.17M subscribers, 2,225 videos) gets about 11.6M views a month, and its biggest hits are theme twists on the Finger Family song (Football Finger Family 29M, Planet Finger Family 17M), so a known song frame plus a new theme is its main growth trick, though sheer volume gives low views per video. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In Tubefilter's most subscribed list for the week of 8 Nov 2026 only three kids or family channels made the top 50: Pokemon Kids TV (Japan, about 400K new subscribers, down 20%), Cadel and Mia (about 300K) and VocaVoca Kids Songs (US, about 300K), so a nursery song channel like VocaVoca can still out gain most of YouTube. (tubefilter.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • CoComelon's owner Moonbug launched The Melon Patch on YouTube (season 2 from 23 Jul 2026), a live action show led by a music teacher host with acoustic nursery rhymes, original songs and real children singing along in new 15 minute episodes every other week, a move towards the warm human host style Ms Rachel proved. (moonbug.com, Jul 2026, high)
  • Moonbug's content chief says the company is YouTube first, a brand must build a strong YouTube audience before toys, live tours and streaming deals, and content should fit each viewing moment from a short clip on a phone in the car to living room co viewing; its 2026 slate adds a Little Angel spin off with pop songs and pretend play for ages 3 to 5. (senalnews.com, Jun 2026, medium)
  • VocaVoca's last 28 days to 12 Nov 2026 brought about 1.42B views versus 2.91B in October, so even a fast rising song channel roughly halved its monthly reach once the Halloween spike passed; seasonal surges must be followed at once by the next season's songs. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • VocaVoca's newest upload, a good manners song ('May I Please?', 11 Nov 2026), reached about 133K views in its first 13 hours, more evidence that manners, habits and safety songs are this channel's engine after Halloween. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Jasmin and James (Germany based duo, 43.1M subs, 79.9B views from about 26,700 videos) get their best recent Shorts from behind the scenes bloopers (120K to 188K views) and 'Can you do it?' challenges, ahead of plain trend tutorials; a Bro Bros bloopers Short (a brother slipping on a dance move) and a direct 'Can you do it?' challenge are cheap, proven formats. (Vidanalyze, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Jasmin and James lean on movie character trend tutorials (Spider-Verse costume trends); we skip anything using protected characters and copy only the tutorial format (slow step, then full speed) with our own Bros. (Vidanalyze, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Acamar Films (Bing) launched Again! Again!, a gentle paced public service style preschool channel on YouTube in June 2026 with presenter led themed blocks, live streamed segments and nine starter titles; Acamar already runs 67 channels in 33 languages with 1.3M viewing hours a day. (Senal News, Jun 2026, high)
  • Lalafun's top recent breakout 'Catch the Black Sheep! Baa Baa Song' reached 33M views in about two months, 30 times its median, and its other hits follow the same title shape: an urgent mission for the baby ('Baby Helps the Itsy Bitsy Spider', 'Paramedic Cures the Boo Boos'), then a well known rhyme anchor, one or two emojis and the channel tag. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Lalafun has only 77 videos but 158M views, uploads about three long videos a week averaging nearly 18 minutes with no Shorts, and its estimated audience is the US 44%, UK 17%, Brazil 17%, Turkey 11% and Poland 11%. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Super Simple Songs' best recent upload is a remake of its own 'The Animals On The Farm' (38M views, 5.7 times median), and it now publishes 'High Contrast Kids Video' versions of songs (Fruit Is Yummy, 11M), so remaking our own proven hits and making high contrast baby editions are both proven moves. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Super Simple Songs still uploads only about once a week, recent uploads average about 30 minutes, long form gives 96% of its views, and its estimated audience is the US 53%, UK 18%, Canada 12%, Japan 12% and Vietnam 6%, showing English songs travel to ESL markets in Asia. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Kids Diana Show's recent breakouts are scale challenges ('10 vs 100 vs 1,000,000 House Decorating', 43M) and opposite pairs ('Ice Princess vs Fire Princess', 57M) plus story compilations, formats an animated channel can copy as '1 snowman vs 100 snowmen vs 1,000,000 snowmen' style songs. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Big kids channels keep about 85 to 90% evergreen content and only 10 to 15% trend based (Lalafun and Kids Diana 90/10, Super Simple Songs 85/15), a useful split for planning our 14 songs a week: roughly 12 evergreen and 2 trend songs. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Cocomelon's Instagram (about 790K followers, 1.1K posts) runs as a parenting humour and toddler life account aimed at adults, averaging about 214K Reel plays but only 0.26% likes per follower and about 10 posts in two weeks, far smaller than its YouTube reach. (IQFluence, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Rhymington Square (Canada, 311K subscribers) has 291M views from only 74 videos, about 3.9M per video, built on original friendly monster songs about toddler life; few, strong, rewatchable songs can out earn a big volume of weaker ones. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Rhymington Square's recent breakouts are everyday toddler moments told as songs ('It's Way Too Hot Today' 17M, 'Let's Blow A Bubble' 16M, 'My Glasses' 10M) and numbered sequels of proven hits ('There's A Monster In My Tummy #2', 'Open Shut Them #2'). (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Seasonal holiday songs are Rhymington Square's largest topic cluster (15 of 74 videos) and about 24% of its content is trend based, with audience in the US 61%, Canada 21%, UK 12% and Australia 6%, so holiday songs suit North American audiences especially. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • TinkaBop Baby Sensory, a young baby sensory music channel, had 11 videos and about 5K subscribers by Sep 2026 with a gentle bath time song as its best (18K views), showing how slowly a new routine song channel grows and how bath, wake up and bedtime routines lead in the baby niche. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, low)
  • OutlierKit flags dependence on YouTube Kids distribution and on one signature voice as key risks for small baby music channels, so Bro Bros should keep the Bros' voices consistent but build reach on main YouTube, Shorts and Instagram too. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, low)
  • Cocomelon's biggest 2026 breakouts stack two proven hooks in one title ('Yes Yes Finger Family Playground Song' 52M views, 14 times its median; 'The Rainbow Popsicle Cafe + Super Muffin Man' 21M) or revive a novelty classic ('Bananaphone' 40M). (OutlierKit, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Cocomelon still uploads about three videos a week averaging about 5.5 minutes with almost no Shorts, keeps about 95% evergreen content, and roughly 10% of recent uploads are Hello Kitty and Sanrio collaborations, showing big brands now team up with other kids IP for fresh reach. (OutlierKit, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Cocomelon's estimated audience is the US 50%, India 17%, UK 17%, Canada 11% and Australia 6%, so India is now as big as the UK for English nursery songs. (OutlierKit, Oct 2026, low)
  • Ms Rachel uploads only about 1.4 videos a month but each runs about 45 minutes, and her top titles lead with a parent search promise ('Baby Learning with Ms Rachel', 'Learn to Talk', 'First Words', '2 Year Old Milestones') before 'Nursery Rhymes & Kids Songs', proof that parents search by developmental goal. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • An exploratory academic study of English and Portuguese AI made kids videos (2022 to 2024) found music and stories are the main content types, most such videos get low view counts with a few viral exceptions, and many sit on a spectrum of partial AI use; a Bro Bros edge is visible human craft (story, choreography, edits) on top of AI tools. (AoIR Selected Papers (Mintz and Bozzi), Jan 2026, medium)
  • Super Simple Songs turned 20 in 2026 with over 70M subscribers and 90B views; it began in 2006 as teachers abroad posting songs to help children learn English, so English learning classrooms worldwide are a lasting audience Bro Bros can serve with clear, slow, repeatable English lyrics. (YouTube Official Blog, Aug 2026, high)
  • Super Simple's maker Skyship moved to a self funded Toronto studio in 2015 with 40+ in house animators, musicians, puppeteers and educators, and works with researchers (an Oxford University Press project in Spain) on how music shapes early learning, using that teaching credibility to win parents and teachers. (YouTube Official Blog, Aug 2026, high)
  • Moonbug says Little Angel has over 150M YouTube subscribers and about 1.4B monthly views across 25 languages, and it programmes its linear channels in 100+ countries around daily routines from morning to bedtime (meals, tooth brushing, bedtime), the same routine slots Bro Bros playlists should be named for. (Senal News, Jun 2026, high)
  • Moonbug's 2026 plan is YouTube first but non exclusive ('be on every platform where kids and families are'), extending hit IP into Spotify music, toys and live tours, and it is pushing hardest into Southern Europe (Spain and France), a sign those markets reward kids brands now. (Senal News, Jun 2026, medium)
  • Mother Goose Club licensed its YouTube library to the SKIDOS ad free learning app for ages 2 and up (Aug 2026), showing a later revenue path for a big kids song catalogue: subscription learning apps that pay for familiar, education framed content. (Toy Book, Aug 2026, medium)
  • Moonbug's Blippi spinoff Meekah opened on its own YouTube channel on 7 Nov 2026, warmed up by a single music video ('Happy Place') on 2 Nov, with roughly 15 minute episodes for ages 3 to 6 every other Saturday. (Foro3D, Oct 2026, high)
  • Meekah episodes alternate short bursts of dance and physical play with short pauses, a move then rest rhythm built on UCLA backed learning principles that Bro Bros can copy inside long compilations (dance, calm breath, dance). (Foro3D, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Moonbug launched Big Feelings Music in Sept 2026, offering label services, publishing administration and YouTube distribution to outside children's music creators, a possible future partner route for an independent kids song brand. (Advanced Television, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Pinkfong is releasing the soundtrack of its 5 Dec Baby Shark Christmas sing along film in two waves (10 Nov and 27 Nov), 15 tracks with seven new songs, and uses an on screen MC character to lead audience participation, a staged drop pattern we can copy for a December song pack. (Sports Kyunghyang, Oct 2026, high)
  • ChuChu TV grew by refreshing old nursery rhymes with new stories instead of making lullabies, and even early on earned 40 to 50% of revenue abroad (mostly UK, US and Canada) while Vietnam gave many views but little revenue. (Indian Television, 2018, low)
  • Kids Diana's network is 32 channels in 17 languages with about 429M subscribers and 261B views; its 27 smaller language channels together have about 240M subscribers, more than the 138M main channel, showing that separate dubbed channels can outgrow the original. (AIR Media-Tech, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Kids Diana's largest language channels are Spanish (41.1M), Arabic (30.9M), English (30M) and Hindi (29.4M), and about 12 of its channels run 24/7 live streams, while the main channel has added multi language audio tracks. (AIR Media-Tech, Oct 2026, medium)
  • In Tubefilter's week of 8 Nov 2026, Spanish preschool channel El Tren Nam Nam dropped 52% (from No. 7 to No. 39) while Keizo and Friends climbed from No. 29 to No. 20 and two Sierra and Rhia channels sat in the top 8, showing how fast kids channel weekly views swing. (Tubefilter, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A Spanish kids channel admitted to the YouTube Kids app about a month after an official partner submitted it saw views grow 396%, with the app supplying 67.4% of its traffic, so getting Bro Bros reviewed for the Kids app is one of the biggest single growth levers once the catalogue is clean. (AIR Media-Tech, 2026, medium)
  • AIR's order of fixes for a stalled kids channel is trust signals first (clean thumbnails, remove weak old videos, resolve yellow icons), then dubbed audio tracks, then 24/7 streams, because languages and streams only work once YouTube trusts the channel. (AIR Media-Tech, 2026, medium)
  • BabyBus (44.2M subscribers, about 186M views in the last 28 days) has slowed sharply in 2026: about 100K new subscribers a month versus 300K to 700K in 2024, and monthly views fell from about 328M in April to 218M in October 2026. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • BabyBus's most watched videos are still older evergreen songs (Rainbow Juice colours song from 2022 at 147M views), while its 2025 and 2026 'Sharing is Caring' good habit songs are the clear outliers at 10 to 16 times the channel's normal views, so manners and feelings songs keep pulling new viewers. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon's Portuguese channel posted 48 uploads between 31 Aug and 9 Nov 2026 (29 long videos, median 5:22, and 19 Shorts, median 22 seconds), roughly five uploads a week split about 3 long to 2 Shorts. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon's dubbed channels tag brand new songs with a star and the word NEW at the start of the title and still publish 30 minute holiday compilations, and their best recent long uploads are simple action or routine songs (a rain go away song at 4.7M, a car wash song at 2.4M). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Brazil's kid pop acts show how fast a school age music brand can grow: duo Kysha e Mine reached about 1.2B YouTube views and 130M TikTok likes in roughly a year with a school themed series, and MC Divertida has about 18.3M subscribers; their label has psychologists review lyrics and scripts, which it says wins parent and school trust. (Billboard Brasil, Oct 2025, medium)
  • Disney Jr. tests stories with children through an internal panel and feeds results to writers (its programming head calls young viewers 'our bosses'), and grew SuperKitties over three years with 60 minute specials, shorts and long episodes side by side, so one Bro Bros song should also ship as a Short, a long video and a compilation slot. (Senal News (MIPJunior), Oct 2026, medium)
  • Pinkfong launched 'Baby Shark Boy' in Aug 2026 with the single 'WAVE', which opens on the familiar Baby Shark melody and grows into upbeat electropop with trap beats and a featured K-pop rapper, plus a point choreography that nods to the original dance but stays easy to follow, a way to keep kids who have outgrown nursery songs. (Sports Kyunghyang, Aug 2026, high)
  • Pinkfong's new Baby Shark musical (2 Dec 2026 to 28 Mar 2027, Seoul) has no seats: children roam seven themed zones, join missions, hold colour changing microphones and their voices become part of the music, and the story is about recovering a lost rhythm and melody, showing that 'help us fix the song' participation is the brand's next step. (Sports Kyunghyang, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Russian language family creator Sasha Show grew from about 1.2 to 2.2M new subscribers a month in mid 2026 to 9.47M in October (18.3M total, 633M views in the last 28 days) with only about 46 uploads a year of toy, candy and bath challenge videos and remixes, yet vidIQ models only about 17K USD of earnings, showing how little very large Shorts led kids audiences can pay. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Toys and Colors' franchise reported 136M subscribers and 149B lifetime views, with its top three YouTube channels reaching 348M unique viewers and 11.6B minutes of watch time in 90 days, and its holiday special came with an original single released on Spotify, Amazon Music and Apple Music, so a kids channel's holiday song should also live on music apps. (Senal News (pocket.watch), Nov 2025, medium)
  • Sasha Show's titles lean on famous toy and candy brands and extreme 'who will win' challenges, a growth route Bro Bros should not copy (brand names invite claims and do not suit made for kids quality rules), but its question style titles ('Who will...?') match the mystery question hooks already in our playbook. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, low)
  • Bebefinn's main English channel (37.3M subscribers, 25.1B views, 1,086 videos since Mar 2022) still adds about 370M views a month, but its subscriber gains fell to 100K to 300K a month in 2026 from 500K to 1.3M a month in 2024 and 2025, the same plateau BabyBus and Little Angel show, so the biggest 3D song brands are no longer growing fast and newer channels have room. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Bebefinn's newest upload, 'We Are Car Mechanics! Let's Fix the Car!' (13 Nov 2026), drew about 133K views in 13 hours with a title built as emoji, pretend play job and action call, and its all time top video is a 2022 good morning wake up routine song (775M views), so pretend play jobs and daily routine songs remain the brand's core. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • vidIQ models Bebefinn's main channel at only about 97K USD a month of ad revenue from roughly 370M monthly views (about 0.26 USD per 1,000 views), confirming that made for kids song views earn little per view and that brands like Pinkfong earn mainly from streaming deals, toys and live shows. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Indonesian kids family channel Keizo and Friends (started Dec 2022) reached about 9.9M subscribers and 39.2B views from 1,998 uploads by Oct 2026, adding about 1.65B views and 390K subscribers in 28 days, with a new upload passing 1.5M views in 14 hours; vidIQ models only about 9K USD a month, so its scale comes from Shorts views in a low pay market. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, medium)
  • AIR's study of 282 kids channels found the largest (10M to 50M monthly views) earned the most total revenue at 16+ videos a month, but each video then earned only about 165 USD against about 2,161 USD per video for channels posting one or two a month, so our 14 songs a week buy reach, while a few polished flagship songs per month carry most of the money. (AIR Media Tech, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Keizo and Friends' all time top video is from 7 Dec 2025 (about 626M views), a December upload that kept growing for a year, another sign that early December family videos get a long tail and our holiday songs should be live by the first week of December. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, low)
  • Skyship's live action 'Super Simple Play with Caitie!' (Canada, 5.25M subscribers) steadied at about 47 to 58M views a month through 2026 after a 2025 peak (332M in Apr 2025); its all time hits are 'Here Comes the Fire Truck' (109M), the colour hunt 'I See Something Blue' (78M), a Halloween knock knock song (63M) and the freeze game 'Can You Dance and Stop?' (50M), and vidIQ models about 46K USD a month. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • US rhyme channel Super Supremes (4M subscribers, 960 videos) has been flat since late 2025 at about 3 to 7M views a month and its newest Short (9 Nov 2026, a fire truck wheels song) drew only about 1.8K views in five days, showing that a big but stale subscriber base no longer guarantees views for generic rhyme remakes. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Across both channels the top songs are fire trucks, Halloween and colour or freeze games, and Caitie's newest upload (12 Nov) is already a Christmas party song, so Super Simple starts holiday uploads in mid November. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Five of the ten most viewed YouTube videos of all time are children's songs (led by Baby Shark Dance and CoComelon's Wheels on the Bus), together estimated at about 84M USD in ad revenue, proof that one evergreen kids song can earn for years. (Mediaweek citing BonusInsider, Nov 2025, medium)
  • Lalafun's 'Learning Time!' side channel (605K subscribers, only 91 videos) was flat until May 2026, then jumped to about 34 to 61M views a month from July to October; its hits put a verb and a baby helper into a classic rhyme title ('Catch the Black Sheep!' 76M, 'Baby Helps the Itsy Bitsy Spider!' 31M, 'Animals Go to a Picnic! Wheels on the Bus' 20M). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Funny Lala, Lalafun's kindergarten channel (1.77M subscribers, 326 videos since Jun 2023), still gains about 80K subscribers and 72M views a month, and all of its top five videos are remixes of rhymes into little stories (a rainy farm 'where is the sun?' remix leads at 31.5M). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Lalafun's Canada feed has 2,408 videos and 1.64M subscribers, yet its 31 Oct 2026 toothbrush song drew only 495 views in 41 hours while the brand's young Learning Time channel got about 25K views in under two days on its newest upload, so the algorithm rewards fresh focused channels over huge back catalogues. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Both healthy Lalafun channels title new songs as an action plus a familiar character or animal ('Catch the Little Frogs with Baby Lala!', 'Five Little Ducklings and Mommy Duck'), mixing a known rhyme cue with a small adventure, which is a title pattern we can copy with our own originals ('Catch the Snowflakes with Little Bro!'). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Jason Vlogs, two brothers' kids channel that grew from 23M to 46M+ subscribers with a peak of about 1B views in one month, keeps a baseline of one main video a week with extras as bonuses, plans and batches weeks ahead, and runs on a core team of five. (AIR, Feb 2026, medium)
  • Jason Vlogs brainstorms about 30 ideas a week and produces only 3, filtering by current platform trends, what kids already react to and whether the idea stays fun and teaches something, a stricter filter than making every idea that comes up. (AIR, Feb 2026, medium)
  • ChuChu TV's newest English uploads (Oct to Nov 2026) are 24 to 34 minute story and learning compilations: 'Celebrate and Shine', a combined Diwali and Christmas story video, reached about 197K views in 16 days, a surprise egg colour song about 140K in 9 days and a learning story set about 15K in 2 days, so even a 98M subscriber channel's new uploads start small and the library carries it. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • ChuChu TV tested a 2 minute read along toddler story with copy the duck play actions ('Hello, Ducklings!'), which drew about 94K views in 25 days, close to its long compilations, showing short copy me action stories are a cheap format worth testing beside songs. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Little Angel Playtime (3.24M subscribers) fell from about 10.5M monthly views in Aug 2026 to 8.6M, 7.5M and then 4.9M in October, and its newest song ('Eye Tests Are Not Scary!', 14 Nov) had under 1K views after 11 hours, showing that even a famous brand's spin off channel fades when it keeps posting small routine topics without fresh hooks. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Little Angel and Friends (7.3M subscribers, about 26M views in Oct 2026) earns mostly from 2021 to 2022 songs: Baa Baa Black Sheep 601M, a bedtime 'Monsters Under the Bed' song 210M and a lollipops, balloons and sunglasses colours song 205M; its new Baby John Wheels on the Bus vehicle song had about 3.7K views in 10 hours. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Super Simple Songs' uploads from late August to mid October 2026 were mostly 'Top 20' themed mixes (about 0.8 to 1.2M views each) and two 'Super Simple Live!' Halloween streams, while a single party song, 'Everybody Celebrate' (27 Aug), reached 6M, the clear outlier; a celebration song for any party day can outperform themed compilations. (VidAnalyze, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Pinkfong launched Kikipuppup (with Japan's TBS) on YouTube first, in English, Japanese and Korean, as about 3 minute slapstick episodes with a cat, a dog and a grumpy rival, and is rolling out a wordless comedy (SEALOOK) in Russia, so the biggest song brand is adding short, dialogue light comedy that travels without dubbing. (The Pinkfong Company, Oct 2025, medium)
  • Pinkfong keeps refreshing Baby Shark through partner remixes: a 'Do The Shark' remix in Doggyland's style, a Baby Shark and Peppa Pig mash up for the song's 10th anniversary (26 Dec 2025), and a Bebefinn medley with the London Symphony Orchestra; a hit song can be re released many times in new styles. (Pinkfong newsletter, 2025 to 2026, medium)
  • The Blocks Universe (Numberblocks, Alphablocks) launched its first Christmas single, 'Making Christmas Magical' with K-pop group FIFTY FIFTY, as two videos of the same song a week apart (a live action dance video on 28 Nov, the animated video on 5 Dec) plus a printables hub, a model for getting two premieres out of one holiday song. (Blocks Universe, Dec 2025, medium)
  • Blippi's strongest Shorts of early November 2026 are timed challenges and playground games: 'Can Blippi build a rocket in 45 seconds?' (about 130K views, 2x its usual) and 'Red Light Green Light with kids' (about 198K), so a 'Can the Bro Bros build a snowman in 30 seconds?' countdown Short fits what kids are clicking now. (vidIQ (Blippi videos), Nov 2026, high)
  • Blippi's titles in November follow one pattern: a direct question with the character's name plus a challenge or a 'what if' ('What would Blippi look like as an animal?', 'Can a fire truck be as fast as a race car?'), with one or two emojis; the same pattern works for us as 'Can Vihaan ...?' or 'What if the Bro Bros ...?' Shorts titles. (vidIQ (Blippi videos), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Blippi still alternates 15 minute episodes with 1.5 to 2 hour compilations, and the 2 hour vehicle race (12 Nov) is its top outlier at about 2x, so for a strong brand very long vehicle compilations still pay even after YouTube cut the boost for ultra long videos in 2025. (vidIQ (Blippi videos), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Blippi's 3 November dance collab with Doggyland (ice cream truck dance party, 2:48) scored only about half its normal views, a reminder that a collab or a single dance video does not beat a strong concept like a challenge or a vehicle race. (vidIQ (Blippi videos), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Junior Squad Nursery Rhymes has 5.45M subscribers yet its new uploads get only about 2K to 3K views each in the first week and 4.4M views in 28 days across 1,164 videos, so a big old back catalogue does not lift new uploads; fresh concepts and packaging decide each video. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Junior Squad started Christmas on 5 and 6 Nov 2026 (a Santa finger family Short, its best recent Short at about 9.4K views, and a Christmas version of its ambulance song), while its October outlier was a 75 second Frankenstein dance party song at about 19K views, so short themed dance songs and an early Christmas switch are the safe seasonal plays. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon Brasil's new Portuguese 'Rain Rain Go Away' ('Vá Embora, Chuva', 3:01, 17 Oct 2026) reached about 4.7M views in under a month, about 36 times the channel's usual, and a two song combo ('Lá na lagoa & Os Patinhos', 5:55) reached 1.7M, so re sung classic rhymes are the breakout engine for a Portuguese track. (vidIQ (CoComelon Brasil), Nov 2026, high)
  • CoComelon Brasil had no Christmas video among its last 48 uploads by 10 Nov 2026, while English kids channels switched in the first week of November, so Brazilian Christmas songs can go live later (late November to mid December, when the summer school holidays start). (vidIQ (CoComelon Brasil), Nov 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon Brasil's Shorts are only 11 to 27 seconds (find the hidden JJ, making a JJ snowman or doll, a magic fruit salad) and draw 3K to 92K views, against 12K to 4.7M for its long songs, so even for the biggest brand the local language Shorts are a side feed and long songs do the heavy lifting. (vidIQ (CoComelon Brasil), Nov 2026, high)
  • CoComelon Brasil marks every new long song with a '⭐NOVO⭐' (new) prefix and ends each title with the same brand and category tag, a cheap packaging habit that tells returning parents which upload is fresh; a 'NEW' star prefix on our newest song of the day is worth testing. (vidIQ (CoComelon Brasil), Nov 2026, medium)
  • ChuChu TV's main channel (98.2M subscribers, 61B views) gained no net subscribers in the 28 days to mid November 2026 and its most watched video is a 30 minute classics compilation led by 'Rain Rain Go Away' (109M views), showing that a giant catalogue can stall while old compilations keep earning. (vidIQ (ChuChu TV), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Rain songs keep winning across brands in late 2026 (CoComelon Brasil's 36x rain song, ChuChu TV's top compilation, our own rain themed Didi story among our better Reels), so an original Bro Bros rain song with puddle jumps and umbrella moves is a safe evergreen bet. (vidIQ, Nov 2026 + Metricool, medium)
  • Bebefinn's Portuguese channel (about 9.1M subscribers) gained about 150K subscribers and 296M views in the 28 days to 24 Oct 2026, roughly twice CoComelon Brasil's size and still growing fast, so a newer brand can overtake the incumbent in a dubbed language within about three years. (vidIQ (Bebefinn Português), Oct 2026, high)
  • Bebefinn's Japanese channel (1.62M subscribers) pulled about 108M views in 28 days and adds 50K to 60K subscribers a month, the same monthly views as BabyBus Japan with a quarter of the subscribers, so in Japan a fresh brand's new videos still get recommended while old catalogues plateau. (vidIQ (Bebefinn Japanese), Nov 2026, high)
  • Bebefinn Japanese grew most in January (+110K) and June 2026 (+90K) and least in April and May (+30K), matching school holidays and rainy season in Japan, so Japanese audio tracks should launch before the winter break and the June rainy season. (vidIQ (Bebefinn Japanese), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Bebefinn's newest local uploads are practical life lessons: a Portuguese 'never open the door to strangers' safety song (24 Oct 2026) and a Japanese 'what do we wear on a rainy day?' dressing song (6 Nov), both built as a question the child answers, which supports our safety and routine songs with a question hook. (vidIQ (Bebefinn), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Bebefinn Portuguese's biggest hit is an episode of a shark finger family song (about 60M views, over 100x the channel average), showing that a brand's signature character song re sung locally can carry an entire language channel. (vidIQ (Bebefinn Português), Oct 2026, medium)
  • Lalafun Nursery Rhymes (15.1M subscribers) is one of 2026's fastest growing preschool song channels: about 139M views in April, then 585M to 722M every month from May to October with 500K to 700K new subscribers a month. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Lalafun uploads about three videos a week, almost all long form (recent average about 18 minutes), which shows a mostly long form preschool channel can still grow fast in 2026 without leaning on Shorts. (OutlierKit, Sep 2026, medium)
  • BabyBus's English channel (44.2M subscribers) is steady rather than growing: about 186M to 257M views a month through 2026 and 100K new subscribers a month, flat in October; its newest upload (12 Nov) is a good habits 'Boo Boo Song' that drew about 46K views in 13 hours. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • By 13 November 2026 neither BabyBus English nor Lalafun had posted a Christmas video (Lalafun's newest is a 'Sharing is Great!' manners song, 158K views in under two days), so big preschool brands start Christmas late and an early, original Christmas song still has room. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • VocaVoca (US nursery songs) is 2026's breakout kids song channel: monthly views grew from about 368M in January to 1.11B in July, 1.82B in August, 2.29B in September and 2.91B in October, and subscribers from 4.9M to 10.5M. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • VocaVoca is cooling in November 2026: about 1.46B views in the 28 days to 15 Nov, roughly half its October pace, though it still adds about 1.16M subscribers a month and 300K a week (Tubefilter, week of 8 Nov), a reminder that kids song surges can halve within weeks. (vidIQ and Tubefilter, Nov 2026, medium)
  • VocaVoca's newest upload, 'Toothy and Tootsie Help the Toy Train Find All Colors' (14 Nov 2026, about 121K views in 11 hours), combines three proven hooks at once: named helper characters, a mission verb in the title and this season's toy train theme, plus a colours learning tag. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • VocaVoca's all time top videos are practical life skill songs from 2021 to 2022 (The Dentist Song 164M, Taking Care of Baby 68M, Police Officer Song 52M, Stranger Danger Song 42M, Buckle Up Song 37M), more proof that safety and routine songs keep earning for years. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Pokémon Kids TV has 44.8M subscribers and gains about 1.2M a month (400K in the week of 8 Nov, #23 worldwide) yet draws only about 71M views a month, so a big brand's subscriber surge does not mean views; we should judge competitors and ourselves by monthly views and returning viewers, not subscribers. (vidIQ and Tubefilter, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Super Simple Songs (47.3M subscribers, about 65B views) is still growing in 2026: monthly views rose from about 446M in February to 574M in September and 592M in October, with 100K to 200K new subscribers a month, proof that a mature brand keeps rising through steady themed uploads. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Super Simple Songs' newest song 'Scrubbity Rubbity Doo' (wash your hands and face, 5 Nov 2026) reached about 915K views in nine days; a silly made up word in the title plus a hygiene routine is exactly our playbook's nonsense chant and healthy habit formula. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Super Simple Songs' biggest videos add a new action or a puppet cast to a familiar song ('If You're Happy and You Know It Spin Around' 176M, 'Five Little Speckled Frogs' with frog puppets 164M, '500 Ducks' 214M, the puppet food song 'Are You Hungry?' 183M), so a known tune with one surprising action twist is a proven long term hit. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • By 15 November 2026 Super Simple Songs, BabyBus English and Lalafun had all not yet posted a Christmas song, while smaller channels such as Junior Squad started in early November, so the big preschool brands seem to time Christmas releases for late November or December. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Danny Go! (5.43M subscribers) gets about 160M to 210M views every month of 2026 from just 131 videos, adding 100K to 160K subscribers a month; a few big, carefully made movement videos can out earn hundreds of quick uploads. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Danny Go!'s newest video, the 'Burning ENERGY! Don't Stop Moving Challenge' (9 Sep 2026), reached about 21.5M views in two months; naming a dance song a 'challenge' with a clear goal (never stop moving) suits older preschoolers and school classroom brain breaks. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • All five of Danny Go!'s top videos are pretend danger movement games with sequels: 'Quicksand, Lava, Sharks' compilation 270M, 'The Floor Is Lava 2: Into the Volcano!' 263M, 'The Floor is Lava Dance!' 223M, a spooky spiders version 208M and 'Sharks in the Water 2: Rise of the Shark King!' 202M, so a winning game should get numbered part 2 and seasonal versions. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Bounce Patrol (Australia, 34M subscribers, 28.7B views) has stalled: about 89M views in the 28 days to 27 Oct 2026 with no subscriber change, and its Halloween upload drew only about 371K views in 24 days while its top hits ('Fruit So Yummy' 335M, Wheels on the Bus remixes) are years old, a warning that live action remix channels without new characters lose momentum. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon's main channel (203M subscribers, about 230B views) gets about 1.2B to 1.6B views a month in 2026 after 2.18B in January, with roughly 1M new subscribers every other month; even the biggest kids channel is flat to slightly down, so its audience share is slowly opening to newer brands. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • CoComelon's newest upload (14 Nov 2026) is 'Snowy Holiday Ski Race! JJ VS CODY', a friendly winter race between two characters rather than a Christmas song, about 203K views in its first day or so; a gentle 'Big Bro VS Little Bro' snow race with a tie and a hug at the end fits the same winter competition hook. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon's all time top videos reset classic rhymes in everyday places or routines: 'Humpty Dumpty Grocery Store' 1.57B, 'Yes Yes Fruits Song' 1.24B, 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star' 878M, 'Pasta Song' 417M and 'Fire Truck Wash Song' 402M, supporting our rule of familiar tune plus everyday setting. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • LooLoo Kids, a 3D animated nursery rhyme brand, has about 62.8M subscribers and 43.2B views from only about 985 videos and still uploads (latest 13 Nov 2026), proof that a small catalogue of long compilations can build a giant channel. (subsub.io, Nov 2026, medium)
  • vidIQ's older snapshot of LooLoo Kids showed about 2 uploads a week with an average length of about 31 minutes and a low engagement rate (0.21%), the classic pattern of long, passively watched compilations. (vidiq.com, Oct 2024 data, medium)
  • LooLoo runs separate channels per language (Spanish, Portuguese, Polish, French, Arabic and more); the Spanish one alone has 15.1M subscribers and about 154M views in the 28 days to 14 Nov 2026, so dedicated dub channels can grow into big channels of their own. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • LooLoo's Spanish channel gained 200K to 600K subscribers a month in early 2025 but mostly 0 to 100K a month in 2026, while views stayed around 100M to 150M a month, a sign that old rhyme channels keep views but are losing new fans. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • LooLoo's newest Spanish upload (13 Nov 2026) stacks three classic songs plus a learning tag in one title ('Los Pollitos + Rompe la Piñata + La Vaca Lechera, Animales de la Granja'), the same multi hook title stacking Cocomelon uses. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • Bounce Patrol has about 34M subscribers but CreatorDB shows zero subscriber growth over the 365 days to Oct 2026 and only about one upload every few weeks, another big kids song channel living on its back catalogue. (creatordb.app, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Bounce Patrol's biggest 2026 uploads are collaborations with a famous puppet show ('Where is Elmo? (Hidey Tag)' 11.2M views, 'Ball Pit Party' 8M) while its own new songs (Rainbow Disco colours song, 30 Oct 2026) sit near 270K, so borrowed fame lifts old channels far more than fresh songs do. (vidanalyze.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Bounce Patrol's top video overall is a seek and find song ('Can You Find the Yummy Fruit?', 18.2M) and its hide and seek collab is its 2026 leader, which adds to the evidence that 'can you find it?' games are one of the strongest kids song formats. (vidanalyze.com, Nov 2026, medium)

(5.0M), GVO Kids (4.2M), Cosmic Kids Yoga (2.0M) and GoNoodle (1.7M) as the leaders, the field our dance songs compete in on classroom screens. (vloggingpro.com, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Bounce Patrol's Halloween compilation built on a marching song ('Halloween Ants Go Marching & More', 3 Oct 2026, 517K) outperformed its newer original upload, a reminder that seasonal versions of marching and counting songs are dependable. (vidanalyze.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • Toys and Colors' 2025 holiday plan was a 22 minute 'Elf Academy' special (premiered 21 Nov on its own kids streaming app, then Hulu on 27 Nov) plus a new holiday single and guest appearances by other creators, so a single longer holiday special is how big YouTube kids brands mark Christmas. (senalnews.com, Nov 2025, high)
  • That holiday single was released on a multi creator 'Holiday Hits Snow Day Soundtrack' distributed to Spotify, Amazon Music and Apple Music, so kids brands now push their Christmas songs to audio streaming as well as YouTube; a small Bro Bros Christmas EP fits the same pattern. (senalnews.com, Nov 2025, medium)
  • Hey Bear Sensory has about 3.99M subscribers and 3.36B views from only 95 videos (about 35M views per video) and still gets about 50M views a month in 2026 while uploading less than once a month, the most efficient catalogue of any kids channel we have checked. (nexlev.io, Nov 2026, high)
  • Hey Bear's top videos are all dancing fruit and vegetable parties with upbeat funky, disco or cumbia music (Smoothie Mix 383M, Fruit Salad Dance Party counting 1 to 10 334M, Funky Veggies Extended 279M, Disco Fruit Party 243M), so cheerful dancing food characters are a proven baby sensory hit.   • Hey Bear's recent uploads average about 29 minutes and its holiday videos also travel (a Halloween fruit dress up party 98M, a Christmas themed animation 89M), so one long seasonal sensory dance video can earn for years. (outlierkit.com, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Hey Bear's 'EXTENDED' and '10 mins' versions of its hits sit in its top 10 beside the originals, so extending a winning dance loop into a longer edition is a cheap way to add a strong long form video. (outlierkit.com, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Disney turned Gracie's Corner's YouTube songs into a Disney+ and Disney Jr. series of 120+ short sing along videos and 18 themed compilations (first drop of 68 shorts and 7 compilations on 15 Jun 2026, with global linear and streaming rights), so a clean library of short songs plus themed compilations is exactly what TV buyers want.   • Three of Dave and Ava's five most viewed videos are Halloween songs from October 2021 (top one about 11.8M), a sign that seasonal holiday songs keep coming back every year and become a channel's evergreen best sellers. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)

  • Mother Goose Club (9.89M subscribers, 12B views, 1,742 videos) gained zero subscribers in the 28 days to 31 Oct 2026 and only about 10K in its best 2026 month, while views drifted between about 19M and 25M a month, and vidIQ models it at about 27K USD a month: another veteran rhyme brand coasting on its catalogue.   • Mother Goose Club's newest upload, a 'BOO-tiful Songs' Halloween compilation posted 29 Oct 2026, had only about 9.9K views two days later, and its recent top videos are 'song plus more' compilations (ABC, Baby Shark, phonics) of 1.6M to 4.4M views, so a seasonal compilation from an old brand no longer gets a launch push and fresh characters are what the feed rewards. (vidiq.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • IvyBears, an animated kids franchise made with human led storytelling and AI supported production, launched on YouTube in May 2026 and by July reported 2.5M subscribers and 40M views, with its third music driven episode at 3M views in three days (company press release, unverified); a very high subscriber to view ratio like that usually signals paid promotion, so it is not a normal organic benchmark. (aap.com.au (PR Newswire), Jul 2026, low)

  • DRAGGLiNS, an AI animated series for 4 to 8 year olds made by one solo creator without a studio, launched on YouTube in April 2026 with four episodes, a new one every Saturday, a merch store and a US trademark filing for its name, a reminder that a solo AI assisted brand like Bro Bros should secure its name and characters early.   • Morphle TV (Moonbug's 3D magic pet cartoon) has 13.1M subscribers and 10.1B views from 2,263 videos but gained no subscribers in the 28 days to 23 Oct 2026 and drew only about 15M views a month (about 6.6K per video), its newest Shorts start at about 5K views, and all of its top 5 videos date from 2021 to 2023.   • Little Angel's main channel uploaded almost daily in late Sep and early Oct 2026, with most new videos at about 7K to 30K views, while its 'Brush Your Teeth Song' healthy habits video reached about 96K, so routine and habit songs still beat generic play stories even for a big brand.   • Legacy brands dominate kids demand worldwide (Sesame Street 55 years, Peppa Pig 20+, CoComelon's roots 15+) and a 10 year old action series, Miraculous, rose 98% to become the most in demand kids IP, so a new brand wins by staying consistent for years with the same characters rather than chasing one hit.   • Cartoon Clubhouse, a CoComelon compilation channel with 12.8M subscribers and 5.7B views, gained zero subscribers in the 28 days to 24 Oct 2026 and got about 26M views, while its newest upload had only 3.3K views, so even a giant brand's reupload channel now lives on its old library, not on new uploads.   • Kids Funny Songs (7.81M subscribers) still gained about 230K subscribers in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026, and its newest song about learning to ride a bike (13 Nov) drew 62.7K views in its first two and a half days, about 966 views an hour. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)

  • Zoobees, a nursery rhyme channel launched in March 2023, got all five of its biggest videos (Wheels on the Bus 23.6M, Finger Family 9.8M, Johny Johny 5M) within its first two months, but now sits at 179K subscribers and about 1M views a month, so the 2023 window when a new channel could ride classic rhyme remakes has closed.   • Zoobees posted a Christmas song (five little elves playing peekaboo with Santa) on 12 Nov 2026 and it drew only about 1.9K views in its first two and a half days, showing that small rhyme channels are already in the Christmas lane by mid November but a generic seasonal rhyme alone does not break through.   • A Zoobees safety remix, 'Wheels on the Ambulance', reached 4.3M views as one of its top five, a sign that putting a familiar tune on a rescue vehicle with a safety message travels better than plain rhyme covers; our own version should be an original tune about a helper vehicle, not a cover.   • HeyKids' Polish song channel (856K subscribers) drew only about 3.2M views and 1K subscribers in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026, and its 14 Nov upload had 881 views after two days, roughly a fourteenth of the home grown Polish leader Spiewajace Brzdace (about 46M a month). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)

  • Super Simple Songs (47.3M subscribers) grew its monthly views steadily from about 479M in June 2026 to 592M in October, while louder channels such as Bounce Patrol and Brazil's Cleo e Cuquin stalled or fell, a sign that calm, simple, clearly sung songs are gaining in 2026.
