  • YouTube's animation report (data to Oct 2025, published Apr 2026) splits online animation into three formats: memes (a short clip of an original character singing or dancing to a set audio), animatics (rough storyboard versions) and full episodes; the meme format is exactly what a Bro Bros Short of one brother dancing to our own hook is. (YouTube Culture and Trends report, Apr 2026, high)
  • Original meme characters spread worldwide through one sound: France's Le Poisson Steve drew over 95M views of titled videos in eight months of 2025 and Japan's Lemon Melon Cookie audio was reused in over 14,000 uploads, so a simple, instantly recognisable Bro Bros pose plus a short signature sound can be copied by fans across countries. (YouTube Culture and Trends report, Apr 2026, medium)
  • The same report says 63% of 14 to 24 fans watch YouTube made animated series weekly and 61% rate independent series as good as or better than studio ones, so viewers no longer expect studio polish; a consistent original world and characters matter more than budget. (YouTube Culture and Trends report, Apr 2026, medium)
  • In the same audit, challenge formats showed only a small, not significant view premium (about +21%) and product placement none, so a challenge label alone does not lift a kids video; the payoff inside the video matters more. (arXiv 2606.03173, Jun 2026, low)
  • The UK Department for Education's March 2026 guidance tells parents of children under five to choose 'slow paced, age appropriate' content, and commentators add that a kind moment (a hug, a sorry) needs a short pause on screen before the next cut so a child can take it in; Bro Bros should hold one to two seconds on every feelings beat. (bdnews24 citing The Guardian, Sep 2026, medium)
  • A Polish study of 80 children aged 3 to 5 (Ophthalmology Journal, Sep 2026, EEG, fNIRS and eye tracking) found that a calmer, low motion six minute animation produced longer fixations (about 2.3 vs 1.9 seconds), fewer eye jumps (12 vs 18) and better story recall (81% vs 72%) than a busier version, so our calm songs and story sections should keep camera and background motion low. (journals.viamedica.pl, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Mogu and Perol, a new preschool series from Zephyr Animation (France) with Taiwanese partners, turns a stop motion short into 39 seven minute 3DCG episodes set on a bright island, with gentle pacing rather than fast action; producers chose 3DCG to grow the world and reach more countries, the same route Bro Bros takes with Blender. (Animost industry news, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Its lead pair is a calm, slightly shy big character with a tiny, energetic, cuddly sidekick, a size and energy contrast that reads instantly to toddlers and suits Big Bro and Little Bro: keep Big Bro steady and kind, Little Bro bouncy and curious, in posture and movement as well as in the song. (Animost industry news, Nov 2026, low)
  • Meta's Reels guidance (repeated by two safe zone guides updated in Nov 2026) keeps the top 14% (about 270 px of a 1080x1920 frame), the bottom 35% (about 670 px) and 6% on each side (about 65 px) free of key content, because the account name sits on top and the caption, username and audio name sit at the bottom. (adsap.ai and supercarousels.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Google's vertical Shorts template leaves the right edge wider than the left (about 190 px right, 48 px left, 288 px top, 672 px bottom on 1080x1920) because the like, comment and share buttons run down the right side, so in Shorts the dancing Bros should sit just left of centre, not hard right. (supercarousels.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • TikTok's in feed template keeps 120 px clear on both sides, 240 px on top and about 660 px at the bottom, plus a 300 px icon column on the right from about mid height down, and the safe area shrinks as captions get longer, so short captions keep more of our dance visible. (supercarousels.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Combining the three platforms gives one shared safe box on a 1080x1920 frame of roughly x 120 to 890 and y 290 to 1250, so a single Blender vertical render with the Bros' faces, raised hands and any on screen words inside that box can be posted unchanged as Reel, Short and TikTok. (derived from adsap.ai and supercarousels.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Tall 19.5:9 to 20:9 phones can crop about 108 px from each side of a 9:16 video in some views, so wide arm moves in our dances should stay within the centre ~820 px of the frame. (socialmediasafezones.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • Because Instagram's caption, username and audio line fill the bottom third of a Reel, burned in singalong lyrics in our vertical cuts should sit just above that band (around 55 to 65% of the frame height), not at the very bottom where they would be hidden. (adsap.ai, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Kids distributors at a TV Kids Festival preschool panel said taste differs by market: China tends to prefer CG shows with very cute characters while the UK prefers quirkier ones, so Bro Bros dubs aimed at China and East Asia should lean on the cutest close ups and soft round designs. (worldscreen.com (TV Kids Festival), 2026, low)
  • A CAKE development executive said toddlers now pick shows themselves by tapping thumbnails on touch screens in a 'wall of content', so a distinctive, instantly recognisable look (our two Bros' fixed outfit colours and silhouettes in every thumbnail) matters more than ever, and demand for 3D preschool content is rising. (worldscreen.com (TV Kids Festival), 2026, medium)
  • Producers on the same panel advised building learning into a show's core with small 'breadcrumbs' that let kids work out the answer themselves, and planning game and platform extensions from the start (one preschool brand timed a Roblox game to its TV launch), which supports our riddle pauses and a future Bro Bros game tie in. (worldscreen.com (TV Kids Festival), 2026, low)
  • A small kids channel (Small World Play, about 10K subscribers) posted eight one minute Shorts on one day with generic keyword titles such as 'Kids Learn Kids Songs #Shorts' and 'Animal Names for Kids #Shorts', and each got only 10 to 40 views, while its one named toddler song long video from 2023 holds about 2.2M; vague keyword titles and batch dumping give the algorithm nothing to match, so every Bro Bros Short needs its own specific title naming the song and the moment. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In the ISB randomised test on made for kids educational videos, adding medium background motion raised view rates about 1.6% and high motion about 2.0% over a still background, a small gain, and the authors advise using motion in short bursts at moments when attention tends to drift rather than nonstop, so Bro Bros should add drifting snow or sparkles at the verse to chorus change and keep the background calm while a key word is taught. (ISB via PTI (DD News, DT Next), Oct and Nov 2026, high)
  • Small studio guidance on turning YouTube characters into toys (Whizzy Studios, Jun 2026) says a character must show its personality in one still image with no sound and look the same in 3D, plush, print and books, and that proportions and palette chosen now decide later licensing; Bro Bros should write a one page style guide (fixed outfits, colours, silhouettes, signature pose for each Bro) before the catalogue grows. (Whizzy Studios, Jun 2026, low)
  • A gentle animated 'little tree hut that saved their farm' village story from a cosy animation channel reached about 174M views in about ten weeks of 2026, showing calm, warm, soft lit 3D worlds with a small rescue story can rival loud content for all ages, a good model for a Bro Bros bedtime or story song video. (aifreeforever, Nov 2026, medium)
  • 1of10's analysis of over 300,000 viral 2025 YouTube videos found thumbnails with and without faces perform about the same overall, but thumbnails with several faces beat single face ones, which supports always showing both Bros (and a friend) together on Bro Bros thumbnails rather than one character alone. (Search Engine Journal, Dec 2025, medium)
  • Blender Studio's stylised lighting recipe uses a warm sun key from the front side (never from the camera), a cool purple blue fill to colour the shadows, a warm rim behind the head and a tiny dim light near the jaw to soften the face, so the Bros' faces stay the brightest, highest contrast area of every frame. (Blender Studio, 2021, high)
  • For speed Blender Studio fakes light shafts with an emissive noise textured cube instead of true volumetrics, casts leaf like shadows with holey 'blocker' planes that do not bounce light, and swaps the visible sky to a plain colour with a Light Path camera ray mix, cheap tricks that give our 3D sets depth without long render times. (Blender Studio, 2021, high)
  • Blender Studio's Cycles settings for a stylised family film (3 max bounces, indirect clamp 10, caustics off, 200 samples with OpenImageDenoise, Filmic) are a tested starting point for Bro Bros renders that keeps noise low while holding render time down for 14 songs a week. (Blender Studio, 2021, medium)
  • Generic 3D nursery rhyme channels that reuse the same stock family characters look almost identical to one another and lose audiences quickly once uploads stop, which supports keeping the Bro Bros brothers visually distinctive (own colours, outfits and faces) instead of the default rhyme channel look. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, low)
  • A self taught Japanese animator's music video in a fake 1960s and 70s TV look (film scratches, rubber hose motion) reached about 195M views and took only ten days to make, so one bold, consistent visual style can travel worldwide; a once a month 'old cartoon' style special could test this for Bro Bros, keeping our usual bright look for the main songs. (Cartoon Brew, Feb 2026, low)
  • When rigging a Bro Bros character through Meshy's API, leave out the old texture image option (deprecated 23 Oct 2026): if it is sent, that single image replaces the model's own textures and the PBR maps are lost, so the brothers would look flatter in Blender. (Meshy API changelog, Oct 2026, high)
  • Meshy retired its meshy-5 model on 10 Oct 2026 (requests now fail) and added a Deprecations page with retirement dates for every model, so any saved prompt or script that still names meshy-5 must switch to meshy-6-lite or newer before the next week's characters and props are made. (Meshy API changelog, Oct 2026, high)
  • Meshy's API changelog to 26 Oct 2026 and its web changelog for October list no animation, motion preset, retargeting or text to motion change, so the July 2026 text to motion limits (2 to 10 second clips) still set how long each Bro Bros dance move prompt can be. (Meshy changelogs, Oct 2026, medium)
  • YouTube's animation report names three formats that grow indie animated worlds: short meme clips cut from the show (watched weekly by 66% of young fans), rough animatics (57%) and full episodes (63%), so cutting tiny funny moments from each Bro Bros song into Shorts is the same ladder that grew the big indie series. (YouTube Culture and Trends, Apr 2026, medium)
  • A kids animation studio's May 2026 post claims calm, low stimulation animation is the fastest growing kids niche but cites no numbers, so we keep calm bedtime songs as one weekly slot rather than switching the whole channel to a slow style. (Whizzy Studios, May 2026, low)
  • Meshy's animate guide lets us stack several dance moves on one rigged Bro in an 'Added' list and export them all together ('All Added') as one FBX with a Mixamo style skeleton for Blender, which saves a re export for every move in a song. (Meshy docs, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Meshy's preset library and Text to Motion work only on humanoid characters, while four legged characters get just an automatic walk cycle, so animal friends that must dance (cats in the kitty band, farm animals) should be designed standing upright on two legs or hand animated in Blender. (Meshy docs, Nov 2026, medium)
  • An AIR case (Oct 2026) shows a 7M subscriber Arabic kids channel whose recommendations fell 91% even though click rate and watch time held; the team blamed sensational thumbnails (open mouths, distorted faces, exaggerated emotion), replaced them across the whole catalogue and then saw about 2.8x views, 5x recommendations and 6.6x revenue, so calm, friendly Bro Bros thumbnails protect reach on kids content. (AIR Media-Tech, Oct 2026, medium)
  • A 2026 Reels layout guide says that on a 1080 by 1920 Reel the top 150 px (header), the bottom 420 px (about 22%, caption, handle and audio line) and the right 100 px (like, comment, share buttons) get covered, so when we crop our 16:9 songs to vertical, the Bros' faces, the lyric line and the punchline must sit in the centre band, not at the bottom where our long video lyrics usually go. (TryMyPost, Jan 2026, medium)
  • In a Japanese online study (Oct 2026 preprint, 162 children aged 3 to 5, then 183 girls) boys mostly picked humanoid robots and girls mostly picked same gender dolls, and recolouring robots pink or lavender or giving them doll like faces shifted girls' choices only weakly (not significant), so surface colour changes do not win girls over; for a two brothers channel the better route to girl viewers is real girl friend characters with their own roles, jokes and solos. (Research Square preprint, Oct 2026, medium)

  • Many US kindergartens and lower schools run a pyjama 'train day' on the last school day before winter break: paper ticket necklaces, a conductor punching tickets, hot cocoa, cookie decorating and a small bell as a gift, so an original pyjama train song (no film names or characters) matches a real classroom ritual teachers search for in mid December. (Carolyn's Creative Classroom / school news, medium)
  • A Christmas Carol retelling ('Ebenezer') won the US box office on 13 to 15 Nov 2026 with about 19M USD and The Angry Birds Movie returned to select cinemas on 13 Nov for its 10th anniversary, so the giving and kindness story of Christmas and silly birds are both in family conversation this month (we use only our own characters). (Hollywood Reporter and Yahoo family guide, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A YouGov survey for the US games industry (3,557 people, Oct 2026) found 71% of kids want their parents to play video games with them more often, up from 58% in 2025, rising to 81% among 5 to 8 year olds, and 60% of kids see family gaming as a holiday tradition, so a December Bro Bros song where a parent joins the Bros as 'player two' in a dance game hits a real wish. (ESA and YouGov via PR Newswire, Nov 2026, high)
  • In the same survey 58% of US kids aged 5 to 17 plan to ask for a gaming gift this holiday (69% of boys, 46% of girls), led by accessories, in game currency and consoles, so game style visuals (level up banners, scoreboards, 'player 1, player 2') feel current in our December videos without naming any real game. (ESA and YouGov via PR Newswire, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A survey of 1,007 US parents (Jul 2026) found 29% say YouTube and TikTok creators drive their child's wish list and searches for bag charms jumped (Labubu charms +808%, Jellycat +790%, plush charms +349%), so a small, collectable Bro Bros charm or plush is the kind of merchandise kids now use to show what they love, for later. (K12.com, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Cambridge's Pre A1 Starters exam for 6 to 12 year olds, used by English schools in many non English countries, tests animals, body and face, clothes and colours, food and drink, school objects, family, sports and action verbs (kick, throw, jump), meals and times of day, place words (behind, next to, between, in front of, under) and question words, so songs built on exactly these word sets double as homework help for millions of learners and teachers. (Cambridge English, Pre A1 Starters classroom activities, high)
  • Oxford's Children's Word of the Year (Jan 2026), voted by almost 5,000 UK children aged 6 to 14, was 'peace' (35%), ahead of 'AI' (33%) and 'resilience' (21%); one in ten who chose peace mentioned war, so a calm 'peace and friends everywhere' song and a 'try again, never give up' song match words children picked themselves. (Oxford University Press, Jan 2026, high)
  • Indonesia marks Hari Ibu, its national Mother's Day, every 22 December; kindergartens hold card making, paper flower crafts, lunchbox decorating with visiting mums and short singing performances for mothers, so an original Bro Bros 'thank you, Mum' song with Indonesian subtitles posted around 20 Dec reaches a top kids market on a day the big Christmas channels ignore. (detik.com, Dec 2025, high)
  • Indonesian primary schools also run Hari Ibu talent shows where children dance and sing for their mothers, so a simple copy along mum dance (hugging arms, heart hands, a slow bow) gives kids a ready routine to perform at school, the kind of real world use that brings repeat views. (detik.com, Dec 2025, medium)
  • Computer Science Education Week 2026 runs 7 to 13 December (kickoff 5 Dec), the week schools run Hour of Code and Hour of AI lessons with no prep activities for any teacher, so a Bro Bros song where one brother is a robot and the other 'codes' him with simple commands (step forward, turn, jump, wave) is a classroom ready sequencing game that week. (csedweek.org, Nov 2026, high)
  • A study of Google searches from Jan to Aug 2026 ranks the most looked up Gen Alpha slang as 6 7, chud, rizz, cap and no cap, mog, bop, larping, aura, sigma and crash out; only 6 7, no cap, aura and crash out are harmless, while 'bop' has turned from 'a catchy song' into a sexual insult online, so Bro Bros titles and captions should stop calling our songs 'a bop'. (euronews.com, Sep 2026, high)
  • Japan's New Year's Eve TV ritual is NHK's Kohaku song contest, a red team against a white team taking turns to sing, a friendly sing off shape we can borrow for a year end Bro Bros special (Big Bro's team in red, Little Bro's in white, each singing a verse, everyone wins at the end), without using any real show branding. (nippon.com, 2026, medium)
  • On 31 Dec Japanese temples ring their bell 108 times and some let visitors ring it, while families eat long soba noodles for a long life near midnight, so a gentle 'ring the bell, slurp the noodles' New Year counting song fits Japanese families and teaches big number counting without any religious lesson. (nippon.com, 2026, medium)
  • In 2027 Bhogi and Lohri fall on Thu 14 Jan and Makar Sankranti and Thai Pongal on Fri 15 Jan in India, but on Thu 14 Jan (Lohri the evening of 13 Jan) for families in the US, Canada and the UK; Lohri has children going door to door singing for treats, so an Indian festival kite and bonfire song should be live by 10 Jan for both India and the diaspora. (hindutone.com, 2026, high)
  • Royal Mail asks UK children to post letters to Santa by Wednesday 9 Dec 2026 to get a reply, and Canada Post runs its own reply programme each December, so a 'Dear Santa' letter writing song should go out in the last week of November or first days of December while families are writing their letters. (hotukdeals.com and canadapost.ca, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Doozie's Doghouse folds shapes, colours, music, emotions and vocabulary into crafts and treat making, and pauses to ask viewers direct questions (for example which yellow fruit a shape looks like), with 'be yourself' and 'keep trying' messages carried by songs, a lesson mix our own songs can match with a pause and answer moment. (commonsensemedia.org, Nov 2026, high)
  • Sensory toys keep turning into learning hooks for preschoolers: counting by popping a fidget toy's bubbles was one of Blippi's best new Shorts in November 2026, a simple 'pop and count to five' chorus idea for our own song. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Friendship bracelet and bead making is back as a kids craft this Christmas through a new Rainbow Loom kit on the 2026 hot toy lists, a simple, global and brand free theme for a pattern and sharing song. (today.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Copernicus' seasonal forecast (Oct 2026) makes a milder than normal winter more likely across much of Europe, with Scandinavia the exception, and Spain's weather office expects above average temperatures from November to January, so most European children will again not see snow at Christmas. (rustourismnews.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Real Christmas snow in Europe is reliable only in Finnish and Swedish Lapland, inland northern Norway and high Alpine resorts; in the UK widespread snow on Christmas morning has happened only four times since 1960, so snow in our songs works as a magical wish for most viewers rather than their reality. (rustourismnews.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Kaspersky's 2026 kids report says children's interest in cartoons rose to about 53.5% of searches in that area, with searches most often leading to an animated story channel, an indie animated series and CoComelon's nursery rhymes, while video streaming searches overall fell from 18% to 8.7% as AI tools and learning rose. (kaspersky.com, May 2026, medium)
  • GivingTuesday falls on Tue 1 Dec 2026 and opens a global Generosity Week (1 to 5 Dec) whose suggested acts are simple and family friendly: share a skill, tidy up the neighbourhood, collect goods, check on a neighbour and share a meal, a ready made theme for a kindness song posted on 30 Nov or 1 Dec. (givingtuesday.org, Jul 2026, high)
  • The volunteering network behind Generosity Week links people in more than 110 countries, and GivingTuesday runs national campaigns in places such as the UK and Canada, so a 'helping hands' song in that week travels without being tied to any one religion or holiday. (givingtuesday.org and canadahelps.org, 2026, medium)
  • Ozzy Fox's most watched episode is 'The Floor Is Lava!' at over 7M views, ahead of its routine songs (brushing teeth, getting dressed, tidying), which again shows pretend danger movement games beat chores as hooks; a Bro Bros floor is lava jump dance with an original song is a safe bet. (laughingplace.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • In Japan, 31 December (Omisoka) is the one night children may stay up late: families clean the whole house before it, eat long 'year crossing' noodles for a long life, watch special TV and hear temple bells ring 108 times around midnight (about an hour), then visit a shrine in the first days of January; a Bro Bros New Year song for Japan can use the clean up, the long noodle stretch and a slow count of bell rings as its actions. (Web Japan Kids, 2023, medium)
  • The cheap toys children saw their favourite creators try on TikTok in the 2025 holidays were sensory and surprise toys: clicky keyboard key fidgets in 70 plus collectible designs, stretchy butter slime, slime kits with a hidden mini figure to unbox, and blind capsule miniature food and book sets; click, squish and 'what's inside?' moments are the toy sounds and reveals kids already love. (ABC7 Chicago, Dec 2025, medium)
  • A Bro Bros counting or colours song can borrow those toy mechanics without any brand: each verse opens a plain gift box or capsule to reveal a tiny toy (click, squish, pop sound effects) and kids guess what comes out before the reveal, matching the unboxing habit without showing real products. (ABC7 Chicago, Dec 2025, low)
  • Across seven big 2026 holiday gift guides (count of 14 Nov 2026) a giggle toy and a dinosaur vehicle appear on six, a customisable slime kit and a reusable hatching shark egg on five, and singing dolls on four, which shows the play patterns kids want this December: giggles, dinosaurs, squishy sensory play, surprise reveals and singing. (Playroom Chronicles, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Gift guides note singing dolls 'having a moment' even with kids who do not follow the band behind them, because children sing along and stage their own concerts at home, a good hook for an original Bro Bros 'Living Room Concert' song where kids grab a hairbrush microphone and perform with the brothers. (Playroom Chronicles, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A party horn and popper countdown song is a strong New Year's Eve topic for under 6s because toddlers can copy the 'toot' and 'pop' sounds and many families do an early 'kids midnight' at 7 or 8 pm; publish by 27 Dec so it is ready for search. (vidIQ (Hogi), Nov 2026, medium)
  • Hopscotch's 'Boundaries Song' (asking before hugs, tickles and teasing) spread through parents' TikToks and a share by a big preschool creator, showing social and emotional skill songs travel because parents actively pass them on; a cheerful 'ask first' song suits every culture. (Tinybeans, Aug 2023, medium)
  • A teacher's song about making dumplings, sung with her class and a toy dumpling showing the fillings, went viral because adults loved its warmth and every culture has its own dumpling; a 'let's cook together' song built around one shared world food (dumplings, flatbread, noodles) travels across countries. (Upworthy, May 2022 (updated Feb 2026), medium)
  • Google Trends reports that every December people worldwide search how to draw a snowman and how to make one, along with scarf and beanie, so a Bro Bros 'build and draw a snowman' song with on screen drawing steps meets a search that comes back each year. (Google for Creators, Dec 2021, medium)
  • Cookies are among the top December searches worldwide (sugar cookies first, then gingerbread, peanut butter, chocolate chip and shortbread), so a Bro Bros cookie baking song with mixing, rolling and decorating moves fits a reliable December interest without any brand or character. (Google for Creators, Dec 2021, medium)
  • December search spikes are very local (fried chicken in Japan, latkes in Israel, Yule log cake in France, panettone in Italy, tamales across the Americas), so a 'holiday treats around the world' counting song can travel to many markets in one video. (Google for Creators, Dec 2021, medium)
  • December 2026 has no big animated franchise opening in cinemas: Shrek 5 moved to June 2027 and the sixth Ice Age film (Ice Age: Boiling Point) now opens about 28 Jan to 4 Feb 2027, even though some box office calendars still show the old December dates; Jumanji 3 (11 Dec, live action) is the main family film of the month. (Variety, Cartoon Brew, HOYTS, Box Office Mojo, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Because the Ice Age sequel arrives around late January 2027, kids' interest in prehistoric ice animals (woolly mammoths, sabre tooth cats, sloths) should climb through January, so an original Bro Bros woolly mammoth stomp song is best released in mid January rather than during Christmas week. (HOYTS, Nov 2026 (our inference from the release date), low)
  • On the night of 5 Jan children in Spain, Mexico and much of Latin America leave their shoes out, often with grass or water for the Three Kings' camels, and Spanish towns hold a big parade with sweets thrown to kids, so a playful 'feed the camels, leave your shoes' song with a parade dance can be posted around 2 to 5 Jan for Spanish speaking families. (vozdeamerica.com and elsalvador.com, Jan, high)
  • Simple learning Shorts sit among 2026's most viewed: 'Easy Opposite Words for Kids' has about 965M views and a colourful balloon toy craft about 1.45B, so a Bro Bros opposites dance song (big and small, up and down, fast and slow) fits a proven Shorts topic. (AIFreeForever, Nov 2026, medium)
  • UK search interest in wooden toys rose about 194% ahead of Christmas 2026, the strongest UK toy trend in that analysis, so a warm 'wooden toy workshop' song where Bro Bros build a wooden train, blocks and a spinning top fits the season's calm, classic play mood. (Yorkshire Post, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Parent approved toy lists for Christmas 2026 feature 'heal the pet' play (an interactive plush pet with a little doctor kit, ages 5+), so pretend vet and caring songs, like our boo boo bandage idea but for a puppy or kitten, match what kids will unwrap this December. (Global News, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Pretend kitchens and food play (toy stovetops, pizza party and grocery sets, modelling dough kitchens) appear in both retail and editor toy lists for 2026, so cooking and shop play songs (like our veggie soup song, our best morning Reel on 18 Nov) stay a strong evergreen theme into the holidays. (ABC News and Global News, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Advent calendar videos on YouTube grew from about 14M views in September 2025 to 75M in October and 280M in November, over 850M for the season, so an advent countdown series must already be live by late November rather than starting on 1 December. (Google, 2026, high)
  • Which? (17 Nov 2026) says deliberately odd, 'ugly cute' plush toys are a 2026 Christmas trend driven by meme humour, so a lovable lumpy original Bro Bros side character (a wonky snowman plush that comes alive) fits the moment without copying any brand. (Which?, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Building bricks that light up and make sounds and keyboard style collectible 'click' keys are among 2026's novelty Christmas toys, which points to a 'click clack build it' Bro Bros song where each click on the beat adds a glowing block to a tower. (Which?, Nov 2026, medium)
  • ABC's 2026 toy roundup (21 Oct) says sensory play, collectibles and screen free activities are all rising, with screen free kids cameras in the list, so Bro Bros songs that send children off screen ('now you try, go find something red!') match what parents want this Christmas. (ABC News, Oct 2026, medium)
  • In Russia and much of Central Asia the biggest winter holiday for children is New Year's Eve, when Grandfather Frost and his granddaughter the Snow Maiden bring gifts under a decorated New Year tree, so a non religious 'New Year tree' song with a frosty grandpa style helper (our own invented character) travels there better than a Santa song. (ITMO and mel.fm, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Grandfather Frost's 'birthday' is celebrated in Russia on 18 November and marks the start of the New Year season there (in 2026 he even released a New Year playlist for it), so Russian speaking families are already in festive mode from mid November. (mel.fm, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In much of Latin America (Mexico, Colombia, Puerto Rico, Venezuela and others) Nochebuena on 24 December is the main family night, with a late dinner, music and gifts often opened at midnight, and in Mexico and Spain the Three Kings bring more gifts on 6 January, so Spanish dubs should time 'gift night' Shorts for the 24th and a second wave for early January. (History.com and CTV News, medium)
  • ABC's holiday 2026 trending toys list (21 Oct, drawn from Amazon's top 100, Walmart's trending page and social buzz) is full of toys that react: a plush that laughs and flaps when tickled, a tiger cub that grows and roars, a kitchen that sizzles, an egg that hatches a shark in water, so cause and effect play (do something, it reacts) is what kids want this Christmas; a Bro Bros song where each action makes a funny sound fits that wish. (abcnews.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Ugly cute plush with wonky teeth and slow rise squishies show up on both ABC's and BestReviews' 2026 toy picks, with ABC saying squishies sell out in some stores, so a silly, lovable 'ugly cute' original pet or a squish and stretch moment is a timely toy theme for December songs and Shorts. (abcnews.com and bestreviews.com, Sep to Oct 2026, medium)
  • Parent guides each December recommend short New Year's Eve countdown videos for kids (10 seconds to 10 minutes, from PBS Kids, Sesame Street, Netflix and simple YouTube channels) that families play at bedtime as a pretend midnight, and they favour ones with music, a cheerful non scary 'bang' ending and no year in the title so they can be replayed every year, so our New Year countdown song should leave the year out of the video and title. (The Everymom and Cool Mom Tech, Dec 2023, medium)
  • Cambridge Dictionary named 'human' its 2026 word of the year on 18 Nov 2026, presented as a push back against the spread of AI, so with parents wary of AI made 'slop' for kids, Bro Bros should keep showing a human made side (our own story ideas, behind the scenes of drawing a character, a real voice on intros) while still disclosing AI use where YouTube requires it. (Khaleej Times and NBC, Nov 2026, medium)
  • UAE schools on September start calendars (Ministry of Education, Dubai KHDA and Sharjah SPEA) close for winter from Monday 14 Dec 2026 and reopen Monday 4 Jan 2027, so Gulf families are home all day a full week before the US break (from 21 Dec); our Christmas and winter songs should already be live and in playlists by 12 Dec for the Middle East. (Gulf News, Nov 2026, high)
  • Indian school winter breaks are short and vary by state (last year mostly about 25 to 31 Dec, with Punjab, Rajasthan, Delhi and the south running into early January and Jammu and Kashmir closing for most of the winter), so for India, our biggest audience, the big home viewing week is Christmas to New Year rather than all of December. (Patrika, Dec 2025, medium)
Global markets · 443
  • Infobells (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu channels) and ChuChu TV lead Indian kids content; Hindi rhymes like Lakdi Ki Kathi have 4B views. (Social Blade / Wikipedia, high)
  • Regional-language versions (Hindi, Tamil, Telugu) each build channels with 30M+ subscribers. (Social Blade, high)
  • Food-themed content is a reliable way to reach Indian kids on Shorts. (Tubefilter, Feb 2026, medium)
  • The audience is global: the most-viewed kids channels reach every region by dubbing into many languages (Kids Diana Show alone runs Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, Portuguese, Indonesian, Japanese and German versions). (AIR Media-Tech, Nov 2026, high)
  • In an 11 language dubbing test on a kids channel, Spanish, Arabic, Indonesian and Portuguese pulled ahead first (then Japanese and Korean); dubbed audio tracks now bring over 30% of its views. (AIR Media-Tech case, Mar 2026, medium)
  • Dub new uploads at release and most of the back catalogue: viewers who liked one dubbed video left when nothing else was in their language; that channel dubbed about 70% of its catalogue. (AIR Media-Tech case, Mar 2026, medium)
  • Audio quality decides whether dubbing helps: on an Italian kids channel weak AI dubs cut average watch time to under 1 minute versus 5 to 6 minutes for professional dubs, and can pull the whole channel down. (AIR Media-Tech, Mar 2026, medium)
  • Cheap demand test before dubbing: translate titles and descriptions of the top 20% of videos into many languages and watch 60 days of views by country and audio language. (AIR Media-Tech, Mar 2026, medium)
  • Multi language audio on one channel amplifies signals the channel already has; separate language channels start from zero (Vania Mania's own Portuguese channel underperformed until it became an audio track). (AIR Media-Tech, Mar 2026, medium)
  • El Reino Infantil (Argentina) is the biggest Spanish kids network: 180 billion lifetime views, 9 billion in H1 2026, audience led by Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Peru and the US, built on named farm animal characters singing preschool songs. (Senal News, Sep 2026, high)
  • Dubbed tracks can hold kids longer than the original: average view duration was Spanish 8:24 vs English 6:26 (+31%), Portuguese 7:59, Indonesian 7:12, Arabic 6:46. (AIR case, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Indonesia is a kids viewing giant: in one Aug 2026 week five Indonesian, kid friendly family creators sat in the worldwide top 50 (Keizo and Friends #18 with 655M weekly views), even after an under 16 social media ban. (Tubefilter, Aug 2026, high)
  • YouTube music royalties per 1,000 streams (Content ID, Aug 2025 to Jul 2026): Canada 9.57 USD, Germany 7.34, UK 5.81, Australia 5.78, US 4.30, Mexico 1.39, Brazil 1.03, India 0.48, Philippines 0.31, Indonesia 0.15. (Dynamoi royalty data, Nov 2026, high)
  • The biggest kids audiences (India, Indonesia, Philippines, Brazil) pay the least per view, so the winning mix is English songs that travel to high value markets plus dubbed tracks for volume markets. (Dynamoi / AIR, 2026, medium)
  • In Inflr's Oct 2026 ranking of Brazilian channels that engage kids, the animated music brand Mundo Bita ranks 3rd (14.5M subs, 22.9B views) above creators with 50M subs, and Turma da Monica is 5th, so animated song brands compete equally with star creators in Brazil. (Meio e Mensagem, Oct 2026, high)
  • Seven of Brazil's top nine kids channels sell licensed products (toys, books, school supplies), and six of the top 30 build on Minecraft or Roblox; Brazilian kids reward recurring characters they can buy and play with. (Meio e Mensagem, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Brazilian kids pop is booming: MC Divertida has 8.6B plays and 18M subs with a strong preschool audience, and the duo Kysha e Mine passed 1.2B YouTube views and 130M TikTok likes in about a year; upbeat pop sung by kids works in Portuguese. (Billboard Brasil, Oct 2025, medium)
  • Brazil's leading kids music producers have lyrics and scripts checked by teams that include psychologists and keep a general audience rating, which they say builds trust with parents and teachers. (Billboard Brasil, Oct 2025, low)
  • El Reino Infantil runs 50 YouTube channels in 11 languages (Spanish, English, Italian, German, Portuguese, French, Turkish, Russian, Romanian, Korean, Hindi) for 240M subscribers, so a Latin brand now localises into Hindi and Korean too: songs with recurring characters travel both ways. (Senal News, Sep 2026, high)
  • El Reino Infantil releases about 40 pieces of content a week as a steady drip rather than full series drops, and it grew from a single focused niche (preschool music videos) into theatre, licensing and streaming. (PRODU, Jan 2025, medium)
  • El Reino Infantil's audience order is Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Peru, the US, Colombia, Ecuador, Chile, Spain and the Dominican Republic, so one Latin American Spanish track covers most of the Spanish speaking market including US Hispanic families. (Senal News, Sep 2026, high)
  • YouTube auto dubbing supports 27 languages, and its expressive speech mode (keeps pitch, intonation and energy) is live in 8: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Hindi and Indonesian; over 6M viewers a day watch 10+ minutes of dubbed video. (PPC Land, May 2026, high)
  • Auto dubbing skips videos with no speech or speech too fast to dub and videos with Content ID claims, so sung songs will not dub reliably; our spoken story intros and Didi stories can use it, while songs need re sung language versions. (PPC Land, May 2026, medium)
  • Auto dubbing is on by default for eligible channels; creators can review dubs before they publish, unpublish single languages, and opt into an experimental lip sync pilot. (PPC Land, May 2026, medium)
  • Abu Dhabi's culture chief said in Sep 2026 that about 80% of what Arab children watch is not in Arabic and suggested a 50 50 goal, so quality Arabic language kids songs face a large unmet demand across 430M Arabic speakers. (Khaleej Times, Sep 2026, medium)
  • With under 16 bans in Australia and soon the UK, kids in those markets will reach us mainly through YouTube Kids and parents' accounts on TV, which makes YouTube Kids eligibility and TV friendly quality even more important there. (PPC Land Jun 2026 with our strategy, medium)
  • In Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa kids songs are part of caregiving (soothing toddlers during chores, on journeys and at bedtime); communal homes make the calming songs the whole household's most played tracks, with global brands like CoComelon and Pinkfong dominating beside local language lullabies. (expression.africa, Dec 2025, medium)
  • LooLoo's Bahasa Indonesia kids channel (started Mar 2022) reached 3.08M subscribers with about 292M views in Oct 2026 and 140K new subscribers in 28 days; its top videos are an Indonesian Five Little Ducks (Lima bebek kecil, 102M), a vehicles song (55M) and Baby Shark with peekaboo (38M), so sung local versions of public domain rhymes win in Indonesia. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • CoComelon, Pinkfong, Little Angel, BabyBus and Lalafun each run a separate Bahasa Indonesia channel, a sign that the big kids brands see Indonesian as worth full re sung versions; an Indonesian audio track on our best songs is a priority test. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In Germany (Precisify, 750 kids aged 2 to 12, Jan 2026) YouTube reaches 51% of 2 to 5s, 67% of 6 to 9s and 80% of 10 to 12s, nearly half watch it on a TV, 62% watch their favourite creators mainly on YouTube rather than TikTok or Instagram, and Lego is the best loved toy brand. (advanced-television.com, Jan 2026, high)
  • In an AIR case (Q4 2025 against Q3) a localised kids network grew from 24M to 299M views; its Brazilian Portuguese channel jumped from 13.5M to 278.6M views (+1962%, 93% of the network), Spanish +703% and Hindi +216%, while the English channel fell 7%, so Portuguese Shorts can be a breakout market for a kids brand. (air.io, Apr 2026, medium)
  • Argentina's preschool clown cartoon El Payaso Plim Plim (#36, 377M weekly views) and Indonesia's Keizo and Friends (#20, 498M) sit in the world top 50 beside Mexico's El Tren Nam Nam, so Spanish and Indonesian language kids brands reach the same scale as English ones. (tubefilter.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • In Kaspersky's Saudi Arabia data YouTube took about 38% of children's Android app use, ahead of Roblox (14%) and TikTok (11%), and Baby Shark was the most searched song, so Gulf kids are reachable through YouTube songs first. (Eye of Riyadh (Kaspersky), 2023, medium)
  • In the same Kaspersky data K pop acts (BLACKPINK, BTS) and Latin pop led kids' music searches and music videos were about 16% of YouTube searches, close behind entertainment (19%) and cartoons (17%), so pop styled kids dance songs travel to the Gulf. (Eye of Riyadh (Kaspersky), 2023, medium)
  • Baby Shark had ranked No. 1 in global YouTube views for 71 consecutive months by Oct 2026, and Pinkfong is opening a Baby Shark Christmas cinema special in Korea on 5 Dec, proof one signature song can carry a brand across every market for years. (Sports Khan, Oct 2026, high)
  • Blippi reaches Spanish speaking families with English Spanish (Espanglish) remixes made with Mexico's Los Meniques de la Casa (10M+ subscribers); their first one passed 3M views, so a bilingual remix of a Bro Bros hit with alternating English and Spanish lines is a low cost bridge to US Hispanic and Mexican viewers. (Moonbug, Jan 2026, medium)
  • YouTube Japan's Silver Week kids playlist (20 to 27 Sep 2026) featured mainly domestic brands: a 41 song Bon Bon Academy dance and exercise medley for ages 2 to 4, Anpanman, Shimajiro, Sanrio and Tamagotchi, with Bluey Japan and Pokemon Kids TV the only global names, so Japan rewards local characters and long dance medleys and would need Japanese audio. (YouTube Japan blog, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Japan's education ministry survey (Apr to May 2026) found 21.7% of sixth graders use social media or online video four or more hours each weekday, up 50% in two years, and almost every child now has a device. (Nippon.com, Aug 2026, medium)
  • In France live TV is still the main way 7 to 14 year olds watch kids shows (M6 Publicite and Gulli, Dec 2024) while 4 to 6 year olds are moving to subscription streaming, so France is a TV first kids market where a French audio track matters less than Spanish or Portuguese. (Ozap, Dec 2024, low)
  • In Indonesia's top 10 YouTube channels (15 Aug 2026) two are foreign kids brands dubbed into Bahasa: BabyBus Indonesian (28.7M subs, about 10M views a month) and Tayo Bahasa Indonesia (26.8M, about 34M views a month and 1.1M average per video), proof that dubbed animation can reach the very top of a local market. (Databoks (noxInfluencer), Aug 2026, high)
  • BabaSharo TV, a kids song channel started in 2020 by one creator in Doha, reports 1.8B views and over 1,000 original animated songs dubbed into English, Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese and Hindi, plus a kids app and releases on Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music and Anghami (the Arab world's main music app). (Observer Reporter (press release), Jul 2025, medium)
  • Anghami is the leading music streaming service in the Arab world, so releasing Bro Bros songs with Arabic audio through a distributor that delivers to Anghami adds a Gulf and North Africa audio channel beside YouTube. (Observer Reporter (press release), Jul 2025, low)
  • AIR's dubbing review (Sep 2026) found AI only voice tracks held viewers 4 to 10 times less than the same videos with professionally voiced tracks; one Italian kids channel kept 5 to 6 minutes on pro dubs but only 54 seconds on its English AI track. (air.io, Sep 2026, high)
  • Across several multi language tests the first extra languages to pull ahead were Spanish, Arabic, Indonesian and Portuguese, followed by Japanese and Korean; French and Italian AI tracks lagged well behind English. (air.io, Sep 2026, medium)
  • A kids channel in Indonesian (HZD, 165M views) found its Spanish track held viewers slightly longer than the original (2:11 against 2:00), showing that a well made second language audio can match the home language. (air.io, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Inflr's ranking of the 20 Brazilian channels that most engage kids (Oct 2026, HypeAuditor data) mixes creator families and gamers (six of the top 30 are Minecraft or Roblox based) with animated music brands Mundo Bita, Turma da Monica, Bolofofos and 3Palavrinhas; foreign dubbed channels were excluded from the list. (meioemensagem.com.br, Oct 2026, high)
  • Brazil's most played kids songs include farm animals (Fazendinha), under the sea (Fundo do Mar), a little yellow chick (Pintinho Amarelinho) and a freeze like statue game (Estatua), alongside CoComelon's Wheels on the Bus: animals and stop and go games are what Brazilian kids replay. (billboard.com.br, Oct 2024, medium)
  • Spotify Wrapped 2025 in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa was dominated by children's picks (CoComelon, Pinkfong, Super Simple Songs, soft classics such as You Are My Sunshine) played on smart speakers and family TVs, so English language kids songs already reach anglophone African homes with no dubbing. (newstrends.co.ke, Dec 2025, medium)
  • El Reino Infantil, the Argentine network behind La Granja de Zenon, runs 50+ YouTube channels in 11 languages with over 240M subscribers and 180B views, gained 8.8B views in Jan to May 2026, and Mexico is its biggest market (39.1M subscribers, 32.4B views), making Mexico the core Spanish kids audience. (publimetro.com.mx / mercado.com.ar, Sep 2026, high)
  • Argentina's El Payaso Plim Plim had about 1.07B views in one month (May 2026, up 20.7% on April) in the YouTube Rating chart, more views per person in Argentina than MrBeast gets in the US; its creator credits gentle stories with positive values that connect with families. (senalnews.com, Jul 2026, medium)
  • In Akatsuki's survey of parents in 10 Indian metros, YouTube (76%) leads kids animation viewing ahead of Netflix (57%) and TV (26%), with TV the main daily screen (60%) ahead of phones (49%); parents choose shows mainly for entertainment (64%) over the child's happiness (45%) and learning (35%). (indiantelevision.com, 2025, medium)
  • The same urban Indian parents most prefer English language animation, with Tamil, Telugu and Bangla the top regional language choices, and they rank local characters and storylines lowest (11%), so our English songs already suit metro Indian families and South Indian dubs may matter more than expected. (indiantelevision.com, 2025, medium)
  • Indian kids studio PunToon (early 2026) says parents increasingly pick culturally rooted Indian stories, and that India's kids creators are moving away from YouTube only income after COPPA ad cuts, toward game apps, school holiday mall events and brand partners (Duolingo, FirstCry), so festival songs plus off platform partners suit the Indian market. (indiantelevision.com, 2026, medium)
  • Tunes Kids, a UAE based Arabic kids song channel (2.84M subs, 1.94B views), gains about 16 to 35M views and 20K subscribers a month in 2026; its most viewed videos are upbeat 'remix' versions of family songs (top one 125M), and its newest upload is a funny family baby story song. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • Moonbug Kids Arabic, a dubbed channel mixing Morphle, Blippi and other brands (909K subs), fell from about 4.2M views in Jun 2026 to about 2M in Oct with only 1 to 7K new subscribers a month, so a mixed brand dubbed channel loses to song channels that feel local; for Arabic we should add re sung audio tracks to our own channel rather than open a generic dubbed one. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • YouTube's largest audiences in 2026 are India (518M users), the US (259M), Indonesia (151M), Brazil (149M), Mexico (86M), Japan (81M), Germany (66M), Vietnam (63M), the Philippines (61M) and Turkey (59M). (globalmediainsight.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • English, Hindi, Indonesian, Portuguese and Spanish together cover the five biggest YouTube countries, matching our dubbing order; Vietnamese and Turkish are the next large markets with no plan yet, and both already appear among strong second language tracks in kids dubbing tests. (globalmediainsight.com / air.io, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Indonesia (151M users) and the Philippines (61M) together are a YouTube audience larger than the US, and both have big young populations, which is why kids brands run Bahasa channels and why English songs travel well in the Philippines. (globalmediainsight.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Vlad and Niki runs separate full channels in Vietnamese (46.6M subs), Hindi (39.4M), Indonesian (39.9M) and Spanish (32.5M) next to the 151M English one, each among the top 100 YouTube channels, proof that a localised copy of the same characters can become a giant on its own. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • BabyBus's Vietnamese channel (BabyBus Nhac thieu nhi) has about 9.75M subscribers and 11B views, and still adds about 70 to 115M views a month (92M in the 28 days to 7 Nov 2026) from roughly 20 uploads a month, proof that a dubbed foreign 3D song brand can own Vietnam's kids songs. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • In Playboard's daily ranking of Vietnam's education channels (Nov 2026) BabyBus is the only kids song channel in the top 20, beside adult lesson and history channels, so a Vietnamese dub of Bro Bros would face few direct local competitors in that category. (playboard.co, Nov 2026, low)
  • BabyBus's Vietnamese subscriber gains slowed from about 40 to 80K a month in 2024 and 2025 to 20 to 30K in late 2026 while monthly views held steady, showing kids song views come from repeat viewing and recommendations, not new subscribers, in this market too. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Three of Turkey's ten most viewed YouTube channels (Feb 2026) are for kids: Sevimli Dostlar (16.9B views, No. 2), Oyuncak Oynuyorum toy play (13.2B, No. 3) and Masha and the Bear's Turkish dub (9.7B, No. 7), so Turkish is a big kids market where a dubbed foreign 3D brand can reach the top ten. (tamindir.com (BoomSocial), Feb 2026, high)
  • Turkish 3D kids song brand Kukuli has 6.05M subscribers and 7.3B views, earning about 56 to 97M views a month in 2026; its top songs are the 'Bakkal Amca' (corner shop uncle) series (258M and 114M), so everyday neighbourhood characters and errands are a strong song theme in Turkey. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • Kids Tv Bangla (Bengali nursery rhymes) has 3.69M subscribers and 2.1B views and still gains about 55M views a month (28 days to 15 Nov 2026) from rhyme remixes and long collections, showing Bengali is a big kids market that a Hindi or English song channel can enter with a Bangla dub. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • Google Pakistan reported (Dec 2025) that about 60% of watch time on Pakistani YouTube content comes from viewers outside Pakistan and over 1,000 Pakistani channels passed 1M subscribers, so an Urdu version of our Hindi Didi stories (the spoken languages are close) could reach South Asian families in the Gulf, UK and North America. (dawn.com, Dec 2025, medium)
  • Small South Asian learning channels with ABC and alphabet videos (a Pakistani one with 145K subscribers got only about 2,200 views in 28 days) show subscribers alone do not keep views; Kids Tv Bangla's long rhyme compilations, not short lessons, carry its steady monthly views. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • Little Baby Bum's 'Multi Language Songs' channel, mixing several languages, has only 234K subscribers and about 2.7M views a month against 100M+ for the English channel, so mixing languages on one channel works poorly; dub into separate language channels or audio tracks instead. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A 2026 RPM guide (unsourced) puts the Gulf far above the rest of the Arabic speaking region: Qatar about 5 to 12 USD per 1,000 views, UAE 4 to 10, Saudi Arabia and Kuwait 3 to 8, against Egypt 1 to 2 and Turkey 1 to 4, so an Arabic dub is worth most where Gulf families watch. (fluxnote.io, Mar 2026, low)
  • UAE studio TwelveP licenses its preschool shows to YouTube networks by region (Rockoons musical series to El Reino Infantil in English, Spanish and Portuguese and to Yoboho in India; Claymotions to Epic Story World in English, Arabic, Chinese, Spanish and Portuguese), showing that licensing a song library to regional YouTube hubs is a second route to global reach besides own dubbing. (thedrop / dropmedia.co.uk, May 2026, medium)
  • Thailand's biggest family and kids YouTube channels in Nov 2026 include Vlad and Niki's Thai channel (14.2M subscribers, 5.8B views) and local J Jai Pan (13.5M, 14.8B) and YimYam TV (10.5M), so Thai is a big, proven dub market that our tree had not covered. (hypeauditor.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Russian kids song channel TaDaBoom (Masha and the Bear songs, 6.24M subscribers) gets about 82.5M views a month but vidIQ models only about 7,800 USD a month from ads, roughly 0.1 USD per 1,000 views, because ad sales in Russia are restricted, so a Russian dub brings reach, not income. (vidiq.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • TaDaBoom's second biggest recent hit is a premiere lullaby (18.3M views since Jan 2025) and it now streams English lessons with its characters, showing that bedtime songs and English learning travel into non English markets. (vidiq.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Akili and Me, Ubongo's East African preschool channel (1.24M subscribers, about 7.7M views a month), has a toilet training health song as its all time top video (14.3M), ahead of alphabet songs, so potty and hygiene songs are among the most searched kids topics in emerging markets too. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Mexico's El Tren Nam Nam rocketed to No. 2 among the world's most viewed channels (about 1.08B views in the week of 25 Oct 2026, +96%) and two weeks later fell to No. 39 (about 360M, -52%), so Spanish language kids content can produce the biggest weekly spikes on YouTube, but they fade fast without a steady catalogue. (Tubefilter, Oct and Nov 2026, high)
  • Kids and family channels in the worldwide weekly top 50 (week of 8 Nov 2026) came from Australia (Cadel and Mia, No. 3, about 890M), Germany (Jasmin and James, No. 11, about 623M), Indonesia (Keizo and Friends, No. 20, about 498M) and Mexico, so family Shorts audiences are spread across every region, not centred on the US. (Tubefilter, Nov 2026, high)
  • VocaVoca (US nursery songs) was No. 11 worldwide with about 675M weekly views in late October but missing from the top 50 by the week of 8 Nov, showing how fast weekly views swing for song channels and why we judge our results on monthly, not weekly, trends. (Tubefilter, Oct and Nov 2026, medium)
  • Nigeria's House of Ajebo runs Jeni and Keni, an animated YouTube series about two siblings for ages 1 to 6 with Afrobeat style songs that teach kindness and share African culture (relaunched 2025); sibling led song brands are being built in Africa too, and an Afrobeat flavoured Bro Bros song would speak to West Africa and its diaspora. (BusinessDay Nigeria, Aug 2025, medium)
  • Heidi dan Zidane's Spanish dubbed audience came mostly from Mexico (24.2% of views) and Argentina (11.1%), with Spain watching longest (5:08 average), yet the US gave only 5.3% of views but 43.2% of revenue: volume comes from Latin America, money from US viewers. (AIR Media-Tech, Mar 2026, medium)
  • AIR's Sep 2026 data found AI only dubbed tracks held viewers 4 to 10 times less than pro dubbed tracks on the same videos, with the biggest gaps on kids channels (an Italian kids channel kept 5 to 6 minutes on pro tracks against 54 seconds on its English AI track). (AIR, Sep 2026, medium)
  • On kids channels the voice is part of the product, and an AI voice that sounds too adult, flat or emotionally off can hurt retention and even draw misleading content flags, so Bro Bros dubs should be sung by real or carefully cast child like voices, not YouTube's default auto dub. (AIR, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Good human dubs can match or beat the original: a kids channel with an Indonesian original (165M views) held 2:11 on its pro Spanish track against 2:00 on the original, and Turkish, Italian and German tracks stayed close. (AIR, Sep 2026, medium)
  • On one kids channel with the same videos dubbed three ways, Arabic brought the most views (3.4M) but German, with only 134K views, had the highest share of returning viewers (about 52%) and the longest watch time, so small markets can be the most loyal. (AIR, Apr 2026, medium)
  • AIR judges a new dubbed language by the share of its views that come from casual plus regular (returning) viewers: under 20% after four months is a problem, 20 to 40% is building, over 40% is working and over 60% is strong, and the first 90 days are too early to judge. (AIR, Apr 2026, medium)
  • CIMM's July 2026 report says US young children's video time is now about 35% streaming, 32% YouTube and 16% short form (TikTok, Shorts), with linear TV down to about 6% from 80 to 90% in 2005, and children make up nearly a quarter of all YouTube viewing. (CIMM, Jul 2026, high)
  • US children aged 0 to 8 now average about 2 hours 27 minutes of screen time a day (up from 1 hour 44 in 2005), with mobile the main device, while YouTube Analytics only shows demographics for viewers 13 and over, so our own analytics can never show the true age of our audience. (CIMM, Jul 2026, high)
  • Kenya's Akili TV added read along captions to existing cartoons in a 'Read Along Hour' (Swahili and French pilots) and child viewing rose about 15% while adult co viewing rose about 39%, so big on screen karaoke style lyrics in Bro Bros songs can draw parents in and help reading. (Pulse, Apr 2026, medium)
  • At least 14 kids and family channels sit in France's top 100 YouTube channels by subscribers (11 Nov 2026), led by Masha et Michka (12.2M), Kidi Fun (11.9M), Titounis comptines (7.7M), Kidibli (7.5M) and Little Angel's French channel (5.7M), so French is a strong second language market for nursery songs. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • International song brands run separate French channels that rank high in France (Little Angel French 5.7M, HeyKids French 4.9M and its English channel also in France's top 100 at 4.8M), showing French parents subscribe to both local language and English kids song channels. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Kaboochi's French channel (197K subscribers, 618 videos) earned only about 135K views in the 28 days to 29 Oct 2026 after its uploads stopped in September, with Shorts as its best videos, so a dubbed language channel fades fast without steady uploads; audio tracks on the main channel are safer for a small team. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Spotify Wrapped 2025 coverage from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa says children now shape whole household listening there, with Cocomelon nursery rhymes, Baby Shark and gentle singalongs like You Are My Sunshine topping family recaps, used for mornings, car rides and bedtime and spread through siblings and cousins sharing one phone. (NewsTrends Kenya, Dec 2025, low)
  • In an AIR test where one kids channel ran the same videos, thumbnails and schedule in Arabic, French and German (16 Feb to 24 Mar 2026), Arabic drew by far the most views (3.4M in five weeks against 745K French and 134K German), confirming Arabic as a high volume first dub for kids songs. (AIR Media-Tech, Apr 2026, medium)
  • In the same test German viewers were the most loyal (about 52% returning, 10.6% regular, new viewers averaging 4:30 against 2:49 for Arabic), so smaller rich markets can repay a dub through watch time and higher ad rates even with fewer views. (AIR Media-Tech, Apr 2026, medium)
  • AIR suggests judging each dubbed audio track by returning viewers, not views: in YouTube Analytics' 'Audience by watch behaviour' filtered by audio track, casual plus regular viewers above 40% means the language is working, 20 to 40% is building and below 20% after four months needs fixing; this share should climb about 3 to 5 points a month in the first year. (AIR Media-Tech, Apr 2026, medium)
  • On one entertainment channel the Spanish dubbed track's viewers watched about two minutes longer per view than the English original (8:55 against 6:59), which AIR puts down to less competition in Spanish. (AIR Media-Tech, Apr 2026, low)
  • Audiences in Russia, Germany, Italy, Spain, Mexico, Brazil and France prefer dubbing, while adults in China, South Korea, India and Japan prefer subtitles; young children everywhere need dubbing because they cannot read subtitles fast enough, so for kids songs only re sung audio tracks count as localisation. (Kapwing compilation (Morning Consult), Apr 2026, medium)
  • Only about 13% of creators in AIR's 3,000 channel network have paid for professional dubbing and 36% have tried AI dubbing, yet dubbed tracks averaged about 45% more views and YouTube says creators with dubbed tracks get over 25% of watch time from non primary languages, so early dubbing is still a gap Bro Bros can use. (Kapwing compilation, Apr 2026, medium)
  • One small counter example: a creator's dedicated Spanish channel got 3,897 views in 90 days against just 32 for the same video's Spanish track on his main English channel, so a separate language channel may beat audio tracks when the main channel has little audience in that language. (Kapwing, Apr 2026, low)
  • In Latin America children aged 3 to 5 use only YouTube for screen content, subscription apps appear around age 6 and games around 9 to 12, so a Spanish and Portuguese dub of our preschool songs reaches the youngest kids on the one screen they all share. (marketing4ecommerce (Kidscorp study), Jul 2026, high)
  • Kidscorp finds YouTube is the only screen with similar reach across high, middle and low income homes in Latin America, reaching about 68% of under 18s in Mexico and Chile versus under 30% for TV, and above 70% digital adoption in Brazil and Argentina. (marketing4ecommerce (Kidscorp study), Jul 2026, high)
  • Across 16 MENA markets kids animation is 40.6% of supply but only 30.2% of demand, while US and Japanese titles drive over 85% of animation demand, so a new kids channel there competes in a crowded field and must stand out with quality and Arabic audio. (Parrot Analytics, 2026 Q1, medium)
  • Children aged 0 to 14 are about a quarter of MENA's population, and parents stay closely involved in judging whether content fits family values, so modest outfits, kind behaviour and no romance matter for Arabic speaking families. (Campaign Middle East, Jun 2026, medium)
  • Pan Arab kids hits mix dialects (the Mansour reboot blends Emirati, Saudi, Iraqi, Egyptian and other voices) and the original Mansour drew most of its 2.5B views from outside the UAE, notably Iraq and Egypt, so an Arabic dub should use simple, widely understood Arabic rather than one local dialect. (Kidscreen, 2023, medium)
  • Sanrio launched 'Sanrio Kids - Cartoons & Kids Songs' on YouTube on 15 Sep 2026 as a global preschool channel whose 3D videos carry Japanese and English audio switchable within the same video, the same multi audio track route open to Bro Bros. (Sanrio, Sep 2026, high)
  • Sanrio Kids splits its channel into three series (sing along music, movement and play including calming down, and everyday story episodes), each about two minutes, a clean playlist structure for a song brand entering Japan and Asia. (Sanrio, Sep 2026, medium)
  • In a Philippine survey of 1,000 parents (29 Oct to 2 Nov 2026), 34% named child specific apps such as YouTube Kids as a safety measure and 97% wanted evidence based rules for children's social media, so Filipino families value clearly kid safe channels. (Daily Tribune Philippines, Nov 2026, medium)
  • The same survey found 60% of Filipino parents say their children use social apps for rest and relaxation and 70% for learning, which favours calm songs and learning songs in Filipino focused playlists. (Daily Tribune Philippines, Nov 2026, low)
  • Vietnam's first music video to pass 1B YouTube views (June 2024) is the kids song 'Mot con vit' about a mother duck and five yellow ducklings, sung by a three year old, from a channel with only about 40 short songs under five minutes; other kids songs hold several of Vietnam's next biggest totals (crocodile song 665M), so a simple animal family song can top a whole country's music charts. (Tuoi Tre, Jun 2024, high)
  • Vietnamese parents use the duck song as a mealtime helper to get children to eat, the same 'song for a daily routine' role our habit songs aim for, so mealtime songs are a strong fit for Vietnam and other Southeast Asian homes. (Tuoi Tre, Jun 2024, medium)
  • POPS Kids, Vietnam's largest kids channel, has about 20.3M subscribers and 15B views from 4,687 videos (Oct 2026), mixing its own shows with licensed Doraemon and Pokemon cartoons, and drew about 3.5M views on a single day; Social Blade puts its income anywhere from about 94K to 7.2M USD a year, showing how wide and unreliable such estimates are. (CafeF, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Nigerian YouTube watch time grew over 50% in a year and views for one network's Nigerian creators rose from 70M to over 400M, yet Nigerian ads pay only about 0.5 to 2.5 USD per 1,000 views against up to 15 USD in the US, so for Bro Bros, Nigeria and other English speaking African homes are reach and word of mouth markets, not revenue markets. (TechCabal, Oct 2025, medium)
  • Germany's 'Kinderlieder zum Mitsingen und Bewegen' channel has 3.47M subscribers, about 33 to 43M views a month from 1,453 videos and vidIQ models about 14K USD a month; it wraps new titles in 'NEU * ... * NEU', its newest song (13 Nov 2026) teaches tying a bow, and its top videos are remixes of singing games such as 'who stole the cookie from the jar' (24.4M) and a dog's lost bone song (22.9M). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Japan's most viewed kids songs on YouTube are franchise themes (a monster catching game theme at 105M), Japanese language versions of Disney songs and songs from the public TV show 'Okaasan to Issho' (a clock song, a bean hero song), so Japanese children mostly watch Japanese language content and an English Bro Bros song has little pull there until it is re sung in Japanese. (Soundcharts, Nov 2026, medium)
  • German and Japanese hits both lean on practical everyday skills and objects (tying a bow, telling the time), which suggests life skill songs translate across cultures better than culture specific holidays. (vidIQ and Soundcharts, Nov 2026, low)
  • Pakistan's top YouTube channels in Nov 2026 are led by family and Shorts creators: 16 family tagged channels sit in the top 90, including Ak Ultra (19M subscribers, 22.3B views), Anaya Eshaal Family (16.9M) and Minsa Saim Omer (13.4M, 20.9B views), so Pakistani children mostly watch family creators, and an animated English song channel has to win them through Shorts. (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Urdu story channel Geo Kahani has about 7M subscribers and 4.5B views in Pakistan's top 60, which suggests narrated animated stories in Urdu are a large format there, similar to the Hindi story videos we already make. (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026, low)
  • Pakistani learning channel TinyTaleem still has 145K subscribers but drew only about 2,500 views in October 2026 from 453 videos (top videos are English ABC and animal name lessons and an Urdu alphabet poem), a reminder that a subscriber count means little once a channel stops posting fresh, recommendable videos. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In Bangladesh's top 100 YouTube channels (vidIQ, 12 Nov 2026) there is no nursery rhyme or kids music channel; children's attention goes to craft and drawing giants (Tonni art and craft 19.5M subscribers, Farjana Drawing Academy 15.6M, Mukta Art and Craft 8.2M) and Maasranga Kids (5.3M, 4.9B views), so a Bengali dub of our songs would face little direct competition. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Draw along videos are among the biggest family formats in Bangladesh (three drawing or craft channels in the top 60), which supports a 'draw Little Bro step by step' Short with our song playing as a cheap extra format for South Asian viewers. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, low)
  • Poland's most subscribed YouTube channels (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026) include dubbed foreign kids brands (WB Kids 7.1M, Cartoonito Polska 3.6M, Masha 2.8M, Peppa Pig and Disney Junior 1.8M each) beside local rhyme channel Singing Toddlers (2.6M) and family creator Hejka tu Lenka (1.8M), so Polish families accept dubbed animation readily. (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026, medium)
  • HeyKids' Polish song channel (856K subscribers, 630M views) gets a steady 3.5 to 5M views a month in 2026 with almost no subscriber growth; its top songs are about a cheeky little boy character (19.3M), construction machines (6.9M) and a red car (5.7M), the same vehicle and mischief themes that win elsewhere. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Jason Vlogs runs 10 localised channels and says they did not cannibalise the main channel but brought in new viewers, another data point that separate language channels add audience rather than split it. (AIR, Feb 2026, medium)
  • Thailand's top kids and family YouTube channels (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026) are mostly family vlogs and comedy: Vlad and Niki Thai 14.2M subscribers, J Jai Pan 13.5M, a slime toy channel 11.9M and YimYam TV 10.5M, while animal and learning song channels 'kids song' (7.7M) and KidsMeSong (7.4M) hold the music slots, so a Thai market favours playful sibling characters plus animal songs. (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Moonbug Kids Arabic (dubbed Morphle and Blippi) has 909K subscribers and 369M lifetime views but only about 2M views a month in Oct 2026 and about 3.6K views on a new upload after three days, so a dubbed foreign brand channel grows slowly in Arabic; local feeling songs and titles matter more than the brand. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Moonbug Kids Arabic's all time hits are emotional story moments ('Morphing Family' 41M, 'Morphle is Alone and Cries' 25M) rather than songs, which hints Arabic speaking families respond to family and feelings stories; an Arabic Bro Bros pilot could start with a brothers and family feelings song. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, low)
  • Egypt's most subscribed YouTube channel (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026) is Kids Diana's Arabic channel 'Diana and Roma ARA' (30.9M), followed by family channels Osratouna TV (21.8M) and Marah TV (14.2M) and about ten Egyptian family comedy channels with 7 to 12M each, so Arabic family audiences favour dubbed sibling characters and family sketches over plain rhymes. (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In Ukraine the second most watched kids YouTube channel is a local Ukrainian language song channel by Lviv authors (about 614M views), about half of the top 20 kids channels are in Ukrainian and the English 3D song brand Sandy the Sticker ranks No. 9 (74M), so a Ukrainian dub of our songs would meet strong demand for local language kids music. (dev.ua (Detector Media), Aug 2025, medium)
  • English language animated kids channels still reach the top 10 in non English markets like Ukraine (two of the top 10: an Ali Baba channel and Sandy the Sticker) because music and movement carry without words, supporting our plan to grow first in English and add dubs where local demand is proven. (dev.ua (Detector Media), Aug 2025, medium)
  • Brazil's ICT Kids Online 2025 survey (2,370 children aged 9 to 17, published May 2026) found 92% are internet users (about 24M children) and 60% of them go online through a television every day, so in Brazil the living room TV is a daily screen for kids, which rewards long form compilations with a Portuguese audio track. (Cetic.br / NIC.br, May 2026, high)
  • In the same Brazilian survey phone ownership among 9 to 10 year olds fell to 55% (from 67% in 2024) and social media use in that age group dropped from 48% in 2021 to 33% in 2025, a sign that younger Brazilian children are moving toward shared family screens and supervised viewing rather than their own phones. (Cetic.br / NIC.br, May 2026, high)
  • 28% of Brazilian 9 to 17 year olds first went online by age 6, and 80% watch influencer videos, series or films online (46% watch influencer content several times a day), so a Brazilian family meets kids' video in the preschool years, the exact age band of Bro Bros songs. (Cetic.br / NIC.br, May 2026, medium)
  • BabyBus's Japanese channel (5.86M subscribers) still draws about 104M views every 28 days, but its monthly subscriber gains fell from about 150K in Dec 2025 to 20K in Oct 2026, so in a mature market views now come from catalogue and recommendations, not fresh subscriptions. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • BabyBus's Vietnamese channel (9.75M subscribers, rank 33 in Vietnam) gets about 71M to 116M views a month in 2026 and a single new Short reached about 528K views in 2.5 days, so Vietnam (63M YouTube users) is a large kids market where a re sung Vietnamese track or Shorts could earn real volume. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Japan's kids songs on YouTube are led by anime and character themes (Pokémon, Doraemon, Anpanman) and songs from NHK's daily preschool show 'Okaasan to Issho' (a clock song, a noodle song), plus family pop such as Gen Hoshino's 'Family Song', so Japanese parents favour songs tied to a familiar show; a Japanese Bro Bros track works best on everyday routine topics like time, food and bath. (Soundcharts, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Nigeria has over 30M adult YouTube viewers, watch time grew over 50% in a year and views from Nigeria rose about 80% (Yoola data), with local CPMs of about 0.50 to 2.50 USD against up to 15 USD in the US; as an English speaking country it is a growing audience our English songs reach with no dubbing. (TechCabal, Oct 2025, medium)
  • Both BabyBus local channels post Shorts and song live streams in local language (for example a Japanese ice cream song live stream on 13 Nov 2026), showing that the big brands run the same three formats (long songs, Shorts, live loops) in every language, not only in English. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • About 80% of the content children consume in the Arab world is in languages other than Arabic, Abu Dhabi's culture chief said in September 2026, calling for a 50 50 split; with around 430M Arabic speakers this is a large, under served audience for a well voiced Arabic track. (Khaleej Times, Sep 2026, medium)
  • Arabic lullaby videos are still scarce online: Spacetoon Mum and Moonbug launched just four original Arabic lullabies in June 2026 to fill the gap, so a calm Bro Bros bedtime song with a human voiced Arabic audio track could rank with little competition. (Spacetoon Group, Jun 2026, medium)
  • AIR's dubbing case data gives typical CPMs of about 0.84 USD for Indonesian, 1.52 Serbian, 1.77 Ukrainian, 2.56 Bulgarian, 3.10 Romanian, 3.69 Greek, 4.02 Hungarian, 5.23 Czech, 5.31 Polish and 9.79 German, so after the big reach languages, Polish, Czech and German tracks earn several times more per view. (AIR Media-Tech, Aug 2025, low)
  • Small language dubs can dominate local charts: an Indonesian kids animation channel (HZH, 12.5M subscribers, about 6.8B views) and the German dub of Vania Mania (1.21M subscribers, #7 in German kids entertainment) both grew from dubbed tracks, which AIR says sometimes beat the original in watch time. (AIR Media-Tech, Aug 2025, low)
  • In YouTube's weekly music charts for 19 to 25 Dec 2025, holiday songs filled the top 10 in the US, UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Australia, Portugal, Spain, France and Japan, but India, Brazil and South Africa had few or none, so for those big kids audiences our December slots should also carry winter, party and New Year songs, not only Christmas. (PPC Land, Dec 2025, high)
  • In Japan a Japanese language Christmas song by a local band sat at No. 3 on YouTube's chart in Christmas week 2025, beside the Western classics, so a Japanese audio track on our main Christmas song is worth testing for that market. (PPC Land, Dec 2025, low)
  • Infobells Hindi (about 72.8M subscribers) has stalled: +0.2M subscribers from May to August 2026 and no change from late September to mid October, with total views rising about 2.2B in four and a half months (roughly 450M a month), so India's oldest rhyme giants are mature and new Hindi entrants face an open, not closed, market. (Vidanalyze, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Kids Channel India (Hindi rhymes, 44.1M subscribers) drew between about 311M and 497M views a month in 2026 (432M in October, its best since January) and +200K to +400K subscribers a month; its newest upload is an elephant rhyme Short ('Ek Mota Hathi', about 284K views in under two days), showing animal rhymes still lead in Hindi. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • El Reino Infantil's Spanish network passed 5.6B YouTube views from January to April 2026 across channels with 229M subscribers, and backs YouTube with more than 90 licensing deals in 15 countries, 2.2M merchandise units and live tours in the Americas and Spain; Spanish kids audiences reward one loved cast built over many years. (Bloomberg Línea, Apr 2026, medium)
  • Brazil's biggest kids music stars are home grown 'pop infantil' acts: MC Divertida (about 18.3M subscribers, 8.6B plays) and the duo Kysha e Mine (about 1.2B YouTube views and 130M TikTok likes in roughly a year, its school life series 'Lance de Escola' over 350M views), built on YouTube plus TikTok plus sold out live shows and family friendly values. (Billboard Brasil, Oct 2025, low)
  • Junior Squad Português, a separate Brazilian dub of an animated nursery channel (813K subscribers), is fading: monthly views fell from about 2.7M in March 2026 to 0.8M in October, subscribers are flat and its newest Short got about 300 views in three days, more proof that a stand alone dubbed channel without new local originals withers while multi audio tracks on the main channel keep the main channel's signals. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Junior Squad Português's all time top videos are a five little monkeys rhyme (46M), a boo boo song (14M) and a peekaboo song (14M), all from 2021 to 2022, showing that in Portuguese the same evergreen topics (counting rhymes, small hurts, peekaboo) lead as in English. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Kids Tv Bangla (3.69M subscribers) gets about 55M views every 28 days but vidIQ models only about 2,500 USD a month in ads, roughly 0.05 USD per 1,000 views, so Bengali language views bring reach but almost no income compared with English views from rich countries. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • That channel's strongest recent upload is an August 2026 remake of an old Bengali folk rhyme (9.3M views, about 68 times its usual), so in South Asian markets refreshed classic local rhymes still beat new songs; for us that argues for original songs in English first and local dubs later, not local rhyme remakes. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
