  • HypeAuditor's top 100 Pakistani YouTube channels by subscribers (Nov 2026) are led by TV networks and dramas (Geo, ARY, HUM) and contain no kids or nursery rhyme channel, which suggests Pakistani children mostly watch global English or Hindi and Urdu kids channels from abroad. (hypeauditor.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • Bengali rhyme channels grow steadily rather than in spikes (Kids Tv Bangla has added about 35M to 90M views a month since late 2024 and about 40K to 50K subscribers a month), the slow and steady pattern of a library of evergreen rhymes and compilations. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • vidIQ models LooLoo's Spanish channel at only about 20K USD from about 154M monthly views (roughly 0.13 USD per 1,000), so Spanish language kids views pay several times less than English ones, though more than Bengali ones. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • The Vietnamese BabyBus channel's most viewed long videos are all December 2021 to 2022 uploads (Kiki and friends 26M, a sushi song 24M, a mystery gift box 23M), showing that its library peaked years ago and new long videos rarely overtake old winners, while new Shorts still reach about 500K views in two days. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • vidIQ models BabyBus's Vietnamese channel at only about 3,500 USD a month from about 92M monthly views (roughly 0.04 USD per 1,000), among the lowest earning kids audiences we have measured, so Vietnamese dubs are for reach, not income. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • A December 2025 look at Spotify Wrapped in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa found kids' picks (CoComelon, Pinkfong, Super Simple Songs, Wheels on the Bus, Baby Shark) became the whole household's soundtrack, used for morning prep, car rides, bath and bedtime, alongside local language lullabies, so routine songs travel well in African homes. (expression.africa, Dec 2025, medium)
  • Kids Tv Bangla (3.69M subscribers, about 2.1B views) gets about 52M to 59M views a month in 2026, yet vidIQ models only about 2,500 USD of ad income from that, roughly 0.05 USD per 1,000 views, so a Bengali dub would add reach and fans but very little money. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Kids Tv Bangla's three most viewed videos are remix versions of traditional Bengali rhymes (15M to 18M each), and an August 2026 traditional rhyme upload reached 9.3M views in under three months, 68 times its usual video, so in South Asian markets a remixed folk rhyme beats new material. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Bangladesh has about 45 million children and too little local children's content, so many kids watch Indian Hindi cartoons on YouTube and some speak Hindi better than Bengali, which makes a Hindi dub reach Bangladeshi children too (article undated, early to mid 2020s). (thedailystar.net, about 2022, low)
  • HypeAuditor's November 2026 Thailand ranking puts localised editions of global family brands in its top ten family channels (Vlad and Niki THA 14.2M subscribers, Brianna's Secret Club TH 8.2M) next to local Thai family channels of 6M to 13.5M, so a separately localised Thai channel of a global brand can reach the top there. (hypeauditor.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Thai preschool song channels stay small next to Thai family vlogs: Little Treehouse Thailand, a kindergarten songs channel, has about 223K subscribers and 83M views, growing about 4% a month, while the biggest Thai kids song channels (kids song 7.7M, KidsMeSong 7.4M) are a fraction of the top family channels. (vidiq.com and hypeauditor.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • LooLoo's Polish channel (about 200K subscribers, 103M views, 622 videos) slid from about 1.8M monthly views in July 2026 to about 0.8M in October and vidIQ models only about 200 USD a month, so Polish is a small, low paying dub market to add late, not early. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • LooLoo Polish's two biggest videos are 30 and 40 minute compilations led by a marching ants song (about 5.3M and 4.7M views), so the marching ants theme that gave our best Reel this week (Ant Parade) also travels to Eastern Europe and suits a long compilation opener. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon Italiano has only about 1.2M subscribers and 1.3B views from 939 uploads; its October 2026 Halloween Shorts drew about 3K to 10K views each while a long seasonal vegetables episode reached about 161K within a week, so in Italy even the biggest brand's Shorts are weak and long episodes carry the channel. (vidanalyze.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Thailand's YouTube top 100 (Nov 2026) includes Thai editions of global kids brands (Vlad and Niki Thai 14.2M subscribers, Brianna's Secret Club TH 8.2M) and three Thai language kids song channels with about 7.1M to 7.7M subscribers and 4B to 4.6B views each, so a Thai dubbed Bro Bros channel would enter a large, song hungry market despite the small language. (hypeauditor.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Nine of Italy's top 100 YouTube channels (vidIQ, 12 Nov 2026) are for kids, mostly Italian editions of global brands (Masha e Orso 7.3M subscribers at 12th, WB Kids Italiano 5.4M, Disney Junior Italia 3.8M, Nickelodeon Italia 2.6M) plus local song brands HeyKids (3.4M, 3.4B views), Dolci Melodie (3.0M) and Coccole Sonore (2.6M), so Italian families readily watch dubbed foreign cartoons and an Italian song channel has room. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Turkey's top animation channel list (Nov 2026) has no large kids song cartoon brand; the biggest kids entry is the Turkish edition of an Arabic kids song channel at about 1.1M subscribers and about 33K average views, so Turkish is an under served language for animated kids songs, worth testing after the big languages. (hypeauditor.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • Boom Buddies India (Hindi and English, 1.24M subscribers) drew about 15.8M views in 28 days to Nov 2026, more than the US main channel's 10.7M, yet vidIQ's modelled ad income was about 830 dollars against about 3,300 for the main channel, roughly a fifth of the money per view, so Hindi editions buy reach while English and European audiences pay the bills. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • Kenyan kids brand Super Sema released a nursery rhyme album remade with Afrobeat rhythms, including a Swahili hello song, a Swahili Twinkle Twinkle and an African safari 'Bear Hunt', presenting them as heritage and bilingual learning, a model for Afrobeat flavoured Bro Bros versions aimed at Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana. (supersema.com, Jul 2025, medium)
  • In a survey of 1,000 Filipino parents of 8 to 17 year olds (29 Oct to 2 Nov 2026) 34% said they use child specific apps such as YouTube Kids for safety and 97% want evidence based rules on children's social media, so Philippine families are open to supervised kids platforms and stricter rules may follow there too. (tribune.net.ph, Nov 2026, high)
  • A University of the Philippines study of children aged 2 to 36 months found touchscreen video use of nearly two hours a day, with mothers choosing shows they see as educational and using that time to work or do chores, so English learning songs (colours, numbers, routines) suit Filipino parents, who already accept English content. (ovpaa.up.edu.ph, 2023, medium)
  • South Koreans spent about 113.6B minutes a month on YouTube in Jan to May 2026, over 20 times Netflix, while YouTube Music usage grew 186% since 2022 and now beats Melon and Spotify there, so for Korean families our songs should be on YouTube Music as well as on the main channel. (hankyung.com, Jun 2026, medium)
  • Pakistan's most subscribed YouTube list (Nov 2026) has few clear kids channels near the top; the main family entry is Peep Peep at 20th with 13.4M subscribers and 10.1B views, so Urdu kids songs look like an open space compared with the crowded Hindi kids market, though the data are thin. (hypeauditor.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • An OpinionWay survey of 1,049 French parents of 3 to 10 year olds found screen exposure peaks in the winter holidays (96% of kids, average 1h51 a day in February versus 1 hour in term time, 16% over three hours), so holiday weeks are when French speaking families watch most. (OpinionWay for tonies via CB News, Feb 2026, high)
  • In the same French survey 46% of parents said grandparents are more relaxed about screens and half leave screens on more in holidays for lack of time, so in holiday weeks the person pressing play is often a grandparent who searches simple words like song name plus 'comptine'. (OpinionWay for tonies via CB News, Feb 2026, medium)
  • 29% of French parents count watching cartoons together as family bonding time, which supports family singalong compilations in French for the Christmas and February holidays. (OpinionWay for tonies via CB News, Feb 2026, medium)
  • Kaboochi's French nursery rhyme channel (197K subscribers, 618 videos) gained no subscribers in the 28 days to 13 Nov 2026 and earns about 100K views a month, down from up to 255K a month in 2024, and its biggest hit is a Short, so small French dub channels stall and Shorts carry what reach they have. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A French expert commission (2024) advised no screens under 3, limited and accompanied screens from 3 to 6 and curbs on autoplay; French parents are primed to prefer calm, educational, co watched videos, so the French version of Bro Bros should lead with learning songs, not hype. (The Media Leader France, May 2024, medium)
  • Parrot Analytics measured global audience demand for preschool titles up about 25% and school age titles up about 21% over the year to mid 2025, while TV demand overall fell, so kids content is one of the few growing categories worldwide. (Parrot Analytics via Kidscreen, Sep 2025, high)
  • India made Mighty Little Bheem reaches US demand at 76% of its Indian level, Pakistan 75% and the Philippines 74%, with Germany and Brazil above half, proof that a wordless or simple English kids brand created in India can be loved almost equally abroad. (Parrot Analytics via Kidscreen, Sep 2025, high)
  • A June 2026 survey of 367 Japanese primary school children found Minecraft (31.8%) and Roblox (12.7%, about eight times last year) are the most played games and HikakinGames is the favourite game YouTuber for the seventh year (29.6%), so block building and obby style challenge themes reach Japanese 6 to 12 year olds. (gamebiz.jp (Gametore survey), Jun 2026, high)
  • In a Shogakukan survey of 500 Japanese parents of 6 to 9 year olds, about 65% of children watch YouTube, most for 30 minutes to an hour a day, and the top channels are variety and Minecraft creators while kids educational channels rank 14th and below, so Japanese Bro Bros audio should aim at preschool families rather than school age kids. (HugKum (Shogakukan), Aug 2024, medium)
  • Maasranga Kids, the children's channel of a Bangladeshi TV station and the only kids channel in Bangladesh's top 100 (vidIQ, 12 Nov 2026, 5.31M subscribers), grew from about 3.0B views in July 2025 to about 4.9B by November 2026 (roughly 120M views a month) by posting about 14 videos a week averaging 9 minutes, showing steady volume beats virality in this market. (vidIQ, Jul 2025 and Nov 2026, medium)
  • A Swahili kids cartoon channel (Kids TV Africa, about 711K subscribers, 245M views from 872 videos) drew only about 28K views a day and gained no subscribers from 11 to 24 Oct 2026, so Swahili is a low priority dub for now compared with Spanish, Portuguese or Hindi. (Social Blade, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Omo Berry, a Nigerian made 3D animated learning show with Black child characters and African rooted songs (launched on YouTube Feb 2021), had its biggest audiences in the US and UK ahead of Nigeria, showing that culturally specific kids songs travel through diaspora families in high ad rate countries; an Afrobeats flavoured Bro Bros song can do the same. (BBC Communique via mirror, 2023, low)
  • WildBrain runs six YouTube channels for The Fixies by language: English passed 3M subscribers and 3B views, Spanish 3M subscribers and 1.8B views, and an Arabic channel opened in 2024 already has 45M views, so Spanish deserves a full channel and Arabic is a fast growing extra. (Senal News, Jul 2026, high)
  • Polish kids song channel Spiewajace Brzdace (2.61M subscribers, 5.1B views) got about 45.8M views and 10K new subscribers in the 28 days to 11 Nov 2026, and its biggest hits are short silly songs about one funny thing (a watermelon, a rooster, a pug, a little chicken), showing a mid sized language market of about 38M people can still give a local song channel tens of millions of views a month. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Moonbug's Arabic hub channel (909K subscribers) mixing dubbed Morphle, Blippi and other shows got only about 1.7M views and 1K subscribers in the 28 days to 14 Nov 2026, with a new upload at 3.65K views after three days, so a big brand's catch all dubbed channel underperforms in Arabic compared with focused single show channels like The Fixies Arabic. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • For Bro Bros dubbing, the two data points together suggest one channel per language built around our own song catalogue with native sounding titles beats one mixed 'international' channel, and Polish is a realistic smaller market where a single funny food or animal song can carry the channel. (own synthesis of vidIQ data, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Germany's Hurra Kinderlieder (4.09M subscribers, 5.7B views) got about 58M views and 10K subscribers in the 28 days to 3 Nov 2026, and its biggest songs are about everyday moments and feelings: a haircut at the hairdresser (44M), an upside down world play song (32M), a tantrum told as a sudden thunderstorm (30M) and get well soon (28M). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • A small Turkish kids song channel (Minnak, 201K subscribers, under 1M views a month) owes almost all its reach to one silly fruit character song, 'Watermelon Man' (8.6M views), and a watermelon song is also the top hit of Poland's biggest local song channel, so a goofy fruit character song is a cheap test that has travelled in two different markets. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In AIR's 2026 dataset a kids channel uploaded the same videos with Arabic, French and German audio tracks (16 Feb to 24 Mar 2026): Arabic drew 3.4M views, French 745K and German only 134K, yet German had the highest share of returning viewers (about 52% versus 47% and 42%) and the longest watch time for new viewers (4:30), so dub languages should be judged by how many viewers come back, not by raw views. (AIR Media-Tech, Apr 2026, medium)
  • AIR's rule of thumb for a dubbed audio track: in the first 90 days most views come from new viewers, so judge it after about 4 months; if casual plus regular viewers are still under 20% of that track's views it is not working, 20 to 40% is building and above 40% is working (YouTube Analytics, Audience, watch behaviour, filtered by audio track). (AIR Media-Tech, Apr 2026, medium)
  • Brazil's Portuguese kids song channel Cleo e Cuquin (6.42M subscribers, 5.36B views) has as its biggest hit a colourful train song (65M), followed by wheels on the bus, surprise eggs with numbers and colours, and a farm song, but its monthly views fell from about 135M in March 2026 to 44M in October, so vehicles, colours and farm topics travel to Brazil while even big local channels are losing ground this year. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • The Arabic kids channel Tn Tn Baby (226K subscribers, 75M views) gets almost a third of all its views from one video, the 'without rhythm' (no instruments) version of its 'hello police, the thief ran away' song at 23.75M, about five times its normal version, which shows that many Muslim families look for vocals only kids songs; a voice only (or voice plus body percussion) edit of our best songs is a cheap extra upload for Arabic, Malay and Indonesian audiences. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Super Dido Kids Songs (474K subscribers, 261M views, about 4M views a month) has as its biggest Arabic hits a 'mama is coming home' song (39.8M), 'grandpa has a donkey' (23.8M), a fish in the sea song and a 'toot toot' train song, mostly as remixes, so family members, farm animals and trains are the safest themes for an Arabic Bro Bros version. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • The police and runaway thief chase is the top theme of Tn Tn Baby (its five most viewed videos are all versions of it), echoing the 'who took the cookie' hook that works in Germany and on our own Reels, so a gentle chase or mystery story is a hook that crosses Arabic and European audiences alike. (own synthesis of vidIQ data, Nov 2026, low)
  • LooLoo Kids' Spanish channel (La Alegría de Cantar, 1.57M subscribers, 664M views) gets its biggest views from a chicks and Lola the cow medley (362M) and then two 'who breaks the piñata?' party song compilations (79M and 43M), showing that the piñata party song is a big Latin American family favourite, useful for birthdays all year and for Mexico's posadas from 16 to 24 December. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Roy Morgan's survey of 1,129 Australian children aged 6 to 13 (Apr to Dec 2025, published Feb 2026) found 89% watch YouTube; for 6 to 9 year olds the top genres after gaming are animation (40%), animals (35%) and challenges (32%), girls lead on animals and music, and the under 16 ban does not cover YouTube Kids or logged out viewing, so animated animal songs with a little challenge are the best fit for young Australians. (Roy Morgan, Feb 2026, medium)
  • The Japanese nursery song channel Utamap (365K subscribers but 1.08B views, about 10M views in 28 days) gets its biggest views from finger play songs (te asobi) sung like the national TV kids show: a 'tonton, Mr Beard' fist tapping game (67M), a baked sweet potato rock paper scissors finger play (38M) and a vegetable song (35M), and even its newest Short is a railway crossing finger play (143K), so seated hands only songs are a strong format for Japanese toddlers and parents. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Panpandodobibi (Pandobi, 1.66M subscribers, 481M views) gets about 253M views from one 'Mosquito Song, Go Away Mosquito' and two more mosquito good habit songs passed 22M and 31M, while its newest 'Which colour do you want?' baby song (29 Oct 2026) is already a 10x outlier at 472K views, so mosquito songs are a proven hit for families in warm countries (India, Southeast Asia, Africa, Latin America) and colours remain a safe evergreen. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Thai kids song channel KidsMeSong (7.39M subscribers) got about 40.5M views in the 28 days to mid October 2026 but vidIQ estimates only about 9K USD a month in revenue (roughly 0.2 USD per 1,000 views), so a Thai dub would add reach and subscribers far more than income. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, medium)
  • KidsMeSong's all time hits are a cat sound song (about 71M views), 3D cartoon Thai alphabet songs (37M and 29M) and caterpillar and insect songs (about 29M each), which again shows animal sound and alphabet songs travel best into a new language. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, high)
  • Italy's top 100 channels (vidIQ, Nov 2026) include two home grown kids music brands, Ninna e Matti (2.69M subscribers, 2.35B views) and CoccoleSonore (2.55M, 2.38B), beside HeyKids Italian (3.36M, 3.4B), so Italian families support original song brands, not only dubbed TV shows. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A Korea Institute of Child Care and Education survey of 13,241 children under 6 (Jul to Sep 2025, published Feb 2026) found 14.6% already take private English lessons, and 85.7% of children in intensive half day academies attend English immersion preschools at about 1.54M won a month, so Korean parents actively seek English for toddlers and clearly sung, simple English Bro Bros songs have a paying audience there. (Korea Times, Feb 2026, high)
  • TD Hub's analysis of Ukraine's 1,137 largest YouTube channels (2024 to Sep 2026) found kids content was the only one of 15 niches where the Ukrainian language share of views fell, mainly because one popular Russian language kids channel kept growing, which shows that in kids video one strong channel in a language can move a whole country's viewing, and that local language kids songs are a contested gap. (UA.NEWS, Nov 2026, medium)
  • 3Vision's Video Markets Tracker (reported Jul 2026) forecasts YouTube ad revenue in Sub Saharan Africa of about 583M USD in 2026, above any single subscription streamer's revenue there, rising to about 1.18B USD by 2031 (about 92% of the region's ad supported video market), so English speaking Africa is a free, YouTube first market where Bro Bros songs can grow without competing with paid services. (Senal News / 3Vision, Jul 2026, high)
  • In the same forecast Nigeria's YouTube ad revenue grows from about 128M USD (2026) to 279M USD (2031) while Netflix there has only about 1.2M subscribers, and South Africa's YouTube ad revenue rises from about 191M to 325M USD; ad rates are low but the audience is large, English speaking and growing, which suits an English kids song channel. (Senal News / 3Vision, Jul 2026, high)
  • If the UK widens its under 16 rule to YouTube Kids, British children would reach Bro Bros mostly through a parent's signed in account or logged out viewing on the family TV, so our UK titles, thumbnails and Reels should also speak to parents choosing for their children. (AI Weekly, Nov 2026 (our reading), low)
  • Parrot Analytics found that across 16 MENA markets family rated animation over indexes (28.6% of demand from 20.6% of titles) while kids only titles under index, so for an Arabic audio track our whole family songs (dancing with parents and grandparents) are a better first pick than toddler only rhymes. (parrotanalytics.com, 2026, medium)
  • In the same MENA data about 23% of the kids animation audience is Gen X or older and the audience skews about 60% male, a sign of heavy parent co viewing, so Arabic titles and thumbnails should appeal to parents as well as children. (parrotanalytics.com, 2026, low)
  • Little Angel's Indonesian channel (14.8M subscribers, about 8.9B views) drew only about 26M views in the 28 days to late October 2026 with no subscriber growth, while its all time top videos (35 to 41M each) are everyday life songs (hot or cold, a zoo visit, favourite vegetables, the playground, healthy morning habits), so in Indonesia simple daily routine songs keep earning long after newer uploads stall. (vidiq.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Indonesia remains one of AIR's top four dub languages by views (with Spanish, Arabic and Portuguese) and Little Angel, CoComelon, LooLoo and BabyBus all run Indonesian dubbed channels, so an Indonesian audio track is a sound third or fourth language for Bro Bros after Spanish and Portuguese. (vidiq.com and air.io, 2026, medium)
  • In Poland, children aged 7 to 14 spend about 4 hours 25 minutes online a day, 88% of it on smartphones, and TikTok takes a bigger share of that time (29%) than YouTube (22%), so in Central Europe our Shorts and Reels cut downs reach older kids more than long videos do. (Internet of Children 2026 report (pkdp.gov.pl, Gemius data), Jul 2026, high)
  • About 400,000 Polish children aged 7 to 12 spend more than two hours a day on TikTok even though it is 13+, a sign that school age kids in Europe drift to short video apps as soon as they outgrow kids content. (Internet of Children 2026 report (pkdp.gov.pl), Jul 2026, medium)
  • A survey of 22,000 Polish children aged 7 to 9 found over 80% watch YouTube regularly, two thirds own a smartphone and about one in four have already posted their own content, so 7 to 9 year olds are an active YouTube audience in Europe, not only toddlers. (FDDS survey via Poland Insight, Oct 2025, high)
  • Egypt has about 49.3M adult YouTube users (almost level with Facebook's 51.6M and TikTok's 48.8M) and 92.6M mobile internet users, making it one of the largest Arabic speaking YouTube audiences even though its ad rates are low. (Egypt IDSC / Kepios via Scene Now, Apr 2026, high)
  • Germany's 'Sing mit mir - Kinderlieder' (3.95M subscribers, 5.2B views, 654 videos, about one upload a week) still pulls about 66M views a month, and its top hits are a vehicles song mix, a grasshopper song and a 2025 silly dog poop song that is 35 times its channel average, so German families reward funny everyday songs and vehicles, the same themes that travel in English. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • Kenya's 'Uli and Tata's African Nursery Rhymes' (on YouTube since Oct 2024, also on free TV channel Akili Kids with a cited audience of about 5M children) follows a brother and sister guided by a giant singing bird to find nursery rhymes across Africa, sung in English, French, Swahili, Gikuyu and Luhya and set in real places; a sibling quest that visits a new country per song is a proven frame for our two brothers to travel with original songs. (Culture Custodian, Nov 2025, medium)
  • The Uli and Tata team visits communities to research each song and setting so the show avoids stereotypes, which is the standard we should keep for any Bro Bros song set in a real country: real foods, clothes, instruments and places checked against reliable sources, never jokes about accents. (Culture Custodian, Nov 2025, medium)
  • On Soundcharts' Philippines kids chart (Nov 2026) 12 of the top 15 kids songs by local linked acts are in English and only 3 in Tagalog, led by Jana Alayra's upbeat songs (25M and 22M views), so the Philippines takes English Bro Bros songs without dubbing. (Soundcharts, Nov 2026, medium)
  • About six of the Philippines top 15 kids songs are faith or worship songs and the rest are kindness, school and play songs ('The Kindness Song', BINGO), so in that market gentle values songs about kindness, sharing and thankfulness fit well, without us needing religious lyrics. (Soundcharts, Nov 2026, medium)
  • HypeAuditor's November 2026 Thailand ranking shows the biggest kids channels there are local language versions and Thai song channels: a Thai dub of a global family vlog brand at 14.2M subscribers, Thai kids song channels at 7 to 8M (one tagged animals and education), and BabyBus's Thai channel at 5.5M, so Thailand rewards a dedicated Thai language track with animal themed songs rather than English only uploads. (hypeauditor.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Indonesia, TikTok's largest market, began a social media ban for under 16s on 28 Mar 2026 with up to a year for platforms to comply, so Indonesian children (a top dubbing language for kids channels) will increasingly reach Bro Bros through a parent's account or the family TV, which favours full songs and long compilations over Shorts and Reels for that market. (insidethecreator.beehiiv.com, Mar 2026, medium)
  • Arab preschool YouTube hits often adapt classic rhymes and songs into a regional dialect (a Lebanese Arabic preschool music channel passed 1M subscribers serving local families and the diaspora), so an Arabic Bro Bros track should pick one warm, widely understood spoken dialect for chants and keep sung choruses simple rather than formal classroom Arabic. (kidscreen.com, 2023, low)
  • A Mexican Spanish rhyme channel built on a global brand's animation (1.39M subscribers, about 3M views a month through 2026) gets its biggest hit by far from a 'who breaks the piñata?' party medley (about 42M views, ten times its next video), and its newest uploads still chain Latin classics (little chicks, the cow, peekaboo) into medleys, so in Mexico a piñata party song and medleys of familiar rhythms are the strongest Spanish formats. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In YouTube's supervised kid accounts for MENA and Turkiye (launched 1 Jul 2026) dance sits in the youngest 'Explore' level next to tutorials and crafts, and autoplay is switched off, so every Bro Bros video there must win the next tap through playlists, end screens and a clear series look. (arabnews.com, Jul 2026, high)
  • Kantar data cited by YouTube shows parental control use in the Middle East up about 60% in a year and searches for children's educational YouTube programmes doubled, so Arabic titles that name what a song teaches (colours, counting, manners) fit what Gulf parents now look for. (arabnews.com (Kantar), Jul 2026, medium)
  • 77% of Turkish parents of under 15s call YouTube an important free resource for learning, while Turkiye and the UAE have moved to near bans on social media for under 15s, so in those markets YouTube (parent supervised) stays our main door and Instagram reaches parents, not kids. (arabnews.com, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Pakistan's Urdu kids series Pakkay Dost, led by a well known pop singer, has 50+ songs and its fourth season (YouTube, 22 Aug 2026) sings about fitness, kindness to animals, vegetable names and the body's bones and joints, built so parents enjoy it as much as kids, a model for an Urdu or Hindi dub of our learning songs. (tribune.com.pk, Aug 2026, medium)
  • A big kids channel tested dubs in 11 languages; Spanish, Arabic, Indonesian and Portuguese pulled ahead first, then Japanese and Korean; dubs added about 125M views in 5 months and now make up over 30% of its views. (AIR case study, Mar 2026, high)
  • In that case, dubbed tracks kept viewers longer than English (Spanish 8:24 and Portuguese 7:59 average view duration against 6:26 for English); traction came first from Suggested, then Browse. (AIR case study, Mar 2026, medium)
  • Adding a language as a multi-audio track on the main channel worked when a separate Portuguese channel failed to take off (Vania Mania Kids). (AIR Vania Mania case, 2026, high)
  • YouTube opened auto-dubbing to all eligible creators in 2026 (Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, French and more); the agencies' advice is to start with the top videos only, and human dubs hold retention better than AI dubs. (OutlierKit Apr 2026 / AIR, medium)
  • Three of the 20 most subscribed YouTube channels in Saudi Arabia (Playboard, 17 Nov 2026) are kids channels: Katakit Baby TV (about 24.3M, Arabic children's songs), Wanasah TV (about 22.1M, Arabic children's songs) and Masha and the Bear Arabic (about 21.4M), so Arabic kids songs sit among the Gulf's very biggest channels and Arabic stays a first wave dub language. (playboard.co, Nov 2026, high)
  • Arabic kids song giants in the Gulf are original Arabic language channels rather than dubs of Western brands, which suggests our Arabic version should get its own translated title, description and sung lyrics (not just subtitles) to compete there. (playboard.co, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Plim Plim, a Latin American preschool series built on positive values told through stories and songs, reached 2 billion YouTube views in May 2026 across its language channels, about double its monthly views of two years earlier, proof that kind, values led song cartoons from outside the US can still grow fast worldwide. (senalnews.com, Jun 2026, high)
  • In Ofcom's Children's Media Lives 2026 (UK) a 10 year old said American channels are the 'only option' she can find because so few creators near her make videos, showing that British children default to US English content, so a clear, neutral global English accent travels to the UK without a separate version. (Ofcom / Revealing Reality, May 2026, medium)
  • Ofcom's 2026 diaries show older siblings choosing videos for little ones (a 15 year old puts CoComelon on an iPad for her younger brothers), so Bro Bros titles and thumbnails must be easy for a teen or parent to find and trust, not only appealing to toddlers. (Ofcom / Revealing Reality, May 2026, medium)
  • UK 9 to 11 year olds in Ofcom's 2026 study mostly watch family vlog and challenge channels (The Norris Nuts, A for Adley, the Royalty family) and gaming creators on the family TV, so Bro Bros older sibling appeal comes from challenge and game formats, while songs serve their younger brothers and sisters. (Ofcom / Revealing Reality, May 2026, medium)
  • Precisify data cited in 2026 says YouTube reaches about 80% of boys and 72% of girls aged 6 to 9, so the older end of our audience leans slightly male, which suits a brothers led cast but means sister and girl friend characters help reach the rest. (eMarketer, 2026, medium)
  • Instagram's long form 'Features' (horizontal videos up to 90 minutes, with short previews in Reels) was tested in Brazil before US creators and will also appear in the new Instagram app for Apple TV in the US, so Brazil is again a first test market for Meta video features. (The National, Oct 2026, medium)
  • In HypeAuditor's November 2026 Colombia ranking the top spots belong to family humour channels (Ami Rodriguez 32.5M, Amara Que Linda 17.8M, Kike y su familia 16.5M), while the biggest kids song channels sit at #32 and #33 (Cuentos y Canciones Infantiles 9.8M, Mundo Canticuentos 9.5M). (HypeAuditor, Nov 2026, high)
  • A Latin American Christmas hit on kids channels is about a little donkey trotting to Bethlehem, not Santa; for Spanish speaking families a cheerful original winter journey song with a friendly animal and clip clop rhythm fits the region's Christmas taste (we write our own song, never reuse that one). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Lellobee runs at least two separate Spanish channels (Latin American, about 802K, and a second, about 244K) that split the same audience and both stalled, so for Bro Bros one Spanish channel or one multi language audio track is better than several thin dub channels. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Kedoo Kids, the YouTube network that took on Hasbro's preschool brands in July 2026, runs kids channels in 34 markets and 19 languages (including Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Turkish and Arabic) for more than a billion views a month, using single episodes, themed compilations and live streams planned per market, so the biggest players treat each language as its own channel with its own compilations. (Senal News, Jul 2026, medium)
  • In October 2026 Banijay Kids and Family pulled more preschool YouTube channels (Olobob Top and TheSoul's DoodLand, Baby Zoo and Learn Toons) into its own YouTube network and also placed shows on a new free preschool channel, so independent kids song channels like ours now compete with large rights networks and should win on speed, trends and a clear character identity rather than library size. (Senal News, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Animation deals for India in 2026 (for example Animotion's series on ZEE5 KidZ and ZEE's YouTube channels, June 2026) dub kids shows into Hindi plus several regional languages because parents increasingly want local language learning content, which supports Hindi as our first dub and regional Indian languages as a later step. (TTV News via Pulse, Jun 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon's Brazilian Portuguese channel (4.45M subscribers, 18 Nov 2026) now adds only about 10K to 20K subscribers a month against 50K to 110K in 2025, with monthly views around 87M to 112M in 2026 after a 191M peak in October 2025, so even the strongest dubbed brand is flattening in Brazil and a new Portuguese channel would compete on fresh, local feeling songs. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • The two most viewed videos on CoComelon's Portuguese channel are a Wheels on the Bus song (703M) and a football song released at the 2022 World Cup (324M), so a football song is a proven Brazil winner; with the 2026 World Cup just behind us, an original Bro Bros kick and score dance in Portuguese is a natural first upload for Brazil. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • CoComelon Portugues posts about 19 videos every four weeks (12 long, 7 Shorts) including dubbed versions of the main channel's films and stories, showing that the big brands localise the full release slate, not just old hits, and pair each long release with a few Shorts in the same language. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • BabyBus's Bahasa Indonesia channel (28.9M) jumped to about 864M monthly views in March 2026 and 535M in April before settling at about 245M a month, so Indonesian kids viewing spikes hugely in the Ramadan and Eid holiday window (Ramadan 2027 starts around mid February), which is when Indonesian dubs and Shorts should be ready. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Brazil's TIC Kids Online 2025 survey (2,370 children aged 9 to 17) found 92% online (about 24 million), 28% online by age 6, and YouTube the standout platform for 9 to 12 year olds while WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok take over from 13, so Brazil's YouTube audience for songs like ours is mostly under 12 and a Portuguese dub targets it well. (NIC.br TIC Kids Online, May 2026, high)
  • In the same Brazil survey phone ownership among 9 to 10 year olds fell to 55% from 67% a year earlier and internet access at school fell to 37% from 51%, while 60% use the internet on a TV daily, so Brazilian children increasingly watch on the family TV and shared devices, which favours long compilations over phone only Shorts. (NIC.br TIC Kids Online, May 2026, medium)
  • Precise TV's Sep 2025 US kids survey (about 2,000 children aged 2 to 12) put YouTube reach at 78% (74% of 2 to 5s, 82% of 6 to 9s) against 53% for YouTube Shorts, with 62% of 2 to 5 year olds watching YouTube on a TV and 49% of children watching with a parent, so in the US our long videos on the TV reach more small children than Shorts do. (Net Influencer (Precise TV), Sep 2025, medium)
  • Hindi kids rhyme channels peak in May, India's school summer vacation: Luke and Lily India (2.68M) had its best month in May 2026 (15.4M views) and its weakest in Nov and Dec 2025 (about 9M), so for an Indian Hindi audience the big season is April to June, while December matters mainly for Western markets. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Super Kids Network India (10.6M subscribers, Hindi) fell from about 191M views in Nov 2025 to about 38M to 42M a month in Sep and Oct 2026 (roughly minus 78%) while still uploading about 16 videos a month, so even large Hindi rhyme channels can lose most of their reach in a year; steady output alone does not protect a channel. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • The top Hindi kids videos are traditional Hindi animal poems bundled as '+ More' collections: a meowing cat poem compilation (168M), a fat elephant rhyme (82M), a horse riding 'chal mere ghode' rhyme (79M), a parrot song and a potato song, so a future Hindi Bro Bros channel should lead with animal and food rhymes (elephant, cat, horse, parrot, monkey) in compilations. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In New Zealand Tonies box sales doubled from 2024 to 2025 and are expected to double again in 2026, Yoto's customer base there roughly doubled in a year with listening up about 125%, and families average about an hour of Yoto a day, spread by word of mouth at school pick up and daycare, so audio only versions of our songs have a fast growing home in smaller English speaking markets too.   • Spain's biggest kids music brand CantaJuego (12.4M subscribers, 11B views) earns a steady 70M to 107M views a month, posting about 13 videos in 28 days, and its top video is an animal dance along song ('the gorilla dance', 31M) ahead of classic Spanish playground songs, so a silly animal dance travels best in Spanish too. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • CantaJuego released its 2026 Spanish Christmas carol compilation ('best villancicos' with the year in the title) on 17 Nov 2026, so Spanish speaking families get holiday compilations from mid November, and a Spanish audio track on our Christmas songs should be live by late November. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Latin American Shorts channels dominate fast growth again: two Uruguayan channels (COPITO and Chispita) and three Brazilian ones sit among the week's fastest gainers for 9 to 15 Nov 2026, backing Spanish and Portuguese as early dub languages. (Tubefilter, Nov 2026, medium)
  • YouTube says auto dubbed versions keep on average about 75% of the original's view duration, and dubbed views can lower a channel's average CPM and RPM even while total revenue goes up, so judge dubbing by total earnings and new viewers, not by channel averages.   • YouTube's Expressive Speech dubbing (keeps tone and emotion) is live in eight languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Hindi and Indonesian, which makes these the cheapest first dubs for Bro Bros songs' spoken intros and outros. (PPC Land citing YouTube, May 2026, high)
  • Across 5,469 animated titles in MENA streaming (Jan to Mar 2026), family animation drew 28.6% of demand from only 20.6% of supply while kids only titles were oversupplied (40.6% of supply, 30.2% of demand), so songs parents enjoy alongside kids have more room there. (Parrot Analytics, Jul 2026, medium)
  • US made animation still earns 46.5% of MENA animation demand and Japanese 38.9%, so English language original animation travels well into the Arab world without local production. (Parrot Analytics, Jul 2026, medium)

  • More than 18,000 Indian YouTube channels have over 1M subscribers, and a Telugu cooking channel reached 6.6M subscribers and 11.8B views by expanding into seven languages, a home grown proof that dubbing into more languages multiplies reach. (MediaNews4U citing YouTube India Impact Report, Sep 2026, medium)
  • 74% of Indian parents who use YouTube say YouTube or YouTube Kids is important for their children's discovery of the world, so learning angles (animals, colours, festivals) in our songs fit what Indian parents value. (MediaNews4U citing YouTube India Impact Report, Sep 2026, medium)

  • In Portuguese, Bebefinn (about 296M views in 28 days to late October) now draws roughly three times CoComelon Portuguese (about 104M in October 2026), so in Brazil a brighter, faster sibling song brand has overtaken the original 3D nursery leader. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In YouTube's music charts for 19 to 25 Dec 2025, Christmas songs filled 7 of the UK top 10 and 5 of the US top 10 but none of India's top 50, and Brazil and South Africa had very little, so our Christmas songs target the UK, US and Europe while Indian viewers get winter fun and New Year songs.   • Jason Vlogs' Hindi language channel passed 9M subscribers, more than its Spanish channel (over 7M), so for a two brothers kids brand a Hindi version can be as big as Spanish; Bro Bros, made in India, has a natural edge there. (AIR Media-Tech interview with Jason Vlogs, medium)

  • Pinkfong names the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Germany, the Philippines, Turkey and Indonesia as Baby Shark's strongest Spotify markets, a list that shows English kids songs are streamed well beyond English speaking countries. (Free Malaysia Today / Pinkfong, May 2026, high)

  • Thai family channels such as J Jai Pan (13.5M subscribers, 14.8B views) and Beam Copphone (8.6M, 14B views) pull more total views than most dubbed foreign brands in Thailand, showing that local family humour still leads there; for Bro Bros, Thai is a later dubbing target after Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi and Indonesian.   • Malaysia's home grown preschool brand Didi and Friends (7.62M subscribers, 8B views, Malay songs) still draws about 62M views a month; its top videos are a vehicle sounds song (25.8M), a 'do not open the door to strangers' safety song (23.3M), a shapes song (19M) and five little monkeys (18.3M), the same universal themes that work in English.   • Moroccan YouTube growth in learning content is driven by Darija, the spoken dialect: educators note many people understand Modern Standard Arabic but do not speak it at home, so an Arabic dub for North Africa may need a friendly everyday style rather than formal Arabic, though no kids specific data was found.   • In the same network, Spanish grew revenue fastest (+1707% on +703% views) and Hindi next (+1231% revenue on +216% views), while Portuguese views brought less revenue per view (+762%), so Portuguese is the reach market and Spanish the money market among our dubbing targets.   • The same brand's Indonesian channel (1.52M subscribers) earns only about 4M to 14M views a month with near zero subscriber growth and an estimated 2K USD a month, against about 200M views for its German channel, so German is a far stronger dubbing market for 3D nursery rhymes than Indonesian for this kind of brand.   • BabyBus Arabic (listed in Saudi Arabia, 10.6M subscribers, about 7.1B views, 1,513 videos) steadily earns about 75M to 90M views a month in 2026 (peak about 132M in March, during Ramadan), proof that one dubbed Arabic channel from an existing song library can become a large, stable audience.   • BabyBus Arabic's biggest videos are colour and counting songs about food and treats ('Dancing Colorful Cakes' 63M, 'Five Rainbow Candies' 57M, 'Ten Dancing Cakes' 45M) plus vehicle songs (garbage truck 22M), so Bro Bros songs about counting colourful foods and big trucks are the safest picks to dub into Arabic first.   • BabyBus Arabic's subscriber count has stalled at 10.6M with zero net gain in several 2026 months while views hold steady, showing that dubbed kids channels in Arabic live on recommendations to returning families rather than subscriptions. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)

  • Sisimpur, Bangladesh's local Sesame Street (1.95M subscribers, about 1.38B views, 900 videos), still gets about 37M to 48M views a month in late 2026 and its top videos are warm character stories about family and kindness (a grandmother story about 58M, a butterfly story 14M), showing Bengali speaking families watch gentle story songs in their own language at scale. (NexLev, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A small Pakistani kids learning channel (TinyTaleem, 145K subscribers) fell to about 2K views a month in 2026 after switching from ABC and Urdu alphabet songs to unrelated viral posts, a reminder that mixing off topic uploads into a kids channel kills its recommendations. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, low)
  • In Japan the biggest TikTok song of 2026 (M!LK's 'Suki Sugite Metsu', nine weeks at number one on TikTok's music chart, Trend Awards music winner) was carried by a simple dance anyone could copy, so a short, easy signature move is what travels in the Japanese market too. (Japan Nakama, 2026, medium)
  • Nippon TV turned that viral dance into a one minute fitness version for its KARADA WEEK health campaign (31 Oct to 8 Nov 2026, slogan 'one minute a day'), showing that a hit dance can be relaunched as a one minute exercise routine; a 'one minute Bro Bros workout' cut of a hit song is a cheap second life for it. (The First Times, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Nigeria's Jeni and Keni (House of Ajebo) relaunched in 3D, is about 80% Afro fusion kids music for ages 1 to 6, and plans spin offs such as folktale segments and kids party DJ mixes, a sign that party mix compilations are seen as a growth format for African family audiences. (BusinessDay Nigeria, Aug 2025, medium)
  • Mexico is the largest single market for El Reino Infantil, the biggest Spanish kids network (about 39.1M subscribers and 32.4B views from Mexico as of Jul 2026, out of 240M+ subscribers worldwide), so a Latin American Spanish dub should be written for Mexican ears first. (Publimetro Mexico, Sep 2026, medium)
  • El Reino Infantil put its farm song characters into Roblox in 2026 and Plim Plim's Christmas 2025 peak came with sold out theatre shows and telethon appearances across Argentina, Mexico and Chile, showing that the top Latin American kids brands treat December as a live event season around their songs. (Publimetro / Senal News, 2025 to 2026, medium)
  • In Ethiopia a 60 second AI generated caterpillar song from the Aynu Kids learning app went viral on TikTok in late 2025 (about 4.3M views and 53K dubs), showing that a short, catchy kids song can travel through TikTok dubs even in smaller African markets. (Shega, Oct 2025, medium)
  • Plim Plim reached 2B monthly YouTube views across its language channels in May 2026, double its level of about two years earlier, and credits language expansion first, more evidence that adding language versions of proven songs is the fastest growth lever for a kids brand.   • El Reino Infantil reached 8.8B YouTube views in the first five months of 2026 (240M+ subscribers, 180+ countries) and names its three content pillars as movement (psychomotor) stimulation, early literacy and family bonding, a simple checklist Bro Bros songs can be measured against.   • Nepal's most subscribed channel is two brothers, Aayush and Abhay (13.4M subscribers, 11.3B views), whose wordless Shorts travel without language and once grew from about 860K to 12M subscribers in a year, but many were remixes of Douyin clips and the channel gained no net subscribers from 22 Oct to 18 Nov 2026, which shows that a brothers format crosses borders while recycled clips stop growing.   • Among Nepal's top 100 channels the only clearly kids or cartoon brand is The Cartoonz Crew (about 3.7M subscribers, 1.3B views from only 219 videos), so Nepali families mostly watch Indian and global kids content, which our English songs and a later Hindi track can reach.   • Ubongo's Kiswahili 'Akili and Me' channel has about 734K subscribers and 4.8M views a month (Oct 2026), against about 1.24M subscribers for its English channel, and its ad revenue is tiny (about 576 USD a month), so a Swahili dub would bring reach in East Africa but little money. (vidIQ, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Sri Lanka's YouTube trending lists on 18 Nov 2026 were almost all Sinhala, with Tamil second, and held only one kids video (a Sinhala song about animals around us), so Sri Lanka is a small, language bound market best reached later through a Sinhala or Tamil audio track rather than English uploads. (kworb.net, Nov 2026, medium)

(vidiq.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Its most viewed Arabic videos are everyday learning songs from 2022 to 2023 (a school morning routine, healthy eating, face painting, being brave) at about 18M to 48M each, so routine and courage topics are what Arabic speaking parents keep replaying. (vidiq.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • A Bengali nursery rhyme channel based in India (Tinku Tv Bangla, about 828K subscribers, 200M views, about 520 videos averaging 25 minutes) added roughly 50K subscribers and about 16M views a month in mid 2025, showing that long Bengali compilations still grow fast in an underserved language of about 45M Bangladeshi children plus West Bengal. (vidiq.com, 2025, medium)
  • Chote Sitare, a Hindi baby rhymes channel (1.83M subscribers, about 784M views, started Jan 2023), had its best month in December 2025 at about 35M views, against 16M to 22M a month through 2026 (21.5M in Oct 2026), so December lifts kids viewing in India too, not only in Christmas markets. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Infobells Hindi still uploads about 3 to 4 new rhymes a week (24 from 22 Aug to 10 Oct 2026) on animals, food, family routines, toys and vehicles, plus festival songs timed to Rakhi, Janmashtami and Ganesh Chaturthi; recent uploads get about 16K to 634K views each, small next to its billion view classics. (vidanalyze.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Parents and teachers who use YouTube to teach English abroad look for channels with a visible, consistent presenter voice and structured teaching rather than the biggest brands, which leaves room for a smaller channel like Bro Bros to be listed as a learning resource if every song states its target words in the description and repeats them clearly. (learnenglishfeelgood.com, Oct 2026, medium)
  • Romania's biggest kids song channel, TraLaLa, has about 7.93M subscribers and 11B views, still earns about 149M views in 28 days (175M in October 2026) from nursery rhymes, animal and finger play songs, and posted traditional Romanian carols on 13 Nov 2026, so even a mid size European language supports a song channel at this scale and its December carol season starts in mid November. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, high)
  • In Ukraine (Detector Media study, Aug 2025) about half of the top 20 kids YouTube channels are now voiced in Ukrainian, up from about one in the top 10 in 2023, and a Ukrainian language song channel made by Lviv authors is No. 2 with about 614M views behind Masha and the Bear; experts say parents now prefer native language channels that mix fun and learning, which supports dubbing our best songs into Ukrainian later. (dev.ua (Detector Media), Aug 2025, medium)
  • English language kids channels still take two of Ukraine's top 10 kids channel slots (about 80M and 74M views), so our original English songs can reach Eastern European children directly before any dubbing. (dev.ua (Detector Media), Aug 2025, medium)

(vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Hungary's OviTeve (since 2012, about 206K subscribers and 295M views) now lives almost entirely on Shorts of remixed Hungarian preschool songs (21 uploads in 28 days, about 3.1M views a month, best Short 1.2M about a donkey), so small language markets are reachable with very short animal song clips, and Hungarian views pay well (about 4 USD CPM in AIR's dubbing data). (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Israel's biggest Hebrew kids song channel, Hop's 'Israeli Childhood' (about 820K subscribers, 1.37B views), still draws about 9M views a month from song medleys and classic characters; its top videos are a 'today is a birthday' song (12.8M) and songs of a beloved gardener character (up to 12.2M), so a birthday song and a recurring gentle helper character are the strongest Hebrew formats, matching what works in other languages. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A Hebrew child presenter channel (Nofiki, about 192K subscribers, 197M views) got its best 2026 results from short lesson stories about bullying, saying sorry after a fall and healthy versus unkind friendships (about 600K views each), showing that small social and emotional lessons travel well even in a small language market. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Cambodia has about 10.8M internet users (61% penetration, DataReportal 2025) and YouTube is its main music platform, yet its Khmer kids channels are small: Kids Planet Khmer, a dubbed fairy tale and moral story channel with about 478K subscribers, drew under 1M views in 28 days (Oct 2026) and an estimated 135 USD a month after uploads paused in May, so a Khmer dub would not pay back and Cambodian families are best reached by our English songs. (vidIQ, Oct 2026; Interspace Music, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Nigerian parent guides (Pulse Nigeria, updated Jun 2026) recommend local language teaching channels (Yoruba Stars, Learn Igbo) next to English brands, plus Bino and Fino, a Nigerian brother and sister cartoon about African culture, showing that West African parents value home language songs and sibling heroes who look like their children; a later Yoruba or Igbo version of a simple Bro Bros song could earn goodwill there. (Pulse Nigeria, 2025 to 2026, medium)
  • Google's Johannesburg briefing (Mar 2026) put YouTube adult mobile reach at about 35M in Nigeria, 25M in South Africa and 12M in Kenya, with watch time growing about 15%, 20% and 30% a year; these English speaking markets are among the fastest growing for YouTube and need no dubbing for Bro Bros. (Webfluential, Mar 2026, high)
  • Connected TV YouTube reach is already about 8M in South Africa and 3 to 3.5M each in Nigeria and Kenya (Sep 2025), so in Africa most kids still watch on a parent's phone, which favours bright, simple, phone readable thumbnails and data light Shorts. (Webfluential, Mar 2026, medium)
  • In Kaspersky's measure of children's app time (Nov 2020 to Apr 2021), Kenyan children spent more than half of their popular app time on YouTube, the highest share of any country listed, an older but strong sign that East African kids are heavy YouTube users. (Statista / Kaspersky, 2021, low)
  • YouTube's MENA review of 2025 (Dec 2025) named a Roblox gardening game, collectible plush charms and 'brainrot' memes among the region's top topics alongside Ramadan and Eid al Adha, and family sketch channels such as Om Saif (19.9M) among the top creators, so Arabic speaking kids follow the same global game and toy waves; Bro Bros Arabic versions can ride seasonal Ramadan and Eid songs plus global play themes. (blog.google MENA, Dec 2025, medium)
  • WARC Media (Jul 2026) puts YouTube's 2025 ad revenue at 40.4B USD (+11.7%) but forecasts only about 7% growth in 2026, so ad rates will rise slowly and a kids channel's income growth must come from more views and more countries, not higher CPMs. (Senal News citing WARC, Jul 2026, high)
  • WARC reports YouTube's largest user bases as India (about 500M), the US (254M), Indonesia (151M) and Brazil (150M), with average daily watch time up to 58 minutes in 2025 from 48, so Indonesian and Brazilian Portuguese audio tracks reach audiences as large as the US. (Senal News citing WARC, Jul 2026, medium)
  • 3Vision forecasts YouTube ad revenue of about 191M USD in South Africa and 128M USD in Nigeria in 2026, rising to about 325M and 279M by 2031, so English language kids songs already earn in the two biggest African markets and the Nigerian one grows fastest. (Senal News citing 3Vision, Jul 2026, medium)
  • Acamar Films runs Bing on 67 YouTube channels in 35 languages and says this brings about 1.3M hours of viewing worldwide on a good day, a concrete benchmark for how far one character brand can scale by opening a separate channel per language. (c21media.net, Sep 2026, high)
  • A tiny Arabic kids song channel (Anghamalatfal, about 18.7K subscribers, 37 videos) pulled about 38.4M views in the 28 days to 18 Nov 2026, almost all from two counting Shorts posted in late October (counting 1 to 10 with a bouncing ball, about 23.8M, and a 10 to 1 countdown, about 10.5M), while its median video has about 9K views. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • That same Arabic channel posts a mix of long songs and Shorts about every 4 days on numbers, letters, colours and vehicles, so a simple numbers Short with one moving object can take a brand new channel from almost nothing to millions in the Arab world; an Arabic counting Short is a cheap first test for our dubs. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Chile's IBOPE cross media study (1,078 homes, May 2026) found video platforms' share of viewing by 4 to 12 year olds rises from 36% in the school year to 44% in the summer holidays, YouTube reaches more than 700K Chilean children a day against about 380K for TikTok, and the TV set still carries about 61% of their platform viewing in summer. (cntv.cl, May 2026, high)
  • In the same Chilean data 97% of children's TikTok use is solo while YouTube is mostly watched on the shared TV, so for southern summer holidays (Dec to Feb) our long form songs and compilations are the family TV play and Shorts are the solo phone play. (cntv.cl, May 2026, medium)
  • eMarketer expects about 30.7M US Gen Alpha viewers on YouTube in 2026, roughly two thirds of the generation, and YPulse finds 73% of US tweens would rather watch shows on YouTube than on cable or streaming services. (YPulse, Jun 2026, medium)
  • China's Winsing Animation (GG Bond, GOGOBUS) told Senal News at MIPCOM 2026 that it now makes fewer but more premium kids shows, runs multilingual GOGOBUS nursery rhyme channels on YouTube, dubs features into Russian for Kazakhstan and Russia (700+ Russian screens for its newest film) and sells a dialogue free slapstick series because it crosses language barriers, a reminder that Russian speaking CIS markets are a dub option and that wordless dance breaks travel everywhere. (Senal News, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Spotify Wrapped 2025 across Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and South Africa was widely described as shaped by children, with CoComelon, Pinkfong, Super Simple Songs and nursery rhymes playing through home speakers and TVs at mornings, car rides and bedtime, so audio versions of Bro Bros songs on Spotify can reach African family homes too. (newstrends.co.ke, Dec 2025, low)
  • Perso's dubbing platform data (Jan 2025 to Aug 2026, about 303K paid minutes) shows creators dub most into Spanish (11.8%), Portuguese (10.1%) and French (6.8%) after English, and its education category also leads with Portuguese and Spanish, so Spanish and Portuguese remain the safest first two dub languages for Bro Bros, with French third. (perso.ai, Sep 2026, medium)
  • UK creator SV2 added Spanish, Arabic, Portuguese, French and German audio tracks (later Vietnamese, Turkish, Russian and Indonesian) and his views rose about 1.7x (252M to 432M) over 18 months, and one video released with nine audio tracks from day one passed 11M views in under 90 days, so dubbed tracks work best when they are live at upload, not added weeks later. (bemultilingual.ca, Apr 2026, medium)
  • Africa had about 600M children aged 0 to 14 in 2025, and Nigeria alone had about 96M (one in six of them), ahead of Ethiopia and DR Congo (about 52M each), so English language Bro Bros songs already speak to Africa's largest child population, and French would open DR Congo, the biggest French speaking child market. (intelpoint.co (World Bank, UN WPP), 2025, medium)
  • Kids First Espanol Latino (Mexico, 10.1M subscribers, mostly licensed Spanish dubbed preschool cartoon episodes, about 30 uploads a month) grew from about 27M views in June 2026 to 55M in October and about 70M in the 28 days to 19 Nov, so Latin American Spanish kids viewing rises strongly into the holiday season, a good moment for Spanish audio tracks on our songs. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • A Portugal based Portuguese nursery song channel (Kids Channel Portugues, 1.75M subscribers) held flat at about 8M to 10M views a month through 2026 with new uploads getting only about 6K views in five days, while its best videos are older Halloween and rhyme compilations, which suggests Brazilian Portuguese, not European Portuguese, is where the growth is. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, low)
  • In Indonesia's weekly top 10 YouTube channels (7 Nov 2026) the only kids channels are two dubbed foreign brands: Tayo Bahasa Indonesia (27.5M subscribers, about 31.4M views in 30 days and about 1.01M views per upload, the best per upload in the top 10) and BabyBus Indonesian (28.9M, about 10.2M in 30 days), so a well dubbed vehicle or song brand can top a big local market. (databoks.katadata.co.id, Nov 2026, high)
  • YouTube said (May 2026, Dec 2025 data) that over 6M viewers a day watch more than 10 minutes of auto dubbed videos and that dubbed versions keep about 75% of the original's average view duration; videos over 120 minutes are not dubbed, so dubbed spoken intros fit our normal songs but not 2 hour compilations. (ppc.land, May 2026, high)
  • Circana (Aug 2026): in Latin America (Brazil, Chile, Peru, Mexico) December alone brings about 32% of a year's toy sales, even more in Chile and Peru, and LATAM toy spending is growing faster than Europe's, so Spanish and Portuguese Christmas songs and dubs pay off most in the next five weeks. (circana.com, Aug 2026, high)
  • Circana: Europe spends about 240 US dollars a year on toys per child under 10, the second highest in the world, while Asia and Oceania are the fastest growing toy regions and Asia had the biggest rise in spend per child in 2025. (circana.com, Aug 2026, high)

  • Parrot Analytics' study of 5,469 animated titles in 16 Middle East and North Africa markets (Jan to Mar 2026) found kids titles are 40.6% of supply but only 30.2% of demand (crowded), while family titles are 20.6% of supply and 28.6% of demand (under served), so songs parents enjoy watching with their children stand out more there than toddler only content. (parrotanalytics.com, Jul 2026, high)
  • In the same study US and Japanese titles take over 85% of animated demand in the region (46.5% and 38.9%), local Arabic animation is still early, and kids titles draw the widest age mix (23% Gen X and older), so imported English animation with Arabic dubbing and co viewing appeal fits the market. (parrotanalytics.com, Jul 2026, high)

  • A Harris Interactive survey for France's parenting observatory OPEN (1,000 parents of 6 to 16 year olds, Jan 2026) found 86% say their children use YouTube for educational content and parents find watching together reassuring, while 89% back a legal social network ban under 13, so French parents accept YouTube when it teaches and is shared.   • France's regulator Arcom (Apr 2026) reports YouTube is the first thing one in three under 25s open when they switch on the TV, the TV is a growing YouTube screen and many viewers watch videos over 30 minutes there, which supports French dubbed long compilations for the family TV.   • A survey of 22,000 Polish children aged 7 to 9 by the Empowering Children Foundation found over 80% of first to third graders watch YouTube regularly, 66% own a smartphone and half already use social media despite the 13+ rule, so Poland's early school age audience is large and reachable through Polish dubs of our songs.   • In the same Polish survey more than 60% of 7 to 9 year olds had met disturbing content online, which is why parents there look for clearly safe, made for kids channels; strong safety signals (made for kids setting, calm thumbnails, no shock titles) help a new brand earn trust.   • In Argentina (Labi survey of 250 parents of 6 to 9 year olds, late 2024) the TV is still the main screen (72%) ahead of phones (46%); 65% of these children use YouTube and 24% TikTok, and their favourite characters are a local public TV educational hero (Zamba) next to Peppa Pig, Bluey and Sonic, with Spanish speaking family creators (Alejo Igoa, Diki Duki Dariel, Fede Vigevani) beside MrBeast.   • Colombia's communications regulator (CRC) found YouTube recalled by 76% of children and teens and 63% of minors watching without an adult present; phones are in 83% of homes and personally used by 61% of children, and about 3 in 10 children aged 6 to 9 already use TikTok, Instagram or Facebook, so Colombian kids often meet Bro Bros alone on a phone and the content must be safe without a parent filter.   • AIR suggests testing translated titles and descriptions in just three languages first, tracking click rate, average view duration and RPM for each, and scaling a language only if its retention stays within about 10 to 15% of the main English market, otherwise moving that market to a full dubbed track.   • A dubbing vendor's three YouTube case studies (Sep 2026) found English AI auto dub tracks held viewers 4 to 10 times shorter than professionally voiced tracks; on an Italian kids channel the human dubs averaged 5 to 6 minutes watched versus 54 seconds for the AI track. (air.io, Sep 2026, low)

  • The vendor says children leave fast when a dubbed voice sounds flat or too adult, so for songs a flat auto dub is risky: re-generate each song in Suno with a child friendly sung vocal in the target language rather than relying on YouTube's spoken auto dub. (air.io, Sep 2026, low)

  • In the same survey the content Mexican kids watch most on YouTube is funny clips and bloopers (53%) and music (49%), ahead of unboxing (44%) and tutorials (39%), so a Spanish Bro Bros track paired with a blooper Short (missed dance moves, silly falls into snow) fits Mexican taste.   • Moonbug Kids Brasil, a separate Portuguese dub channel, had only about 862K subscribers and about 5.4M views in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 from 22 uploads (its newest Short under 1K views in 13 hours), while all its top videos are dubbed Little Angel episodes from 2022 to 2023, more evidence that a separate dub channel grows slowly compared with adding Portuguese audio to the main videos.   • MBC The Voice Kids (Saudi Arabia, 10.5M subscribers) drew about 49M views in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026 without a single upload since July, led by one sung performance from May 2026 near 98M views, so Arabic speaking families replay strong sung performances for months; a clear, emotional Arabic sung version of our best song could keep earning long after release.   • In Kapwing's test (Apr 2026) a 162K subscriber Portuguese creator published one video dubbed into Spanish two ways on the same day: as an extra audio track with a translated title on the main channel it drew 32 views in 90 days, while a new zero subscriber Spanish channel with fresh thumbnail and title drew 3,897 views and 51 subscribers.   • That dub test is one software tutorial, one language pair and a vendor's own blog, and the new channel also had new packaging, so for Bro Bros it only says an audio track alone does not create foreign reach; kids channel cases still favour audio tracks first and a separate language channel only once one language clearly proves itself.   • In vidIQ's Italy top 100 (14 Nov 2026) the only kids channels in the top 50 are TV brands (Masha and the Bear 12th with 7.28M subscribers, WB Kids Italiano 23rd, Disney Junior Italia 44th); the first nursery song channel, HeyKids Canzoni Per Bimbi, sits 55th with 3.36M, so Italy rewards known characters more than song channels.   • Bangladesh's vidIQ top 100 (19 Nov 2026) has no nursery rhyme channel in the top 50, but an art and craft channel ranks 3rd (19.6M subscribers) and a drawing academy 7th (15.6M), so wordless drawing and making videos are a bigger kid adjacent door into Bangladesh than Bangla rhymes. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • The leading Bangla kids channel in that list is a TV network's kids arm, Maasranga Kids, at 72nd with about 5.3M subscribers and roughly 9,000 uploads, showing local broadcasters, not independent animators, own the Bangla kids space so far. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)

  • Roy Morgan's survey of Australian 6 to 13 year olds (Apr to Dec 2025, 1,129 kids) found 89% watch YouTube; girls choose music videos far more than boys (41% versus 27%), and 6 to 9 year olds favour animation (40%), animals (35%) and challenges (32%), so an animated animal challenge song is the strongest mix for that age.   • In Luxembourg 86% of early childhood educators sing every day, mostly in French (98%), Luxembourgish (73%) and English (47%), and in Finland only about 20 to 30% of staff for four and five year olds say music is part of daily education, so in Europe English kids songs travel as a second language through daycare while home viewing fills the gap for older preschoolers.   • Luminate's 2026 midyear report shows English language music at a record low 87.1% of US listening, with Spanish at about 9.4%, and on demand streams outside the US growing 11.8% against 4.8% inside, so the fastest growing music audiences are non US and bilingual; a Spanish version of our strongest songs reaches both Latin America and US Latino homes. (Kapwing citing AIR, Apr 2026, medium)
  • 3Play Media data compiled in 2026 shows 61% of creators who localise use only subtitles and just 12% dub, while subtitles alone lift views by about 7%, far less than dubbing; since young children cannot read, sung dubs are the localisation that actually reaches our audience. (Kapwing citing 3Play Media, Apr 2026, medium)
  • Little Angel's spin off 'Animals Songs' channel (997K subscribers, about 379M views by May 2025, 612 videos averaging about 10 minutes, four uploads a week) says it is available in 15 languages, showing how one animal themed playlist can become its own channel reaching a global audience through dubs. (vidIQ, May 2025, low)

  • Some Hausa YouTube productions add English subtitles for viewers who only partly understand Hausa and to reach the diaspora, a reminder that subtitled or dual language versions of our songs can widen reach in multilingual African markets where Hausa, Yoruba and English mix. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Lalafun's Indonesian channel (1.52M subscribers, 288M views) uploads about 3 times a week but its newest song had only about 800 views after almost two days, and its top video is still a dubbed wheels on the bus song at 94M, so late dubbed channels in Indonesia live off a few old public domain rhymes. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • LiaChaCha's Spanish channel (Mexico based, started Dec 2023) already has 6.64M subscribers and 6.1B views, gained about 90K subscribers and 155M views in the 28 days to 16 Nov 2026 from about 20 uploads, and its top video (a Spanish public domain chick song, Jan 2025) has about 382M views, so a young brand can still win Latin America fast with native Spanish versions of public domain songs. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Mexico's NuNu Tv (started May 2023, 1.2M subscribers) still drew about 58M views in 28 days with only 7 uploads, mostly from colour learning songs (its top video is a colours song at about 8.2M), showing that Spanish colour and learning songs have deep, steady demand even for small new channels. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • In Sweden a local live action band channel (Barnplaneten, 328K subscribers) draws about 7M to 8M views a month, while a dubbed animated nursery rhyme feed with more subscribers (Kids TV Svenska, 517K) gets only about 0.7M to 1.5M and its new uploads reach about 2K views, so small Nordic markets favour home grown performers over generic dubs. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • One of Barnplaneten's three most viewed videos (about 6.9M) is 'Bro bro breja', a traditional Swedish bridge singing game where children walk under raised arms, so 'Bro Bro' already sounds familiar and friendly to Swedish families; a Swedish dub of an original Bro Bros bridge game song could lean on that echo. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • BabyTV's Dutch channel (274K subscribers) grew from about 3.5M views in July to about 5.5M in October 2026, and its top videos are 'best kids songs' and 3 hour compilations, so in the Netherlands long Dutch language song mixes are what keep a dubbed baby brand growing. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Chikoo TV Hindi (4.39M subscribers, about 45M to 55M views a month in 2026) gets its biggest views from a parrot rhyme ('Main Tota', 172M) and a fat elephant rhyme (157M), and a red tomato rhyme ('Lal Tamatar') sits inside its third biggest compilation (88M), so a Hindi dub of our Roly Poly Red Tomato lands on a food theme Indian families already love. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • The smaller Hindi channel Bhola Bhalu (595K subscribers) adds about 16K to 32K subscribers a month on only about 17M to 25M monthly views, built on animal sound rhymes (a rooster 'kukdoo koo' song 19M) and parrot songs, roughly twice the subscribers per view of Chikoo TV, so simple animal sound songs in Hindi turn viewers into subscribers well. (vidIQ, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Ofcom's passive device tracking of 701 UK children aged 8 to 14 over 28 days (Oct 2025 to Mar 2026) found they spend 3h36m a day online on phones, tablets and computers, from 2h53m at ages 8 to 9 up to 4h19m at 13 to 14. (Ofcom CPOM report 2, May 2026, high)
  • In the same tracking YouTube was the biggest single destination: 93% visited in a month, 62% every day, about 244 visits a month per user and 23% of all their online time, more than any other app. (Ofcom CPOM report 2, May 2026, high)
  • Younger children lean on YouTube the most: 8 to 9 year old YouTube users averaged about 1h15m a day on it versus 37 minutes for 13 to 14s, while TikTok time rises with age (14 minutes at 8 to 9, 34 minutes at 13 to 14). (Ofcom CPOM report 2, May 2026, medium)
  • Only about 14% of UK 8 to 12s used the YouTube Kids app (about 30 minutes a day) while almost all used main YouTube, so our discovery happens mostly on main YouTube with Made for Kids settings, not inside YouTube Kids. (Ofcom CPOM report 2, May 2026, medium)
  • Instagram is marginal for children themselves (8 to 12s about 7 minutes a day), which confirms our Instagram Reels mainly reach parents and older siblings who choose videos for little ones. (Ofcom CPOM report 2, May 2026, high)
  • The first Eurovision Song Contest Asia (Bangkok, 14 Nov 2026, 11 countries, votes from 183 countries and territories) was won by the Philippines with an energetic pop song by a singer who rose through The Voice Kids, topping both jury and public votes, which shows how strongly Filipino audiences rally behind bright, upbeat pop. (eurovision.com, Nov 2026, high)
  • Half of the Philippines' top 10 kids songs by YouTube views are faith themed action songs (praise songs with hand moves), alongside one traditional song (BINGO) and one Tagalog song, so gentle values and simple actions matter in this English friendly market. (soundcharts.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Thailand and Vietnam took second and third at Eurovision Asia 2026, with Malaysia and Laos in the top five, a sign that Southeast Asian countries are investing in international pop moments, a region where our English songs can travel. (eurovision.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Baile para niños (about 1.25M subscribers, about 6M views in the 28 days to 19 Nov 2026) posts only 6 to 8 minute medleys whose titles chain three famous Latin kids songs (a piñata game, marching ants, a singing cow); its newest piñata medley reached about 364K views in 12 days, showing Spanish speaking parents search by familiar song names, so a Spanish Bro Bros medley title should name each song inside. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Baby Big Cheese's Spanish channel (about 492K subscribers) posted Christmas versions of a bus song and a carol on 12 and 13 Nov 2026 and they drew only about 0.7K to 1.8K views in nine days, about the same as its ordinary uploads, so in Spanish markets an early Christmas remake alone does not lift a small channel in mid November. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Perso's State of AI Dubbing 2026 (about 113K projects from about 4K creators in 80 countries) lists Hindi, Portuguese and English as the top three dub targets for animation, with Hindi as animation's signature language and Portuguese at about 16.3% of animation projects (its user base leans South Asian), so for Bro Bros the first two extra audio tracks remain Portuguese and Hindi, then Spanish. (perso.ai, 2026, medium)
  • YouTube Brazil's 2025 year end culture report lists the country's top trending topics as brainrot, a survival drama, a Roblox horror game, a K pop demon hunter film, a Bobbie Goods style colouring book craze and blind box dolls, plus creator houses with shared story universes for young viewers, so Brazilian kids reward silly absurd humour and ongoing character worlds; a recurring Bro Bros gang with running jokes fits better than one off songs. (services.google.com (YouTube Culture and Trends Brazil), Nov 2025, medium)
  • Kids Channel Arabic (Saudi Arabia, about 216K subscribers, about 62K views a day in the 28 days to 20 Nov 2026) posts only about twice a month, yet its library keeps earning: a police car and car wash learning video from 2021 has about 28M views and moral story mixes 1 to 15M, so vehicle songs and gentle moral stories are the evergreen Arabic winners we should dub first. (vidiq.com, Nov 2026, medium)
  • Lebanon's Lila TV grew a preschool YouTube channel past 1M subscribers with musical rhymes in local Lebanese Arabic, and a UAE studio's cartoon hero drew most of its YouTube views from Iraq and Egypt rather than the Gulf, so an Arabic Bro Bros track should use a simple, widely understood Arabic and expect its biggest audiences in Egypt and Iraq, not only Saudi Arabia and the UAE. (kidscreen.com, Sep 2023, medium)
  • YouTube's 2026 animation report found 50% of US animation fans aged 14 to 49 watch animated series in a language other than their own, and its biggest indie hit offers subtitles in 18 languages and alternate audio tracks in 21, so multi language audio tracks on one upload are standard for animation that travels. (YouTube Culture and Trends, Apr 2026, medium)
  • Argentina's El Reino Infantil reported over 5.6B YouTube views in January to April 2026 alone and more than 229M subscribers across its brands (main channel about 71M), plus over 90 licensing deals in 15 countries and live tours, so the biggest Spanish kids music brand earns well beyond ads once songs and characters are known. (Bloomberg Linea, Apr 2026, medium)
